title: Taranga 12. The Circuit of Sri Navadvipa and Other Matters
html:
Srinivasa, Narottama and Ramachandra go to Navadvipa; the glory of Navadvipa and its nine islands; the guide Ishana; Mayapura, Mishra's house and the Lord's birth; childhood pastimes, study, the upanayana; the marriages with Lakshmi and Vishnupriya; Ishvara Puri and the Lord's self-revelation; Nityananda and Advaita; kirtan at Srivasa's house, Jagai and Madhai, the Kazi; the pastimes of Navadvipa in songs; Shantipura, Khardaha, Nityananda's marriage; Srinivasa's visions in dreams

1Glory to Gaurachandra, the husband of Lakshmi and Vishnupriya!
Glory to Nityananda, the life of Vasu and Jahnava!1

2Glory to Advaita Ishvara, the lord of Sri Sita!
Glory to Srivasa Pandita, to Gadadhara!

3Glory, glory to Gadadhara Dasa, to Narahari!
Glory to Vakreshvara, glory to Sri Murari Gupta!

4Glory to Jagadisha, to Sri Svarupa Damodara!
Glory to Haridasa, to Shuklambara Brahmachari!

5Glory to Pundarika Vidyanidhi, full of prema!
Glory to Vasudeva Ghosha, to Mukunda, to Sanjaya!

6Glory to Raya Ramananda, noble in every virtue!
Glory to Vasudeva Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya!

7Glory to Jagannatha Mishra, to Vidyavachaspati!
Glory to Sri Vijaya, to Vanamali, the very wise!

8Glory to Kashi Mishra, to Sri Gopinatha Acharya!
Glory to Sri Mukunda, the father of Raghunandana!

9Glory to Sri Pandita Gadadhara, to Dhananjaya!
Glory, glory to the merciful Sri Vamshivadana!

10Glory to Sanatana, to Rupa, the crown of rasikas!
Glory to Sri Gopala Bhatta, the ocean of virtues!

11Glory to Sri Bhugarbha, to Lokanatha, the friend of the wretched!
Glory to Raghunatha, to Raghunatha, the ocean of mercy!2

12Glory, glory to Sri Raghava, dear to Sri Prabhu!
Glory, glory to Sri Hridaya Chaitanya Thakura!

13Glory, glory to Sri Jiva, to Sri Dasa Vrindavana!
Glory to Krishnadasa, to Sri Gopala, to Narayana!3

14Glory, glory to Srinivasa, dear to the Lord's company!
Glory to Narottama Dasa, full of prema for the Lord!

15Glory, glory to Ramachandra, the giver of prema for the Lord!
Glory to Shyamananda, the life of all Vaishnavas!

16Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now listen with kind hearts to what I tell.

17When Sri Jahnava Ishvari went to Sri Khardaha —
what do I know, that I could tell how distraught everyone was?

18From Yajigrama Srinivasa Acharya Thakura
sent all this news to Vishnupura.

19Shridasa, Gokulananda and other disciples
he left in Yajigrama for the study of the shastras.

20To all he speaks very sweet words:
"From Navadvipa I will soon come back here.

21King Hambira will soon come here
from Vana-Vishnupura — I have written [to him] in a letter."

22Having said much of this kind to the disciples, Sri Acharya
set out from Yajigrama at an auspicious moment.

23First he went to Sri Raghunandana in Shrikhanda
and told him of his going to Navadvipa.

24He tenderly took Srinivasa aside;
I do not know what [they] said — [both] were drenched with tears.

25In sending [him] off, [Raghunandana's] heart was utterly unsteady;
Srinivasa bowed down and took his leave.

26Taking both Narottama and Ramachandra with him,
he goes to Navadvipa, deeply absorbed in prema.

27Coming near Navadvipa,
he gazes toward Navadvipa with tear-filled eyes.

28He longs for many eyes to behold Navadvipa;
his body goes limp — he cannot hold it up.

29Again and again he bows down to the land of Navadvipa;
he cannot restrain himself — streams of tears flow from his eyes.

30Seeing the beauty of the Ganga at Navadvipa,
he describes the good fortune of Bharata-varsha.

31The Ganga and other great rivers are in Bharata-varsha;
and the Bhagavata praises Bharata-varsha.

32Among the divisions of Bharata-varsha is Sri Navadvipa;
the Sri Vishnu Purana establishes this in detail.

33Thus [it is said] in the Sri Vishnu Purana:
"Hear of the nine divisions of this land of Bharata:
Indradvipa, Kaseru, Tamraparna, Gabhastiman,4

34and also Nagadvipa, Saumya, Gandharva and Varuna;
and the ninth of them is this island lying by the ocean.

35This island [extends] a thousand yojanas from south to north."

36"Sagara-sambhuta" means "situated at the edge of the ocean" — such is the explanation of Shridhara Svami. Since a separate name of this ninth [island] is not given, it is understood that by name, too, this is Navadvipa.5

37This is the special [meaning] proclaimed about it in the Vishnu Purana:
such is the glory of Nadia, which contains all the dhamas.

38Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:
"That which the many-knowing knowers of rasa call Sri Vrindavana, which some other people call this Goloka,
and others the White Island, and even the supreme Paravyoma —
that is this Navadvipa, whose glory in the world surpasses every wonder."6

39Thus the name "Navadvipa" is famed in the world:
[here] the nine kinds of bhakti — hearing and the rest — shine.7

40The nine kinds of bhakti — hearing, chanting and the rest —
see in the Sri Bhagavata, in the Seventh Canto, in Prahlada's words.

41Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Seventh Canto (7.5.23–24), — the words of Prahlada:
"Hearing about Vishnu, chanting, remembering, serving the feet,
worship, offering prayers, servitude, friendship and offering of the self —

42if a person performs such bhakti of nine characteristics,
offered to Vishnu, directly to Bhagavan, that I consider the highest learning."

43Or else: in Sri Navadvipa are the names of nine islands,
separate, separate — yet [it all] is one settlement.

44At the beginning of the Satya, Treta, Dvapara and Kali [ages]
those names did not change in any way.

45As Kali grows, so the names change;
and yet all those names are [still] perceived.

46Just as in Vraja Vajranabha, by Krishna's will,
founded villages according to Krishna's lilas,8

47[and] after some time some villages vanished,
and people jumbled the names of other villages, —

48so too, for all the villages that lie within Navadvipa,
the names became manifest according to the lilas of the Lord and the devotees.

49Some are jumbled in the same way, some have vanished;
but I will make known the names of Navadvipa in order.

50By hearing the names of the islands all sorrow is destroyed;
on the eastern and western banks of the Ganga are nine islands.

51In the east are Antardvipa, Sri Simantadvipa,
Godrumadvipa, Sri Madhyadvipa — four.

52Koladvipa, Ritu[dvipa], Jahnu[dvipa], Modadruma[dvipa]
and Rudradvipa — these five are known in the west.

53In this Navadvipa — hence the name "Navadvipa" here;
here Shiva, Shakti and others dear to the Lord always shine.

54Thus it was said by the ancients:
"The great sages declared the abode of Sri Navadvipa to be the object of meditation:
this is the eternal Vrindavana, shining on the bank of the Jahnavi,

55where the five Shivas abide, together with Shakti, adorned with bhakti,
divine and enchanting with its nine islands — Antar, Madhya and the rest.

56Some say it [extends] five yojanas, [others] sixteen kroshas;
and in its midst is Mayapura, where the house of Bhagavan stands."

57Beautiful and full of splendor are the dwellings of Nadia;
of the people [living] in Navadvipa there is no count.

58Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata:
"The city of Navadvipa is like Madhupuri;
[people] of a single caste alone are hundreds of thousands — I cannot tell them all.

59For the Lord's pastimes the Creator had beforehand
made everything complete and set it there."

60Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
"In the holy place famed as Navadvipa, supreme [place] of Vaishnavas,
[are] brahmanas, saintly, peaceful, Vaishnavas, born in good families,

61magnanimous, skilled in rites, versed in the meaning of all the shastras;
and there are many other people too — physicians, shudras, merchants —

62devoted to their own proper conduct, pure, all living by learning;
all there shine like gods, in [that place] like the abode of Vaikuntha."

63Thus [it is said] in a song:
Glory, glory to Sri Nadia, the abode of happiness!
Wondrous dwellings — in them dwell [people of] the four ashramas;
there, day after day, are festivals beyond compare. (Refrain.)

64The eight siddhis, the nine nidhis and the rest in every
house constantly go about, as if servants;
dharma, artha and kama, moksha and the like
no one values — they are laughed at.9

65By mighty power the three kinds of misery are crushed;
the nine kinds of bhakti shine unceasingly;
day and night [all here] is full of pure prema;
here the unmoving and the moving are ever intoxicated.

66Houses of every kind; the clear city shines,
encircled by the Suradhuni with its white, lovely waters —
as if a garland of fresh kunda flowers and pearls,
as if, it seems, a crescent of the moon had risen.10

67[Its] beauty is ever new and new, like Vrindavana's;
the six seasons serve [it], [its] horizons are full of rasa;
its lovely great glory has spread over the earth —
the lord of serpents sings [it] but cannot reach the end.11

68With the gods, the best of gods — Hara and the Four-faced One —
hold [it] in meditation, in their hearts boundless joy.
Ghanashyama says: when shall I behold that
Lord with His associates in the midst of that land?12

69Wondrous are Gauranga's pastimes in Navadvipa;
in many ways poets describe the beauty of Nadia.

70Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-chandramrita:
"Where the Lord Himself, golden like molten gold, out of mercy
appeared in a body of the radiant rasa of the bliss of great prema —
in that Navadvipa, where in every house is a festival of devotees,
in that abode, sweeter even than Vaikuntha, may my mind delight."13

71Although this dhama is sometimes manifest, [sometimes] hidden —
[this is] just as in the Kali-yuga the Lord is the hidden avatara.

72Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Seventh Canto (7.9.38):
"Thus by Your avataras as man, animal, sage, god and fish
You sustain the worlds and slay the enemies of the world;
O Mahapurusha, You protect the dharma [proper] to the yugas;
and since in Kali You are hidden, You are Triyuga."14

73Whatever lilas there were in whatever dhama in former, former avataras —
all of them He secretly manifested in Navadvipa.

74Whatever pastimes there were in Navadvipa-dhama in former, former [times] —
in the same way the son of Shachi ever sports.

75The lila of Navadvipa is beyond the reach of Brahma and the others;
only he to whom the Lord made it known knows [it].

76The lila that He performs in Nadia in a single day —
even with a thousand mouths one finds no end to it.

77In whatever Dvapara Krishna sports in Vrajapura,
in that [same] Kali-yuga the Lord sports in Nadia.

78Some say the settlement of Nadia [spans] eight kroshas;
by the inconceivable power of the dhama, all [this] is true.

79Navadvipa-dhama behaves like a lotus flower:
one moment it contracts, the next moment it expands.

80One who lives far from the Lord's abode
comes quickly — for him distance does not appear.

81Countless people fit into the place of sankirtana:
the place is small, and how it expands, no one knows.

82In every respect Navadvipa is the best [of abodes]:
here countless devotees of the Lord abide in bliss.

83In the midst of Navadvipa is a place called Mayapura,
where Bhagavan Gaurachandra took birth.

84As in Vrindavana there is the sweet Yogapitha,
so in Navadvipa the Yogapitha is Mayapura.

85Brahma and the others ever meditate on the beauty of Mayapura;
who does not sing the glory of Mayapura?

86Whoever sees it even once, his distress goes far away;
to such a Mayapura goes Acharya Thakura.

87Taking both Narottama and Ramachandra with him,
he enters Mayapura, unable to restrain himself.

88On the very road on which he walks, a little way ahead,
an old brahmana comes towards him, slowly, slowly.

89Bowing to him, in very sweet words
he asks for news of Sri Ishana Thakura.

90The brahmana says, "I have just come from seeing Ishana.
What can I say? Who does not shed tears over his virtues?

91He knows all truths, he is renowned everywhere;
he served Sri Shachi-devi as was fitting."

92Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-bhagavata:
"Ishana served Ai at all times;
among the fourteen worlds he is the most fortunate."

93"How much affection Shachi-devi showed to Ishana —
how could I put it into words? I saw it with my own eyes."

94Thus [it is said] in the Vaishnava-vandana:
"I shall praise Ishana Dasa with folded hands —
him to whom Shachi Thakurani showed great affection."15

95"Ah, my son, what can I tell of his deeds?
That Ishana is very dear to Nimaichand.

96Ishana's life is Nimai, the son of Shachi;
without Ishana He goes nowhere.

97In childhood Nimai was exceedingly restless;
whatever mischief He made, Ishana set it right.

98What I have seen cannot be put into words;
my heart burns without cease when I think of all that.

99Who does not know what happiness there was in Nadia?
And such a Navadvipa became empty day by day.

100Wherever I look, that direction is dark;
of a happiness now beyond reach even in dreams, what more is there to say?

101Seeing you, joy arises in my heart:
are you not associates of Nimaichand?

102Tell me who you are, my son, tell me who you are!"
Hearing this, Srinivasa respectfully says to the brahmana:

103"My name is Srinivasa Dasa,
and these two are named Narottama and Ramachandra."

104Hearing this, the best of brahmanas spread out both arms
and embraced him, wet with tears.

105He cannot let Srinivasa go from his embrace;
looking at his face, he speaks again and again:

106"Ah, my son, I have heard talk of you;
I longed in my heart to see you, and suddenly we have met.

107Today I went to see Ishana;
he told me that you would come.

108Ishana, in the house of Sri Jagannatha Mishra,
is gazing at the road, waiting for you.

109Go there; I too will come quickly."
Saying this, the brahmana went home, slowly, slowly.

110Srinivasa, bowing at the old brahmana's feet,
went to the Lord's house, deeply stirred.

111He became grey with the dust of the Lord's courtyard;
his whole body is wet with tears.

112He looks in all four directions, unable to keep his composure;
he sees Ishana, whose radiance is like the sun.

113He is sitting alone in deep solitude —
what a wondrous state: tears from closed eyes!

114The tears from his eyes stream over his face and chest;
he heaves long sighs like tongues of flame.

115Now, crying "Vishvambhara!", he rolls on the ground;16
now he says, "O Lord, what happiness You have left me to taste!"

116Saying this, he looks around in distress
and sees before him Srinivasa, full of prema.

117Saying, "Come, my son!", and spreading out both arms,
he embraced Srinivasa and rejoiced.

118He embraced Narottama and Ramachandra —
the wondrous surge of affection that seized him cannot be described.

119Srinivasa, Narottama and Ramachandra — all three,
bowing to Ishana, cannot hold back their tears.

120Sri Ishana Thakura, consoling them with care
and seating them near him, asks about their welfare.

121Srinivasa, having told all that had happened,
shyly speaks of his own desire:

122"When I wandered through Vraja with Sri Raghava,17
it came to my mind that I would go round Nadia in the same way."

123Hearing this, Sri Ishana says, "What you have resolved
Sri Gaurasundara will fulfil.

124This Navadvipa-dhama is exceedingly secret:
he on whom there is mercy knows it; the fool does not know its truth.

125The places of the Navadvipa pastimes are most enchanting;
what to speak of others — they are beyond the reach even of Brahma and the rest.

126What I saw and what I heard from the old people —
even in such sorrow it remains in my mind.

127It suddenly came to my heart to make it known to you;
that is why I sent word through Narottama for you to come.

128It is good that you came quickly — what more is there to say?
Tomorrow at daybreak we shall set out to go round Nadia."

129Hearing this, Srinivasa falls at his feet;
Ishana, clasping him in his embrace, floats in tears.

130Ishana says, "My son, seeing you,
my terribly scorched heart has been cooled.

131I have grown old, I have lost my strength,
and now suddenly strength has come into my body."

132Saying many such things, at that very moment
he introduced Srinivasa to the Lord's dear [associates] who were there.

133How everyone spent that day
in the Lord's house cannot be described.

134When the night gave way to morning, Sri Ishana Mahashaya,
his heart jubilant, sets out to go round Nadia.

135Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama and Ramachandra
go with Ishana; joy overflows.

136Bowing again and again to the Lord's abode,
they set out from Mayapura for Atopura.18

137First of all, having looked at the place Atopura,
Ishana says, looking at Srinivasa:

138O Srinivasa, this place is Atopura;
for a long time this village was lost.

139Formerly it was called Antardvipa;19
how the name Antardvipa arose, that I shall tell.

140In the Dvapara-yuga Krishna sported in Vraja;
who is not bewildered under the sway of His yogamaya?20

141What to speak of others — even Brahma was bewildered:
he stole Sri Krishna's calves together with [His] friends.21

142To crush Brahma's pride at once,
[Krishna] Himself became all the calves and friends.

143Brahma could not understand this pastime of Krishna;
falling into confusion, Brahma could not be at peace.

144As an offender, he offered Krishna many prayers;
by those prayers Sri Krishna showed him His grace.

145Even so, Brahma's heart is not at ease:
"I have committed an offence," he thinks without cease.

146Sitting in solitude, he deliberates within himself:
"I see no [other] means but the Chaitanya avatara.

147At the beginning of [the age of] Kali the Lord, Sri Krishna Chaitanya,
having descended, will make Kali blessed.

148If I worship the Lord in Navadvipa,
the Lord will fulfil the desire of my heart."

149Having reflected thus, Brahma, here in Atopura,
worships the Lord with a jubilant heart.

150Merciful Gaurachandra, affectionate to His devotees,
appeared before his eyes; His beauty enchants the world.

151The effulgence of His limbs lights up the ten directions;
it robs paltry gold and Kandarpa of their pride.22

152His arms reach to His knees, His chest is broad;
His body is adorned with ornaments of many gems.

153His eyes extend to His ears, His glance is wondrous;
the loveliness of His face surpasses millions upon millions of moons.

154His ever gentle, gentle smile showers nectar;
who is there who can keep composure before such grace?

155Seeing the Lord of his life, Brahma was overwhelmed;
unable to hold himself up, he sways to and fro.

156Offering many prayers, wet with tears,
he falls and rolls at the Lord's feet.

157Seeing Brahma's state, the son of Shachi
embraces him and speaks sweet words:

158"You are dear to Me; I am always pleased with you;
now ask of Me whatever boon you wish."

159Brahma says, "In this Kali-yuga, in Nadia,
You will manifest Your pastimes together with Your associates.

160At that time, O Lord, accept me
and let me be born in a low family — this is my wish.23

161O Lord, my pride is excessive:
let there be such a punishment that people despise me.

162You will dispel my terrible, wicked disposition;
You will give me deep attachment to Your holy name.

163As You once bewildered me with maya,
do not do so, Lord, in this incarnation.24

164At every moment I desire the company of Your devotees;
in life and in death may I meditate on You."

165Hearing Brahma's words, the Lord was delighted;
the Lord says, "All [your] desires will be fulfilled."

166Having obtained the Lord's [mercy], in great joy of heart,
Brahma, bowing down, again speaks softly:25

167"You are the independent Lord, beyond all;
who can understand Your heart, Lord?

168You performed many pastimes in former incarnations;
I do not know what pastimes [there will be] in this town of Nadia.

169You will deliver the living beings, Lord — that is a small matter;
if there is something special in this, I long to hear it."

170Hearing Brahma's words, looking at Brahma,
[the Lord] tells him something of what is hidden in His heart:

171"Taking the mood of a devotee, I will taste bhakti-rasa;
I will manifest the supremely rare sankirtana.

172The devotees of the various incarnations, in their various moods,
I will bring to madhura-rasa that follows Vraja."

173At such words, the prema of Radha surges in [His] heart;
as He speaks of the three desires, He floats in tears.

174Mercifully He made known to Brahma
the three desires of the Lord that the wise have expressed.

175Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-charitamrita, Adi 1.6:
"What is the greatness of Sri Radha's love?
What is My wondrous sweetness, which she alone tastes through this [love]?
And what is the happiness she feels in realizing My [sweetness]?" — out of longing [to know] this,
the Moon of Hari, rich with her feelings, rose in the ocean of Shachi's womb.26

176And further the Lord briefly told Brahma,
"You will see My Navadvipa pastimes with your own eyes."

177Having spoken what was hidden in His heart, He disappeared;
for this reason the name Antardvipa is known among people.27

178By the Lord's mercy Brahma became very joyful;
he constantly thinks of the Lord's appearance in Navadvipa.

179The pastimes He performs on this land of Antardvipa
with Gaura's associates — who can describe them?

180O Srinivasa, Antardvipa is full of beauty;
by seeing this place one's desires are fulfilled.

181Look, Srinivasa, over there is Suvarna-vihara;
I will tell later of the pastimes in this village.

182Saying many such things, he took the three with him
and after a while entered the village of Simaliya.28

183Ishana Thakura says to Srinivasa:
Look at this beautiful village of Simaliya.

184Formerly this [was] Simantadvipa, famous in the world;
how it came to be called Simantadvipa I will tell briefly.

185One day on Mount Kailasa, Maheshvara,
drinking the nectar of the devotees' names, lost his composure of heart.

186All the devotees of all the incarnations are in Nadia;
all those names he utters aloud.

187With his five mouths he sings the glory of the Lord's devotees;
the hair on all his limbs stands on end, his heart overflows with happiness.

188Digambara performs a most wondrous dance;29
under the weight of his steps the great Mount Kailasa trembles.

189He plays his own instrument; the sound pierces the sky;
greatly intoxicated, he thunders with cries of "hum!"

190Seeing the state of Lord Shankara, Parvati
was overwhelmed and could understand nothing.

191Absorbed in the dance, the three-eyed god became still;
tears of bliss stream down and cannot be checked.

192Like a silver mountain, seated on a hide,
with his own mouth he praises the good fortune of [the age of] Kali.

193How wondrous is the conduct of Lord Maheshvara!
Smiling ever so gently, he looks all around.

194Seeing Parvati's state, pleased at heart,
he calmed Parvati and seated her at his side.

195Parvati, in the highest bliss, says, "O lord!
The mercy you have shown today you have never shown before.

196The names you have uttered with your own mouth —
such names I have never heard with my ears.

197Again and again you praise the good fortune of [the age of] Kali;
from this I understand that all of them will appear in Kali."

198Hearing Parvati's words, with joy in his heart
he speaks to Parvati in the sweetest words:

199"In this Kali-yuga, Krishnachandra, in Nadia,
will appear from the womb of Shachi-devi.

200He will take on the luster of Sri Radhika's body;
[His] form, conquering the three worlds, is the sweetest elixir.

201No one will be able to find a comparison for that form;
the world will go mad on seeing that form even once.

202By the beauty of His body the pride of Kandarpa will be destroyed;
in Navadvipa He will perform wondrous pastimes.

203Together with all the devotees of all the incarnations
He will joyfully taste the rare love of Vraja.

204He will manifest an ocean of the happiness of sankirtana;
by His own qualities He will deliver the world.

205In this incarnation no one will remain unhappy;
whatever desire anyone has will all be fulfilled.

206If anyone in the past committed any offense,
He will obtain forgiveness for it and make him content.

207He will make known the boundless glory of the devotees;
I tell you, there is no one so merciful."

208What was in Parvati's heart on hearing all this —
who can describe it with a single mouth?

209Coming here to Navadvipa, Parvati
worships Bhagavan Sri Gaurasundara.

210Pleased at heart, for He knew that the goddess was worshipping [Him],
He, the Moon of Navadvipa, appeared before her.

211The loveliness of each of His limbs enchants the world;
millions of moons offer themselves to the moon of His face.

212Who can keep his composure [before] His two long eyes?
The radiance of His cheeks takes away the pride of a golden mirror.

213His arms reach to His knees, His chest is broad;
His body is adorned with ornaments of many jewels.

214With His garments He destroys the pride of Madana;
how much bliss He reveals by the grace of His gait!

215Seeing [Him], Parvati cannot keep her composure;
she cannot check the streams of tears of bliss from her eyes.

216Seeing Parvati's state, Lord Vishvambhara
came near her, rejoicing at heart.

217With the sweetest words He says to Parvati,
"You have performed worship, and your heart has known no rest.

218Whatever you tell Me from your heart,
that I will do — this I promise without fail."

219Hearing this, Parvati's joy knew no bounds;
the beauty of the hair standing on end all over her body is beyond comparison.

220Joining her palms, she says to Lord Vishvambhara,
"You will make this [age of] Kali blessed by Your manifest pastimes.

221You will easily remove the threefold miseries of the world;
You will increase the great bliss of all living beings.

222Lord, You dwell in the heart of everyone, You know everything:
my heart is constantly in distress.

223I committed a grave offense against a devotee:
I cursed [him], and Chitraketu became Vritrasura.30

224The virtues of Your devotee cannot be put into words:
I did wrong, yet he still praised me.

225With all of them You will sport in Nadia;
do this — that they may all be pleased [with me].

226Lord, words cannot tell what is happening in my heart;
may I constantly see Your pastimes in Nadia."

227The Lord said, "What you have in mind will be fulfilled;
none of My works is done without you."

228Having said this, the Lord began to disappear;
Parvati fell at His feet and bowed down.

229She placed the dust of the Lord's feet in the parting of her hair;
for this reason the name Simantadvipa became known.31

230Parvati was distressed at not seeing the Lord;
she thinks in her heart, "When will the manifest pastimes be?"

231O Srinivasa, this place is Simantadvipa;
whoever sees it even once, his eyes become fruitful.

232Without effort the terrible fear of worldly existence is dispelled;
the supremely rare prema-bhakti is attained.

233Even today all the people here worship the goddess;
by the goddess's mercy they know no sorrow or grief.

234In this village of Simaliya Sri Gaurasundara
sports together with countless associates.

235What bliss there was here at the time of nagara-kirtana —
can I tell all of it with a single mouth?

236The fortunate beheld the great splendor;
the tumult of prema spread through the whole world.

237Having said this, he goes on from the village of Simaliya;
remembering the Lord's pastimes, he floats in tears.

238Speaking of the deeds of the Lord and the devotees,
he arrived at the village of Gadigachha.32

239Ishana says: This is the village of Gadigachha;
the wise say that formerly it was named Godrumadvipa.

240How it came to be called Godrumadvipa I will tell briefly,
as I heard it from the mouths of the wise of former times.

241One day Indra, greatly distressed at heart,
softly says to the cow Surabhi:33

242"Under the Lord's yogamaya I could not remain steady;
intoxicated with pride, I committed an offense.

243Although the Lord has become gracious to me,
still I cannot steady my heart.

244The punishment was not what I deserved, though the Lord did punish [me];
will He ever make me worthy of His own service?"

245Hearing Indra's words, Surabhi, with satisfaction,
speaks to Indra in very sweet language:

246"I have understood your heart — do not worry at all:
in this avatara your desire will be fulfilled.

247Only a few days remain before He descends;
the good fortune of this Kali-yuga is immense.

248Krishna, the son of the king of Vraja, [as] beautiful Gauranga,
will sport in Navadvipa most secretly.

249Whomever the Lord lets know, he alone will know;
He will destroy all the sorrows of all people."

250Having said this, Surabhi, together with Indra, here
beholds the beauty of Navadvipa with a jubilant heart.

251As Surabhi worshipped the feet of Sri Prabhu,
the eternal, complete Brahman appeared before her in person.

252Gazing on the golden form that enchants the worlds,
Surabhi, in great bliss, cannot contain her heart.

253Smiling gently, the Moon of Navadvipa
says to Surabhi, "I have understood your heart.

254You will see My manifest pastimes in Nadia;
all your desires will be fulfilled."

255Just as He was saying this, at that very moment Indra came
and, as if utterly wretched, fell at the Lord's feet.

256Seeing how sorely distressed Indra's heart was,
Vishvambhara speaks with very sweet words:

257"Keep no more hesitation in your heart:
all your desires will be fulfilled."

258Hearing the Lord's words, Indra humbly says,
"Who is not bewildered by Your yogamaya?

259As You confused [my] mind in the pastimes of Vraja,
will You do the same, Lord, in the pastimes of Navadvipa?"

260Hearing this, Lord Gaura-raya smiled gently;
the mercy He showed Indra cannot be described.

261Surabhi, together with Indra, offered many prayers;
when the Lord vanished, they were distraught.

262Sri Surabhi, the cow, together with Indra-deva,
after a while became calm by the Lord's will.

263Surabhi, together with Indra, in supreme bliss,
beholds the beauty of Navadvipa — how much wells up in their hearts!

264How could I ever tell how they behaved, O Srinivasa!
Here great prema was manifested.

265Here stood an ashvattha tree, very tall;
very wide-spreading, the tree was beautiful and charming.

266Sri Surabhi, the cow, dwelt at the foot of the tree;
therefore the wise of old call [this place] Godrumadvipa.34

267Now its name is Gadigachha; by seeing this village
pure bhakti arises for the Lord's feet.

268By living in this village one's desires are fulfilled;
what shall I say of this village's glory, Srinivasa?

269In this village are Sri Gauranga's wonderful pastimes;
all the people of Nadia saw them to their eyes' content.

270Having said this, Ishana Thakura, in joy,
went to the edge of the village of Majita and beholds its beauty.

271He says to Srinivasa: this is the village of Majita;
the old people say its former name was Madhyadvipa.35

272In Madhyadvipa are the Lord's most wonderful pastimes;
how the name Madhyadvipa came about I shall tell briefly.

273Here the seven rishis, absorbed in the Lord's qualities,
gazing at Navadvipa, spoke of many things.

274One says, "Look, Navadvipa is full of beauty —
the place of the Lord's pastimes, the abode of happiness.

275All the holy places that exist in the universe —
all those holy places abide in the town of Nadia."

276Another says, "The glory of Navadvipa is boundless:
here are wonderful pastimes, manifest and unmanifest.

277In the manifest [pastimes] everyone sees the Lord;
in the unmanifest only the fortunate see [Him]."

278Another says, "To make this [age of] Kali blessed,
He will appear in the house of Jagannatha Mishra.

279In this avatara [His] golden complexion is incomparable;
the world will go mad seeing the beauty of all His limbs."

280Another says, "These Nadia pastimes of Krishna
are so wondrous that they are beyond the reach even of Brahma and others."

281Another says, "The son of Shachi acts by His own will:
what He will do, and when, cannot be told.

282In the Kali-yuga, taking great pains for the living beings,
He will distribute the supremely rare jewel of prema."

283Another says, "Mahaprabhu is an ocean of mercy;
such mercy as He will show the living beings has never been.

284Taking with Him all the devotees of all the avataras,
He will become intoxicated in sankirtana and intoxicate the world."

285Another says, "Gaurahari, the life of the devotees,
will take sannyasa and go away to other lands.

286Fulfilling the desire of countless holy places,
out of love for Jagannatha He will dwell in the Kshetra."36

287Thus, in great bliss, speaking much with one another,
they meditate unceasingly on the Lord's lotus feet.

288With great love the rishis worship [Him];
the Lord, affectionate to His devotees, grew utterly impatient.

289Like the midday sun, at the midday hour
He appeared in person — who could describe [His] splendor?

290Beholding [His] pose that enchants the worlds,
the rishis' eyes ceased to blink.

291Thrills spread through [their] limbs, streams of tears from their eyes;
falling to the ground, they bow to the Lord again and again.

292They offered many prayers — it cannot be told;
circumambulating [Him], they again say to the Lord:

293"O Lord, great is our desire:
to see these pastimes of Nadia to our eyes' content.

294May we always meditate on Navadvipa
and unceasingly sing the qualities of Your devotees."

295Having said much like this before the Lord, the rishis
long for a thousand eyes with which to see the Lord.

296Won over by the rishis' prayers, the Lord says to the rishis,
"All that you have set your hearts on will be fulfilled.

297My pastimes in Navadvipa are most secret;
keep them hidden — in that lies My joy."

298Hearing this, the rishis say, "What can we say, Lord!
Can the sun ever be hidden by the palm of a hand?"

299Thus the rishis say much in their jubilation;
hearing it, Lord Gaurachandra smiles to Himself.

300Having bestowed mercy on the rishis with joy in His heart,
Lord Gaurahari vanished from sight.

301The rishis, distraught that the Lord was no longer to be seen,
left this place while it was still midday.

302On the bank of the Ganga, near Kumarahatta,37
seeing a wondrous place, they remained there.

303The place where they settled is well known:
people still call it Saptarshi-ghat today.

304O Srinivasa, the account of Madhyadvipa
I have told you briefly: here there was great joy.

305Like the midday sun, at the midday hour
the Lord showed Himself — therefore [the island] is called Madhyadvipa.

306Another rishi performed austerities here for some time;
he too joyfully proclaimed the name Madhyadvipa.

307By seeing this place all inauspiciousness is destroyed;
whoever lives here obtains pure bhakti.

308Here are Gauranga's wonderful pastimes:
He maddened the living beings by giving rare prema.

309Having said much like this, Sri Ishana, in great joy,
walks slowly toward the village of Vamana-paukhera.38

310He looks in all directions, tears of prema pour from his eyes;
overwhelmed, he says to Srinivasa:

311look at this lovely land, O Srinivasa:
in all these places are the Lord's wonderful pastimes.

312The name of this village is Vamana-paukhera;
its former name, the wise say, was Brahmana-pushkara.

313How the name Brahmana-pushkara came about,
I shall tell as I heard it from the mouths of the wise of old.

314Here lived a venerable old brahmana,
a great ascetic, learned in all the scriptures.

315He had boundless devotion for Sri Pushkara-tirtha;39
he wished to go there, but had no strength to walk.

316Distraught, the brahmana says again and again,
"I have never been able to serve Sri Pushkara-tirtha.

317Sri Pushkara lies far away in the western land;
I have wasted [my] time and could not go there.

318I have had no darshan — grief remains in my heart;
will the king of tirthas show me favor?"

319Having said much like this, repeating the name of Sri Pushkara,
the brahmana weeps, sitting in solitude.

320Seeing the brahmana's state, Sri Pushkara, the best of tirthas,
granted him darshan: at this he lost all patience.

321Suddenly a pond appeared here;
the beauty of its clear water was boundless.

322Before the brahmana, at once taking the guise of water,
Sri Pushkara, the king of tirthas, appeared in person.

323Showing the brahmana mercy, he speaks sweet words:
"Do not grieve — bathe in this pond."

324Hearing this, the brahmana bathed in the highest joy;
as soon as he bathed, the brahmana gained divine knowledge.

325Offering many prayers to Sri Pushkara-tirtha, the brahmana
fell to the ground and bowed down endlessly.

326Joining his palms, he says again and again,
"For my sake you have come from afar!"

327Pushkara says, "I have not come from afar:
I always stay in Navadvipa and serve Nadia.

328Countless tirthas abide in Navadvipa-dhama;
Brahma and the others do not know the glory of Navadvipa.

329Navadvipa-dhama, full of prema-bhakti, is eternal;
by the mercy of Nadia one comes to know the truth of Navadvipa.

330In Navadvipa Gaurachandra always dwells —
He who in Vrindavana enjoyed the rasa and other pastimes.

331In Vrindavana He is dark, in Navadvipa golden;
in Navadvipa the Lord sports in secret.

332His pastimes are sometimes unmanifest, sometimes manifest;
in this Kali-yuga there will be an ocean of happiness.

333The Lord will appear at the beginning of this Kali
and will sport with the devotees of all the avataras.

334He will distribute to living beings prema that is hard for Brahma to attain,
and with sankirtana He will intoxicate the whole world.

335He will deliver the wretched, the lowly and the pashandas;
in this avatara no one will be left deprived.

336He will perform endless pastimes in Navadvipa,
and the fortunate people of Nadia will see them."

337Hearing all this, the brahmana weeps loudly
and says again, "Will I be born in Nadia?

338Will I see the beautiful pastimes of Gaurachandra?"
Having said this, the brahmana became greatly agitated.

339Having consoled the brahmana, Sri Pushkara, the king of tirthas,
disappeared on some pretext.

340The brahmana was in great distress at losing sight of Pushkara;
at that very moment a voice from the sky spoke to the brahmana:

341"Meditate constantly on the feet of Gaurachandra;
your desire will be fulfilled — make your mind steady."

342Hearing such words, the brahmana, with a jubilant heart,
constantly meditates on the Moon of Navadvipa.

343He dances, singing of the Lord's deeds;
others are amazed, watching the brahmana's behavior.

344What can I tell of his ways, which I have heard of?40
The story of Pushkara-tirtha became known [to all].

345Pushkara showed the brahmana boundless mercy —
for this reason [the place] is called Brahmana-pushkara.

346Here the fortunate brahmana worshiped the Lord.
See, this is the place bearing the marks of Pushkara-tirtha.

347Whoever beholds [it], whoever lives here,
gains firm faith in the Lord's feet.

348That person will not know the torments of Yama
who glorifies this wonderful place.

349Here are the wonderful pastimes of Gaurasundara;
how can I tell, Srinivasa, what I saw?

350Having said this, Ishana, floating in tears,
set out from Vamana-paukhera.

351Stopping near the village of Hatadanga,41
he speaks to Srinivasa, pointing with his hand:

352See, Srinivasa, this is the village of Hatadanga;
the wise of former times call it Uchchahatta.

353How the village got the name Uchchahatta —
of that I will tell a little, as I heard it from sadhus.

354Indra and all the other gods, staying right here,
spoke much to one another, overwhelmed.

355One says, "Blessed, blessed is this Kali-yuga!
The Lord, Sri Krishna Chaitanya, will appear.

356Lord Advaita and Nityananda-Balarama
He will make manifest in abodes appointed of old."

357Another says, "In Navadvipa all will dwell;
countless are the Lord's associates — what strength have I to tell [of them]?

358All the Lord's associates are oceans of mercy,
the dearest friends of the wretched, the lowly and the fallen."

359Someone says, "The Lord, together with His associates,
will be intoxicated in sankirtana, intoxicating the world [with it].

360A river of bliss will flow in this Nadia,
and the sins of living beings will be destroyed with ease."

361Yet another says, "There will be good fortune without end;
fortunate people will see wonderful pastimes.

362If all of us are born in Nadia,
then the great sorrow of our hearts will go away."

363Another says, "We will certainly be born here
and behold the Lord's pastimes to our eyes' content.

364The devotees who live in Navadvipa will take all of us
and engage us in the service of Gaurachandra."

365Thus they said much, as if they had set up a market,
and on this high place they began a loud kirtana.

366All, raising their arms, cry out with anguished hearts,
"O Lord, do not delay in descending!"

367Speaking thus, the gods in supreme jubilation
dance, striking many poses.

368All sing the series of the Lord's holy names.
For these two reasons [the place is called] Uchchahatta.42

369Seeing this place brings auspiciousness in every way;
in the Lord's kirtana prema grows unrestrained.

370Here the Lord, Shachi's son, together with His devotees
sports, beyond the sight of the gods, the foremost sages and others.

371Having said this, Ishana cannot become calm;
he remembers Sri Gaura's pastimes, and tears flow from his eyes.

372After some time, becoming calm, he, together with Srinivasa,
enters the village of Kuliya-Paharpura.43

373He speaks to Srinivasa in the sweetest words:
See, Srinivasa — [this is] Kuliya-Paharpura.

374Formerly it was known as Koladvipa, called Parvata;
how this name arose, I will tell.

375A certain brahmana, a devotee of Sri Kola-deva,44
worshiped the feet of Kola-deva here.

376The charming deeds of Lord Kola-deva
the brahmana sings, and streams of tears flow ceaselessly from his eyes.

377Extremely agitated, the brahmana says,
"Grant me Your sight just once, O merciful Lord!"

378Thus, with anguished cries, the best of brahmanas says much;
whose heart could keep its composure, seeing his behavior?

379The Lord Gaurahari, the source of the avataras, subject to His devotees,
assumed the form of Kola — a wondrous beauty!

380His body is adorned with various jeweled ornaments;
His hands, feet, nose, face and eyes are enchanting.

381As tall as a mountain — that beauty is a marvel!
Who, seeing Varaha-deva, could keep his composure?

382When Kola-deva appeared to the brahmana here,
the brahmana's joy — who could describe it?

383Falling to the ground, the brahmana bowed at the Lord's feet;
the prayers he offered cannot be told.

384Kola-deva, affectionate to His devotees, to the brahmana
speaks sweet words, filled with great joy:

385"What is in your heart will be fulfilled:
you will see wonderful pastimes in this Navadvipa."

386Having said this and shown mercy to the brahmana,
Kola-deva disappeared after a while.

387When the Lord was lost to sight, the brahmana's heart was in turmoil;
becoming calm, he reflects on the Lord's command:

388the command was that he would see pastimes in Navadvipa —
what, then, will the Lord's descent in Navadvipa be like?

389The brahmana reflects, turning to the Vedas and other scriptures;
the meaning of the Vedas and other scriptures is revealed within his mind:

390"At the beginning of this Kali, assuming a golden complexion,
He will descend in Navadvipa in a brahmana family.

391He will reveal sankirtana, hard for Brahma and others to attain,
and bestow the treasure of bhakti on the wretched and lowly.

392He will taste the ocean of the rasa of Vraja's prema
and, in the mood of a devotee, accept sannyasa."

393Having reflected thus, the brahmana looks all around;
seeing the transcendental land, he speaks with a sorrowful heart:

394"Navadvipa-dhama is supremely dear to the Lord;
this is declared in the scriptures, yet I have not grasped its essence.

395Will Navadvipa show me mercy?
Will I be born here at the time of the Lord's descent?"

396Having said this, the brahmana floats in tears.
A voice from the sky spoke: "You will be born at that time."

397Hearing this, the brahmana's heart was filled with great joy,
and he was constantly absorbed in the Lord's qualities.

398O Srinivasa, this is known everywhere;
I heard it from the mouths of the elders and have told a little.

399Kola, the size of a mountain, appeared to the brahmana —
for this reason Koladvipa came to be called Parvata.

400Seeing this place destroys all that is inauspicious;
one obtains rare, perfectly pure prema-bhakti.

401If one lives here, one's desires are fulfilled:
one sees the pastimes of Gaurachandra in Navadvipa.

402Saying much in this way, he goes on from Koladvipa,
looking at one place of the Lord's pastimes after another.

403Approaching the village of Samudragarhi, he says:
Look, Srinivasa, this is Samudragarhi.45

404The wise call it Sri Samudra-gati.
Here is the delightful story of the Ganga and the Ocean.

405Taking shelter of the Ganga, the Ocean used to come here;
listen, I will tell the story that is well known among the people.

406One day the Ocean says to the Ganga:
"In the world there is none as fortunate as you.

407The Complete Brahman, Sri Gaurasundara, in Nadia
will manifest His pastimes — so everyone sings.

408On your banks there will be boundless bliss:
with His associates Gaurachandra will always sport there.

409As in Vraja He sports in the waters of the Yamuna,
so will Lord Gaura-raya sport."

410Hearing this, Jahnavi revealed what was in her heart46
and spoke to the Ocean in very sweet words:

411"My misfortune — to whom shall I tell it?
Having given joy, the Lord will afterwards give great sorrow.

412The Lord will take sannyasa and leave Nadia;
He will go and live on your shore.

413There He will reveal supremely wondrous pastimes,
ceaselessly increasing your bliss.

414Everyone will sing of your good fortune —
yet, saying nothing of that, you mock me."

415The Ocean replies, "What you have said is true.
I shall see the garb of a sannyasi at which the heart breaks.47

416Remembering that garb, who knows what my heart will do!
That is why I have come and taken shelter of you.

417You will show here, in the town of Nadia,
the world-enchanting Gaurachandra, the best of dancers.

418Moment by moment His dear ones will dress Him beautifully —
who will not lose himself on seeing those curling locks!

419As the Lord is, so are His dear companions;
through you I shall have the darshan of them all."

420Having spoken much in this way, the two think within themselves:
"In how many days will the Lord descend?"

421O Srinivasa, the Ganga and the Ocean here
are ever restless in meditation on Gaurachandra.

422The longing of the Suradhuni and the Ocean grew beyond measure —
and they knew that the time of the Lord's appearance had come.

423The time of the appearance was auspicious in every way:
on the pretext of a lunar eclipse — the kirtana of the holy name.48

424The land of Navadvipa became filled with great effulgence;
the home of Jagannatha Mishra was the very limit of splendor.

425Boundless auspiciousness — and all that was inauspicious went far away;
all the people float in an ocean of bliss.

426The sages offer prayers in many ways;
Brahma and the other gods too shower flowers.

427As soon as the Lord, the son of Shachi, appeared,
the news of the Lord's appearance spread through the worlds.

428Wishing to see the Lord's pastimes, beginning with His appearance,
the Ocean, his heart in turmoil, said much to the Ganga.

429Taking shelter of the Ganga, he comes every day
and watches Gaurachandra's pastimes, intoxicated with joy.

430One day, on the clear bank of the Ganga, the Ocean
saw Gaurachandra with His associates beneath a tree.

431On a divine throne Gaurahari shines in His pastimes,
by His beauty crushing the pride of millions of Kandarpas.

432Kunkuma and gold are no comparison for His beauty;
the world loses itself on seeing the loveliness of His hair.

433The moon of His face destroys the pride of millions of moons;
nectar ever flows as He smiles gently, gently.

434His eyes reach to His ears, His glance is enchanting;
His arms reach to His knees, His chest is broad.

435Most charming are His navel, His waist and His knees;
on the soles of His lovely feet — the rising of the dawn.

436His garment is white silk with a red border;
His body is anointed with the splendid sandal paste of Malaya.

437Adorned with ornaments of many flowers, full of splendor,
with wondrous grace He looks upon His dear ones.

438As Gaurachandra is, so are the Lord's dear ones:
they surround Him on all four sides, supremely beautiful.

439On the right is Sri Nityananda, on the left Gadadhara,
in front Advaita, Srivasa and the other associates.

440All of them, utterly overwhelmed by prema,
gaze unblinking at Gaurachandra.

441The Lord's servants serve Him in many ways on all sides;
seeing this, the Ocean lost all composure in his delight.

442Many desires arose in the Ocean's mind;
the Lord, the Knower of hearts, fulfilled his desires.

443Overwhelmed with bliss, the Ocean
freely beheld the pastimes of the Lord with His associates.

444Again and again he praises the Ganga's good fortune:
in his daily coming and going his only shelter is the Ganga.

445From his coming together with the Ganga — the name Samudra-gati;
now people call this village Samudragarhi.

446Living in this village of Samudragarhi and beholding it
awaken pure devotion to Sri Gaurachandra.

447Gauranga's pastimes here in the homes of the devotees —
how can I tell them with only one mouth, Srinivasa?

448Having said this, Ishana goes from Samudragarhi
in great bliss to Champaka-hatta.49

449He says to Srinivasa: This is the village of Champaka-hatta;
this famous, delightful place is called Chapahati.50

450Here there was a grove of champaka trees;
the garland-makers were always gathering flowers.

451The garland-makers, arranging the champaka flowers beautifully,
sit right here in rows and rows, setting up a market.

452With great happiness many hundreds of brahmanas and good people
buy champaka flowers and worship the Deity.

453From the market of champa flowers came the name Chapahati.
About this I will tell something particular — what the wise relate.

454Here there lived an old, learned brahmana,
exclusively devoted to Sri Krishna, foremost in every respect.

455One day, taking many champaka flowers,
he was worshipping the lotus feet of Krishna in great joy.

456Meditating within his heart on the dark, beautiful form,
he sees the form of Gaura in that dark body.

457Gaura's luster was like a heap of champa flowers;
as he looked and looked, the form vanished.

458His heart distraught at the vanishing of Gaura's form,
he gazes fixedly at the champaka flowers.

459Beholding the luster of the heap of champaka flowers,
as he recites the evidence of the Vedas and other [scriptures], his heart overflows.

460After a while, becoming steady, he speaks according to the scriptures:
"Among the ages this Kali-yuga is blessed.

461In this Kali-yuga Krishna will descend;
He will assume a world-enchanting golden complexion.

462The wise will worship Him with the sacrifice of sankirtana;
the world will float in the ocean of the Lord's pastimes."51

463Considering the scriptures again, he concluded:
"This descent of the Lord will be in Navadvipa itself.

464Many days remain before He descends, I know —
I shall not see that lovely form of Gaurasundara."

465Having said this, he heaves long, long sighs;
his face and chest are drenched — streams flow from both his eyes.

466Utterly distraught, he could not keep his composure;
by the Lord's will sleep overcame him.

467In the guise of a dream Lord Gaurahari appeared to him,
the sweetness of His form like a champaka flower.

468His moon-like face surpasses millions upon millions of moons;
on His head are beautiful curling locks, a snare of Kama.

469No comparison can be given for His eyes, arms and chest;
He enchants the world with the grace of all His limbs.

470Seeing this splendor, the brahmana, his heart jubilant,
fell at His feet and offered many prayers.

471Bestowing mercy on the brahmana, the Lord disappeared;
fainting, the brahmana fell to the ground.

472After a while, regaining consciousness, the best of brahmanas
became like a madman in his loving attachment (anuraga).

473Addressing the champaka flower, he says again and again:
"You have revealed to me Gaura, the Source of avataras!"52

474Because the words in praise of the champaka resounded as in a market (hatta),
the place became famous among the people by the name Champaka-hatta.53

475By the Lord's will the brahmana became calm;
a command came: "What you have set your mind on will be fulfilled."

476Hearing this, in great bliss the brahmana sings the Lord's qualities;
he constantly thinks, "I shall see the Lord in Nadia."

477The deeds of this brahmana dear to the Lord that I have heard —
I cannot narrate them all in detail.

478How [Gaurachandra] here in Champahatta with His associates
enjoys His pastimes — who can describe it?54

479Here is the home of the brahmana Vaninatha,
who is very dear to Gauranga and full of prema.55

480Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:
The brahmana Vaninatha, who lives in Champahatta, is dear to the Lord.56

481Having thus shown the places of the Lord's dear ones,
Ishana leaves the village of Champahatta.

482Approaching the village of Ratupura, he says:
Look, this is Ritudvipa, full of supreme beauty.57

483Formerly a large village, now a village in name only;
here lived many vessels of devotion to Krishna.

484The region of Ratupura is supremely wonderful;
here are Gauranga's most wondrous pastimes.

485O Srinivasa, how [this place] came to be called Ritudvipa —
that I will tell, as the old people tell it.

486Here the six seasons — the rains, autumn, the early winter,
the winter, spring and summer — were all embodied.

487One of them says to another in sweet words:
"Krishnachandra will appear in Nadia."

488Someone says, "He will perform wondrous pastimes;
moment by moment He will increase the joy of us all."

489Someone says, "The son of the lord of Vraja, Gaurahari —
when will He descend and give rise to joy?"

490Someone says, "His descent is at the beginning of [the age of] Kali;
Sri Narada Muni has proclaimed it everywhere."

491Someone says, "Tell the time of the descent."
Someone says, "Immense is the good fortune of spring!"

492The season of spring was filled with irrepressible joy
and itself praises its own good fortune.

493The seasons, together with spring, the king of seasons,
constantly meditate on the Lord's descent.

494The seasons worship [Him] with great longing —
for this reason this place was formerly called Ritudvipa.

495The Lord's pastimes in the six seasons, beginning with spring —
what shall I say of them now? They will be revealed later.

496By seeing this place all afflictions go far away;
[one who sees it], born in Nadia, sees the Lord's pastimes.

497Having said this, Sri Ishana set out from Ritudvipa
on the road to Vidyanagara.58

498To Srinivasa, Narottama and Sri Ramachandra
he speaks most sweet words with joy in his heart:

499look at Vidyanagara — it is supremely beautiful.
I shall tell a little of how [the name] Vidyanagara is explained.

500One day, in the assembly of the gods, Brihaspati
became troubled — so the elders tell.59

501Seeing Brihaspati troubled, the gods
ask, "Why have you become troubled?"

502Brihaspati, with great joy in his heart,
speaks to the gods in most sweet words:

503"In this age of Kali the Lord, in the town of Nadia,
will be born in the house of the brahmana Jagannatha Mishra.

504The Lord Gaurachandra, the son of Jagannatha,
reveals various delights in various avataras.

505In the avatara of Sri Rama — consummate skill in the art of weapons;
in the avatara of Sri Krishna — foremost in herding the cows;

506in the avatara of Sri Gaura — foremost in the study of learning;
what delight there is in this, others do not understand.

507The Lord will fulfill every desire;
He will sport as He has never sported.

508I cannot stay [here]: I shall go quickly to Navadvipa
and worship the Lord for the sake of His appearance."

509Having said much in this way, Brihaspati set out;
day after day he meditates on the Lord's holy sport of learning.

510The Lord will perform the sport of learning in Nadia —
for this reason Brihaspati came here.

511Thus [it is said] in the Chaitanya-bhagavata:
"For the sake of this sport Brihaspati, worshipped by all,
took birth in Navadvipa with his disciples."60

512O Srinivasa, here in Sri Vidyanagara
Brihaspati worships Sri Gaurasundara.

513The Lord's command came to Brihaspati:
"I shall soon appear together with My associates.

514Spread learning in every possible way."
Hearing this, Brihaspati's heart was filled with irrepressible joy.

515He began teaching in a way that words cannot describe;
all became intent on the pursuit of learning.

516For the sake of the Lord's sport he spread learning here —
for this reason [this place] received the name Sri Vidyanagara.

517Seeing this Vidyanagara brings every perfection;
hearing of Vidyanagara dispels ignorance.

518In this Vidyanagara Gauranga, with His associates,
sports with great delight in the homes of the devotees.

519Having said this, Ishana Thakura slowly,
with joy in his heart, enters Jannagara.61

520He says to Srinivasa: look at the village of Jannagara;
formerly the most learned called it Jahnudvipa.

521How the name Jahnudvipa became known on earth —
I shall tell what all the elders tell.

522Here Jahnu Muni, in supreme bliss,
seeing the beauty of Navadvipa, reflects in his mind:62

523"This Kali-yuga is more blessed than the other Kalis:
in it the Lord Sri Krishna Chaitanya descends.

524Together with all the dear associates of all the avataras
He descends in Navadvipa at the beginning of Kali.

525He will assume that golden complexion beyond all comparison;
the grace of His holy form will be wondrous.

526In Navadvipa He will perform wondrous pastimes —
shall I see them, will [my] desire be fulfilled?"

527Reflecting thus, the sage, with joy in his heart,
worships Gaurachandra, the enchanter of the worlds.

528As the sage meditated with closed eyes,
the merciful Lord appeared in his heart.

529The beautiful dark form enchants the three worlds;
He stands in a threefold bend, a peacock feather shining on His head.

530Holding the flute in His hands, He plays it softly, softly;
His lovely moonlike face glitters and shines.

531Having seen this, he sees Him as a young sannyasi,
with staff and kamandalu in His hands and no shikha on His head.63

532He wears a kaupina and an outer cloth the color of dawn;
the radiance of His body surpasses the splendor of millions of suns.

533Beholding this, the sage cannot remain steady;
the moment he opened his eyes, He appeared before him in person.

534With His lovely curling hair He maddens the world;
the ornaments on all His limbs glitter and shine.

535With the radiance of His beauty He lights up the world;
gold and the like are dull — such a comparison does not suit Him.

536The grace of His body breaks the pride of millions of Kandarpas;
seeing it, the sage was overwhelmed with ecstasy.

537Seeing the sage's condition, the Lord Gaurahari
mercifully steadied the sage.

538In great bliss the sage fell at the Lord's feet
and moistened [His] lotus feet with his tears.

539Offering many prayers, he stood before [Him]
and fixed both his eyes on the Lord's holy face.

540The Lord, embracing [him], says again and again,
"All your desires will be fulfilled."

541Having said much in this way, the Lord vanished;
by the Lord's will the sage regained his composure.

542He praises his own good fortune within his mind:
"At last my austerities have borne fruit."

543Reflecting thus, the sage looks in all four directions;
how great is his longing to tell the glory of Nadia!

544Constantly he sings the qualities of the Moon of Nadia,
grey with dust, drenched with streams of tears.

545Jahnu Muni stays here in great bliss —
for this reason the wise call [this place] Jahnudvipa.

546The pastimes of Sri Gaurachandra in Jahnudvipa —
when I think of them all, my heart breaks.

547Here there was a wondrous forest full of flowers;
people say, "This is the penance-grove of Sri Jahnu Muni.

548By seeing this place all afflictions go far away,
and pure devotion to the Lord's holy feet grows."

549Having said this, Ishana went from Jannagara
toward the village of Maugachhi.64

550Beholding the beauty of the Maugachhi region,
he says to Srinivasa with a slight smile:

551among people this village is known as Maugachhi;
formerly its name was Modadrumadvipa.

552How the name Modadrumadvipa became known —
I shall tell what I heard from the lips of the elders.

553To keep His father's word, the son of Kaushalya
left Ayodhya and went forth into the forest.

554Casting off His royal attire, the Lord, His heart in great joy,
wanders from forest to forest with Janaki and Lakshmana.65

555Whatever path He walks with His most tender feet,
that path becomes soft — nothing pricks them.

556Wind, rain and the heat of the sun are always favorable [to Him];
the wondrous pastime of His wandering is unequalled in the world.

557All the people of many lands — women, men and others —
seeing Ramachandra's beauty, all were maddened.

558Every forest, mountain and other place where He stayed
became a great tirtha, its fame made manifest.

559Some distance north of here
Sri Ramachandra stayed in a mountain cave.

560Even today people make pilgrimage there;
merely by seeing that place all sorrow is destroyed.

561O Srinivasa, wandering and wandering in this way,
He came here — what comparison could one give?

562In front — Rama, the son of King Dasharatha;
in the middle — Sri Janaki; behind — Thakura Lakshmana.

563Seeing the beauty of Sri Rama, Janaki and Lakshmana —
what to speak of others — even beasts and birds are utterly enchanted.

564Lotus-eyed Rama, worshipped by Brahma and the others,
walks with the gait of a lordly elephant, looking in all directions.

565From some distance He gazes toward Navadvipa
and smiles softly, softly, with great amusement in His heart.

566Seeing the smiling face of Sri Ramachandra,
Janaki asks, "Tell me the reason for Your smile."

567Hearing Sri Sita's skilful words, He, absorbed in rasa,
speaks to Janaki in the sweetest speech:

568"After the Dvapara, at the beginning of the Kali-yuga,
there will be a great wonder in this village of Navadvipa.

569Having performed most wonderful pastimes in Navadvipa,
after that I will accept sannyasa.

570Just as I wander now, so I will wander then;
thinking of that wandering, I smiled just now."

571Hearing this, Janaki entreats with folded palms:
"How will You, Lord, sport in the town of Nadia?"

572Hearing this, the Lord says: "I will be born in a brahmana family;
in childhood I will show all kinds of mischief.

573I will assume a wondrous, incomparable golden complexion;
looking at Me, the three worlds will go mad.

574I will become learned, My fame will spread through the world;
after My father's passing I will marry twice.

575Just as I have now offered pinda at Gaya,
so I will offer pinda according to the custom of the people.

576In Navadvipa I will increase the joy of the devotees;
I will spread sankirtana, which is rare even for Brahma and others.

577Having instructed My associates in various ways,
I will become a sannyasi and go away to other lands."

578Hearing this, Sri Janaki says with a smiling face:
"If You will accept sannyasa, why then marry at all?

579It seems to me that this is improper:
being supremely merciful, You will become merciless."

580Hearing this, Rama, abashed, says to Sita:
"Do you not know that I always abide in Navadvipa?"

581Speaking thus, with a sweet gait
He came to this place with Janaki and Lakshmana.

582Here there was a huge banyan tree;66
they stood beneath it, in its wonderful shade.

583Again Sri Janaki says to the Lord of her life:
"What is the Lord's joy of sankirtana in Nadia like?"

584Janaki's beloved, the lotus-eyed Rama,
says to His beloved: "Close your eyes."

585Hearing this, Janaki closes both her eyes
and beholds wondrous pastimes in Navadvipa.

586Song, dance and music in Nadia have reached their limit;
the Lord's devotees are countless — there is no comparison for them.

587Amid His associates is the beautiful form of Gaura,
in the kaishora age, an ocean of great rasa.

588With the graceful bends of His limbs He enchants the worlds;
seeing that beauty, Sita cannot stay composed.

589Opening her eyes, she looks at the Lord of her life;
smiling, Sri Ramachandra calmed her.

590Sri Sumitra-nandana, who knows all truths,
became agitated, remembering those pastimes.

591Here everyone's joy (moda) increased beyond measure;
for this reason the place was formerly called Modadrumadvipa.

592Whoever sees this Modadrumadvipa
is favoured by Rama, Janaki and Lakshmana.

593O Srinivasa, this place is Ramavata;
when Kali entered, the banyan disappeared.

594From here Ramachandra, with great joy in His heart,
goes on to Utkala with Sri Sita and Lakshmana.

595Entering Utkala and seeing a charming place,
He installed Shiva named Rameshvara.

596That place is near the river Svarnarekha;67
the fortunate visit it with joy in their hearts.

597From there Ramachandra wanders from forest to forest
and in place after place performs most wondrous deeds.68

598In this village of Maugachhi Sri Gaurasundara
performed a wondrous pastime hidden from others.

599A brahmana who worshipped Rama lived here;
O Srinivasa, let me tell you a little about him.

600On the day that Vishvambhara appeared,
that brahmana was in Mishra's house.

601At the moment of the appearance the gods cry, "Victory!";
seeing the gods, the brahmana was bewildered.

602In supreme joy he reflects within his mind:
"My Lord has appeared — of this there is no doubt.

603This Jagannatha Mishra is King Dasharatha;
Shachi, the mother of the world, is Kaushalya herself."

604Telling no one anything, having seen Vishvambhara,
he went from Mishra's house back to his own home.

605When he began to meditate on Rama, dark as durva grass,
he sees Mishra's son — an incomparable golden form.

606While he was full of such thoughts, sleep overcame him,
and in the guise of a dream Gaurachandra appeared before him.

607The radiance of His limbs surpasses a golden mirror;
His moonlike face puts to shame the splendour of the moon.

608His arms reach to His knees, His chest is broad,
the play of His eyes, extending to His ears, is captivating.

609On His head is lovely, glossy, curling, abundant hair,
wound with many-coloured garlands of various flowers.

610On His neck is the sacred thread — a wondrous beauty;
every limb is beautiful — there is no comparison for Him in the world.

611He shines on a wonderful jewelled throne;
before Him Brahma and the other gods offer praises.

612The brahmana looks and looks with joy in his heart —
and sees Gaurachandra in a form dark as durva grass.

613The Lord who enchants the worlds, the son of Kaushalya,
shines in a most wondrous royal attire.

614With a smiling face, He holds a bow and arrows in His hands;
on His left is Sita, on His right Lakshmana holds the parasol.

615Before Him is Hanuman, the son of the Wind;
he stands with folded palms, and wondrous is his posture.

616Seeing such beauty of Ramachandra, the best of brahmanas
falls to the ground and bows again and again.

617The Lord, affectionate to His devotees, the abode of virtues,
showed the brahmana boundless mercy.

618When the Lord vanished from sight, his sleep broke;
the brahmana, greatly agitated, could not control his body.

619Seeing his state, the Lord again consoled him in a dream
and forbade him to reveal any of this.

620Becoming calm, the brahmana, with great joy in his heart,
tells no one anything, having seen Gaurachandra.

621This brahmana, a very old man, at the time of his departure69
out of mercy told some of it in private.

622He was boundlessly merciful to me;
what can I say of the wonderful glory of that brahmana!

623Look: this is the dwelling place of that brahmana;
by merely seeing this place the fear of worldly existence is dispelled.

624Here Gaurachandra with His associates
manifested the pastimes of Rama — I saw it with my own eyes.

625Having said this, Sri Ishana, filled with prema,
went from Maugachhi to Vaikunthapura.70

626To Srinivasa and Narottama he gently says:
Look, here is Vaikunthapura, renowned throughout the world.

627How the name Vaikunthapura came about
I will tell a little — just as people tell it.

628One day Narada comes from Sri Vaikuntha
to Shiva on Mount Kailasa.

629Shiva with his associates, seated on a skin,
is telling the deeds of Sri Krishna with his five mouths.

630Seeing Sri Mahesha from afar, Narada
was overwhelmed and, bowing, fell to the ground.

631The three-eyed god, embracing Narada,
asks: "Where have you come from?"

632Narada replies with a jubilant heart:
"I went to have darshan of Sri Narayana.

633The Lord of Vaikuntha with His dear associates
is constantly immersed in talk of Navadvipa.

634Navadvipa in Bharata-varsha is a delightful place;
He and His associates rejoice, preparing to set out there.

635Seeing this great festivity, I came here in haste.
I do not know what bliss there will be in Nadia!"

636Hearing Narada's words, the god Maheshvara
smiles gently; his body is filled with prema.

637Looking at Narada, he sways his head
and roars — how wondrous are his movements!

638The holy Lord of Mount Kailasa was overwhelmed;
his white body is drenched with tears.

639Seeing Mahesha absorbed in the Navadvipa pastimes,
Narada Muni took his leave and went away.

640O Srinivasa, here Sri Narada,
seeing the beauty of Navadvipa, reflects within his mind:

641"This Navadvipa-dhama contains all dhamas;
the Lord of all dhamas always sports here.

642I have come after seeing Sri Narayana, the Lord of Vaikuntha;
will I see the Lord of Vaikuntha here with my own eyes?"

643By the muni's mere wish he directly sees
Sri Vaikuntha with its dwellers and the Lord of Vaikuntha.

644Narada Muni was overwhelmed with prema
and could not hold back the tears of his two eyes.

645Having offered many prayers in Navadvipa-dhama,
he went to Dvaraka and had darshan of Krishna.

646At Narada's arrival the Lord of Rukmini,
overwhelmed with prema, cast His glance upon him.

647Having pleased Narada in many ways,
He asks: "Where have you come from?"

648The muni says, "I have come from Navadvipa,"
and, having said this, fell silent.

649Knowing the muni's heart, merciful Krishna
took the form of Gaura, which enchants the world.

650Seeing the Moon of Nadia, Narada Muni —
streams of tears flow from his eyes; he cannot contain himself.

651What he became cannot be put into words at all;
and at that very moment he sees the dark, beautiful Krishna.

652The form of Gaura-Krishna, a priceless jewel,
the muni hid away in the casket of his heart.

653He cannot turn his eyes away and keeps on gazing;
the Lord rejoices, beholding Narada's behavior.

654Calming Narada, He says in soft words,
"Go quickly to Shiva on Kailasa.

655Make known everywhere the coming to Navadvipa:
the time has come, there is no need for delay."

656Hearing Krishna's supremely sweet words,
the muni took his leave and set out.

657Singing on his vina the deeds of Gaura-Krishna,
he soon arrived at Mount Kailasa.

658Bowing to Shiva, the muni told him everything;
hearing it, Mahadeva was greatly overwhelmed.

659Taking Narada in his arms, he dances;
the bliss that there was on Kailasa cannot be described.

660O Srinivasa, the muni proclaimed this everywhere;
and again Sri Narada Muni came to this place.

661Within himself the muni ponders what is in his heart:
"What I saw in Dvaraka — shall I see it here?"

662Pondering thus, the muni looks in all four directions
and sees the opulence of Dvaraka in Nadia.

663On a jeweled throne Gaurachandra shines;
the radiance of His beauty enchants millions of Kandarpas.

664What Narada Gosani became on seeing the Lord's beauty —
there is no power to tell.

665The Lord says to Narada in sweet words,
"In a few days you will see the manifest pastimes here.

666What you have in mind will come to pass in every way:
I shall easily destroy the terrible suffering of living beings."

667Saying something like this and showing mercy to Narada,
the Lord Gaurahari vanished from sight.

668O Srinivasa, when the Lord vanished,
the muni was distraught — how much arose in his mind!

669Here, at this place, Narayana-pitha, the best of munis
stayed some days and then set off on his travels.71

670Here Narada had the darshan of Narayana;
for this reason the name Narayana-pitha arose.

671Here the opulence of Vaikuntha is manifest;
therefore Sri Vaikunthapura is famous in the world.

672The king of this land at that time was a worthy one;
he established the service of Sri Narayana here.

673After some time the village all but vanished;
then once again it became very populous here.

674There lived here an old and learned brahmana;
his worship was with the Lakshmi-Narayana mantra.

675His exclusive love for Lakshmi-Narayana —
what can I say? I saw his pure way of life.

676From time to time, going to the house of Vallabha Mishra,72
he would serve Lakshmi-Narayana, finding a moment of privacy.

677He had great affection for Vallabha Mishra,
and Mishra Mahashaya revered the brahmana as his guru.

678On the day that Lakshmi was married to the Lord,
on that day this brahmana was there.73

679At the time of the wedding, seeing Lakshmi and Vishvambhara,
the brahmana dances, crying, "Lakshmi-Narayana!"

680Tears of bliss flow ceaselessly from the brahmana's eyes;
his whole body thrills, and he cannot keep his composure.

681By the Lord's will the brahmana grew somewhat calm;
staying there that night, he returned to his own dwelling.

682His dwelling was quite dilapidated — he lived almost under a tree;
entering his hut, the brahmana floats in tears.

683Remembering Lakshmi and Gaurachandra in Mishra's house,
his heart ceaselessly overflows with the bliss of prema.

684Within himself the brahmana reaches a firm conclusion:
"Narayana in the form of Gaura is the son of Shachi.

685Vallabha Mishra's daughter is Lakshmi herself.
Lakshmi and Narayana have appeared in bodily form on earth.

686The Beloved of Lakshmi, my Lord Gaurachandra —
will He show me mercy, seeing how wretched and lowly I am?"

687In many ways he offers praises to the Lord,
and the Lord appeared before his eyes in the brahmana's hut.

688Manifesting a supremely wonderful play,
the splendor of Vaikuntha appeared in the brahmana's hut.

689The world-enchanting Lord in the form of Sri Gaura
shines on a jeweled throne together with Lakshmi.

690Their holy bodies are adorned with various jeweled ornaments;
what comparison is there for the sweetness of the beauty of both?

691At that very moment the Lord Gaurachandra, the merciful,
became four-armed; seeing this, the brahmana is amazed.

692Falling at the Lord's feet, the brahmana offered many prayers;
the Lord, who is subject to His devotees, smiling, says to the brahmana,

693"Birth after birth you are My dear servant;
you are worthy to see My pastimes.

694What you have now seen, tell no one;
whatever you may ever desire, that desire will be fulfilled."

695Saying this, He placed His feet on the brahmana's head,
and the pastime of the inconceivable Lord vanished from sight.

696What the brahmana became — who can describe it?
He ever swims in the ocean of the Navadvipa pastimes.

697O Srinivasa, how much shall I tell of this?
Here, look: this is where the brahmana's hut stood.

698The Lord, the son of Shachi, with the assembly of His devotees,
performed endless pastimes in Sri Vaikunthapura.

699One who has an ardent longing to see Sri Vaikunthapura
easily has all his desires fulfilled.

700Saying this and bowing to Sri Vaikunthapura,
he goes on to Matapura, looking in all four directions.

701Sri Ishana Thakura says to Srinivasa:
Here ahead, look, is the village named Matapura.74

702Formerly the village was named Sri Mahatpura;
people call it "Mahat-prasanga-pura."75

703By Sri Krishna's will the Pandavas lived in exile in the forest;
in that exile many great wonders came about.

704The five Pandava brothers wander through many lands;
there is no end to telling the deeds of the Pandavas.

705Those lands to which the Pandavas did not go —
the learned call those lands "bypassed by the Pandavas."

706All the glories of the Pandavas are known from the Puranas:
they destroyed asuras and rakshasas in place after place.

707Wandering on and on, they entered the land of Gauda
and stayed in Rarh, in a village named Ekachakra.

708The asuras and rakshasas in the region of Ekachakra —
Bhima slew them all, and his fame spread everywhere.76

709How the five brothers, the Sri Pandavas, with Draupadi
were devoted to the welfare of the people, there is no power to tell.

710In Ekachakra, in solitude, they live in great bliss,
ever remembering Baladeva and Krishnachandra.

711Seeing the charming beauty of the land of Ekachakra,
Yudhishthira, the wisest of the wise, ponders within himself:

712"I have seen many lands, but none like this;
nowhere was my heart so drawn.

713From this I understand that this place is a site of Krishna's pastimes;
if Krishna reveals it, I shall know its glory."

714As he pondered thus, the night was almost over;
by Krishna's will a little sleep came over him.

715In the guise of a dream, Balarama, the son of Rohini,
appeared before him; His beauty was beyond compare.

716Smiling gently, in a wonderful rush of affection,
He says something to King Yudhishthira in soft words:

717"Some distance from here is a village named Navadvipa,
encircled by the Suradhuni, a supremely charming place.77

718At the beginning of Kali, Krishna will be born there in a brahmana family,
in a hidden form, with great delight.

719His dear ones will be born in various lands;
by His will My birth is right here.78

720This Ekachakra is the place of My pastimes."
Saying this, Baladeva disappeared.

721Amazed, the king thinks within himself;
he sees the village of Ekachakra as if it were Shvetadvipa.79

722Just as he was seeing the beauty of the land, his sleep broke;
in the morning he told the dream to his brothers.

723From Ekachakra the five Pandava brothers
came to Navadvipa and stopped at this place.

724Seeing the beauty of Navadvipa, he rejoices more at every moment;
Maharaja Yudhishthira ponders within himself:

725"As I saw in a dream in the village of Ekachakra —
what shall I see here?" — and, thinking so, he cannot be at rest.

726What was in the king's mind cannot be fathomed;
by Krishna's will a little sleep came over him.

727In the guise of a dream, Krishna and Baladeva, the two brothers,
appeared before him; Their beauty enchants the world.

728Krishna, smiling, says to King Yudhishthira,
"This town of Nadia is My birthplace.

729In the Kali-yuga, appearing together with My associates,
I shall make the world mad and Myself be maddened in sankirtana.

730Together with all of you I shall sport on the shore of the ocean80
and make [you] drink the rare nectar of the prema of Vraja."

731Saying this, and knowing what was in the king's heart,
They took on the supremely beautiful form of Gaura.

732Seeing such a form of Krishna and Baladeva,
Yudhishthira, king of devotees, forgot himself.

733Bathed in tears in supreme bliss,
he rolls on the ground and falls at the feet of the two Lords.

734The two Lords embraced the king
