and, speaking words of consolation, disappeared.

735When the Lords disappeared, his heart was thrown into turmoil;
awaking, he sees that the night is giving way to dawn.

736Telling his brothers this wondrous account,
they stayed here joyfully for some days.

737The noble Yudhishthira is the best of the great (mahat);
because his dwelling was here, [this place] is called Mahatpura.

738Here five banyan trees spread wide;
their very cool shade enchanted everyone.

739The five brothers, the Sri Pandavas, together with Draupadi,
seeing the beauty of Navadvipa, lost their composure here.

740There was [here] a high mound named Yudhishthira-vedi;81
by the Lord's will all of that has vanished.

741O Srinivasa, how much shall I tell of that!
Here the Pandavas lived unrecognized.82

742By the order of Sri Navadvipa-chandra
the Pandavas set out from here for the land of Odra.

743In Utkala, near Purushottama-puri,
they stayed for some days in a wonderful forest.

744There was a Deity there named Sri Madhava;
He was in the possession of a Rakshasa — they found Him.83

745With blows of his club Bhima destroyed that Rakshasa
and spread the service of Sri Madhava among all people.

746Even today fortunate people serve Him.
Who can tell all the deeds of the Pandavas?

747In this Mahatpura Gaurachandra, in great joy,
manifests wondrous pastimes together with His associates.

748Whoever sees Mahatpura even once
easily obtains the priceless treasure of bhakti.

749One who has love for talk of Sri Mahatpura —
by his mere glance the evil-mindedness of others is dispelled.

750Saying this, he goes on from Sri Mahatpura;
remembering the pastimes of Gauranga, he is bathed in tears.

751On the eastern bank of the Ganga is the village of Rahupura;84
some call Rahupura Rudrapura.

752Sri Ishana Thakura, arriving in Rahupura,
says to Srinivasa with a slight smile:

753This Rahupura was formerly named Rudradvipa;
the village has vanished, and now only the place remains.

754How the name Rudradvipa became known —
I shall tell a little of what I heard from the mouths of the wise.

755Gaurachandra would appear in Nadia —
at this there was great joy in Sri Rudra's heart.

756Here Rudradeva together with his associates
became mad in kirtana of Gaura's deeds.

757On all four sides are the charming sounds of various instruments;
in wondrous poses Maheshvara dances.

758The earth trembles under the weight of Sri Rudra's feet;
who, seeing the beauty of that dance, could keep his composure?

759Who does not dance when Rudra dances?
In the heavens the demigods shower down various flowers.

760Joy grows unceasingly in the demigods' hearts;
all say, "The burden of the living beings' sorrow has been broken."

761Even before the Lord's birth, Rudra sings of the Lord's birth:
"Now the Lord will surely be born in Nadia.

762Seeing the pastime of the Lord's birth, I shall gladden my eyes."
Saying this, even in the heavens the demigods dance.

763Singing the Lord's qualities, Rudra forgot himself;
the Lord, seeing Rudra's state, lost His patience.

764Appearing to Rudradeva unseen by others,
He calmed Rudradeva, consoling him thus:

765"The desire of your heart I shall fulfil:
very soon I shall appear together with My associates."

766At the Lord's words Rudra grew calm and, in great bliss,
praises Gaurachandra in many ways.

767Sri Gaurasundara embraced Rudradeva
and, overwhelmed with prema, disappeared.

768When the Lord disappeared, Rudra's heart was thrown into turmoil;
after some time, by the Lord's will, he grew calm.

769Sitting here with his associates, Rudra
showers a rain of nectar, telling of Gaura's deeds.

770O Srinivasa, this is a supremely holy place;
because of Sri Rudra's pastimes it is called Rudradvipa.

771By merely seeing this place one is freed from evil-mindedness:
Rudra awakens love for Gaura's lotus feet.

772Thus Sri Ishana, having told the glory of the place,
joyfully goes to the village of Belpaukhera.85

773He says to Srinivasa: This village is Belpaukhera;
the ancients say that its former name was Bilvapaksha.

774How this place came by the name Bilvapaksha —
I shall tell a little of what the people of old say.

775Here dwelt the Deity of five-faced Shiva;
who knows how to tell his glory?

776Whatever anyone prays for in a matter concerning Sri Krishna,
the merciful Five-faced fulfils it.

777Once several ascetic brahmanas,
for the fulfilment of their desires, were worshipping Shiva.

778When they had worshipped Shiva with bilva leaves for a fortnight,
Shiva became greatly pleased at heart.

779Looking on them with a merciful glance, the five-faced Maheshvara
says to the brahmanas, "Take the boon you desire."

780The brahmanas said, "That which is the best of all deeds —
by your grace give that to us."

781Shiva says to the brahmanas, "You have spoken wonderfully:
there is no deed better than service to Krishna."

782The brahmanas say, "Service is the best.
How will it be obtained — tell us, O merciful one."

783The Five-faced says, "Have no worry at all:
you will obtain service to Krishna without effort.

784In a few days, in this very town of Nadia,
Krishna will descend in a brahmana's house.

785You too will appear along with Him;
when He is absorbed in His childhood play, you will give [Him] great happiness.

786Studying under Him,
you will know Him to be the complete Brahman, the Eternal.

787With His dear devotees, ever rejoicing,
all of you will be engaged in His service."

788Hearing the words of the five-faced Mahadeva,
all the brahmanas fell to the ground and bowed down.

789Offering many praises and taking their leave,
they meditate on Krishna's lotus feet, remaining in seclusion.

790O Srinivasa, by the will of Gaura-Krishna,
after some time the Five-faced became almost hidden.

791The brahmanas worshipped with bilva leaves for a fortnight —
for this reason the wise call [this place] Bilvapaksha.

792At the sight of this place the Five-faced, in great joy,
brings [one] to Gaurachandra, who is supremely hard to attain.

793How Vishvambhara sports here with His dear devotees —
who can describe it?

794Having told this much, Sri Thakura Ishana
goes to Bharaidanga, a great holy place.86

795With joy in his heart he says to Srinivasa:
Behold Bharaidanga, a wonderful settlement.

796How the name Bharadvaja-tila formerly became known —
as the people of old tell it, so I shall tell it.

797The sage Bharadvaja,87 from the ocean and other tirthas,
came to Chakradaha, near the Ganga.88

798Now people call Chakradaha Chakda;
from there he proceeded to Navadvipa.

799O Srinivasa, the sage, coming here,
was overwhelmed beholding Navadvipa.

800Staying some days in this forest on a high mound,
he worships Gaurachandra, feeling himself humble and lowly.

801Won over by Bharadvaja's prema, Gaurahari
appeared before him in great and wondrous beauty.

802Bharadvaja offered abundant obeisances and praises;
the Lord commanded, "Take the boon you desire."

803The sage says, "Lord, this is my prayer:
may I see Your pastimes in Navadvipa."

804The Lord says, "It will be as is in your heart."
Saying this, the Merciful One disappeared.

805When the Lord disappeared, the sage could not be calm;
who can understand what the sage went through?

806Bowing down to Navadvipa, the sage Bharadvaja
went off wandering, to bless the earth.

807On this raised place Bharadvaja dwelt;
for this reason the name Bharadvaja-tila arose.

808Here are the most wondrous pastimes of Gauranga;
by seeing this place one's desires are fulfilled.

809Saying this, Ishana Thakura, absorbed in prema,
went on toward the village of Suvarna-vihara.

810He says to Srinivasa: Behold this village;
from of old its name has been Suvarna-vihara.89

811How the name Suvarna-vihara came about —
I shall tell a little of what the wise have said.

812In this land there lived a fortunate king;
his undivided devotion to Krishna was foremost in every respect.

813The disciples, the disciples' disciples and other followers of Narada are great souls; one of them came to the king's abode.

814The king, showing him the greatest honor,
seated him on a seat, bowing down to the ground.

815He asks him about the many avataras of the Lord;
he told everything in the sweetest speech.

816Pleased with the king, that great soul
again speaks the sweetest words to the king:

817"In Kali, becoming the golden-complexioned avatara,
He will perform wondrous pastimes in Navadvipa.90

818Sankirtana, supremely hard to attain even for Brahma and others —
intoxicated with sankirtana, He will intoxicate the world.

819As He danced in the great rasa in Vrindavana,
so by His dancing He will give happiness to His dear devotees.

820Navadvipa will be the very limit of happiness;
for this reason the Creator established such a settlement.

821The truth of Navadvipa-dhama is beyond the reach of others;
only he will know it to whom the Lord's associates reveal it."

822Having said this much, that Vaishnava, a great soul,
showed mercy to the king and departed.

823Hearing all this, the king reflects in his mind,
"Shame on this human birth, shame on this life!

824I was ceaselessly absorbed in the affairs of the kingdom;
I had no association with saints — such is my misfortune.

825Without the association of saints no endeavor succeeds;
only now has a saint, full of mercy, shown me mercy.

826Now at last I know that this Nadia is the Lord's abode."
As he reflected thus, his heart overflowed with prema.

827Gazing toward Navadvipa, he sheds streams of tears;
again and again he bows down to the land of Navadvipa.

828In Navadvipa-dhama the king prays,
"Grant this: may I be born at that time."

829At these words a voice from the sky came to the king:
"At the time of [the Lord's] descent you will be born in Nadia."

830Though the king rejoiced at hearing these words,
still he could not keep his composure: so much arose in his mind.

831The Lord who is affectionate to His devotees, Vishvambhara Raya,
in the guise of a dream shows the king the wonder of His pastimes.

832On all four sides — thousands upon thousands of devotees;
they play various instruments, and with their singing they enchant the world.

833In their midst dances the moon of Nadia —
a dark, beautiful form, like a mass of nectar.

834Seeing Krishnachandra, the king's eyes are soothed;
and at that very moment he sees Him golden in complexion.

835Losing his composure, the king reflects in his mind,
"Who is this golden form sporting in sankirtana?"

836As he reflected thus, the king's sleep broke;
becoming calm, he praises his own good fortune.

837The sporting of the golden form became his meditation;
for this reason the place bears the name Suvarna-vihara.

838O Srinivasa, I shall tell you more
of the Lord's wondrous play in His manifest pastimes.

839Here Gaurahari with His company of devotees
dances, and people watch, filling their eyes.

840Beside themselves, people say to one another,
"Is a golden form sporting in the kirtana?"

841Someone says, "There is no complexion so beautiful;
nowhere in the world do I see anything to compare [with it].

842What wondrous play — it enchants the three worlds!"
Saying this, no one can remain composed.

843Thus [arose] this celebrated name Suvarna-vihara.
I have told it briefly — I cannot relate it in full.

844Whoever sees the village of Suvarna-vihara,
his mind sinks into the pastimes of Sri Gauranga.

845Saying this, from the village of Suvarna-vihara
he goes to Mayapura, to Mishra's home.

846Mayapura is a supremely unprecedented, delightful place;
whoever sees it even once, his eyes are soothed.

847Who can find the limit of Mayapura's glory?
Brahma and others always meditate on the place Mayapura.

848Together with Srinivasa, Ramachandra and Narottama
he came to such a Mayapura, to Mishra's house.

849Entering inside the house, Sri Ishana
was overwhelmed with prema, remembering the Purusha.91

850After some time, becoming calm and calming everyone,
standing to one side, they behold the sweet beauty of the house.

851To Srinivasa he speaks very softly:
This house of Mishra is the Mahayogapitha.

852This house increases the sweetness of the Lord's pastimes;
unfathomable to others, this house is like a lotus.

853Together with Shachi, the best of Mishras, the son of Upendra,
ceaselessly worships Vishnu in this Vishnu-mandapa.92

854As Jagannatha Mishra was mature in every respect,
so too was his wife Shachi — who does not praise her?

855At the wedding of Shachi and Jagannatha there was great joy;
for all who saw it, all their sorrows were dispelled.

856Nilambara Chakravarti, a man of great learning —
Shachi was his daughter; he gave her to Mishra.93

857To Sri Shachi were born eight daughters and one son;
the son's name — Vishvarupa — is known everywhere.94

858There is no end to telling of Vishvarupa's character;
the fortunate describe his qualities in various ways.

859Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
"Then his guru, knower of the truth, gave him, who knew the meaning of all the shastras,
the title 'Sriman Mishra-purandara.'95

860Once him — a man of good family, learned, the best of the righteous —
the glorious, magnanimous Nilambara by name, a Chakravarti,

861having called him, gave [him] his daughter Shachi — he, honored in his clan;
and Mishra-purandara too, obtaining Shachi, prospered.

862Then, as he dwelt at home, his dharma increased through hospitality, propitiatory rites, purifications, and the fruits of regular and optional rites.

863There in time eight auspicious daughters were born to him;
one after another, by fate, they passed away. Shachi,

864her mind scorched by the grief of a mother's love, in her heart went to Hari as her refuge for the sake of a son; and he, the glorious one, performed the pitri-yajna.96

865In time he obtained a son like the son of a god;
Jagannatha rejoiced, like a pauper who has found a treasure.

866The father gave the glorious [child] the name Vishvarupa.
By him, the great soul, studying, in a very short time

867the Vedas, the nyaya-shastra and the supreme true yoga were mastered;
he was all-knowing, wise, peaceful, a benefactor of all.

868Ever intent on meditation on Hari, he did not turn his mind to sense objects,
ceaselessly intoxicated with tasting the rasa of the Srimad-Bhagavatam."

869O Srinivasa, Vishvarupa's heart —
who can understand what he ceaselessly contemplates?

870Sri Advaita Acharya knows all truths;
"I will bring the Lord down" — at this He rejoices every moment.

871With Ganga water, tulasi, sandal paste and flowers
He worships the Lord, giving great thunderous roars.97

872Gaining great bliss from Sri Advaita's thunderous roars,
Gaurachandra took shelter in Shachi's womb.

873The splendor of Shachi and Jagannatha grew beyond measure;
in Shachi's womb Gaurachandra happily abides.

874When, counting one, two, six months had passed,
the Lord, dwelling in the womb, attracts all hearts.

875Suddenly Sri Advaita, coming right here,
worshipped Shachi's womb, offering sandal paste and fragrances.

876Circumambulating [her], He joyfully went to His own home;
Shachi and Jagannatha here were amazed.

877Here, before Shachi, Brahma and others offer praises;
remaining in the womb, the Lord displays various wonders.

878For thirteen months He remained in Shachi's womb;
who can understand this supramundane lila?

879Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita-mahakavya, in the second sarga, the twenty-fourth shloka:
"Gradually those ten months and three more,
drawing near, came to completion;
the last of them, the month of Tapasya, full of blessings,
became the sole source of the world's happiness."98

880In the year fourteen hundred and seven [of the] Shaka [era], on the full moon of Phalguna, under the Phalguni nakshatra, the limit of all auspiciousness, —

881at the time of a lunar eclipse Vishvambhara
descended: behold, here is the house of [His] birth.99

882Jagannatha Mishra obtained a jewel of a son;
with [His] form, beautiful in every limb, [He] enraptured everyone.

883Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
"Seeing the son — with eyes like blossoming lotuses, with a face like the shining full moon, golden in radiance,
Himself by His effulgence freeing the directions of darkness — he…"100

884O Srinivasa, on the pretext of the lunar eclipse
He made everyone take His own name.101

885Everywhere immense crowds of people gathered;
they perform kirtana, and joy arises in every heart.

886He from whose mouth I never heard the name of Krishna —
he too, taking the name, bathes in the Ganga.

887What to speak of others — even the yavanas say "Krishna."
Thus Shachi's son delivers the living beings.

888The Lord who loves sankirtana was born amid sankirtana;
the glory of sankirtana is known in the three worlds.

889Thus [it is said] in the words of the Prabhasa-khanda cited in the Padyavali:
"Cleansing the mirror of the heart, extinguishing the great forest fire of worldly existence,
spreading the moonlight on the white water lilies of the highest good, the life of the bride of knowledge,
expanding the ocean of bliss, giving at every step a taste of full nectar,
bathing the whole self — supremely victorious is Sri Krishna-sankirtana!"102

890Whoever has heard the kirtana of the holy name — he too is blessed;
who can tell the glory of hearing?

891Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
"The love that arises in half a moment in such as us when we hear the kirtana of Sri Hari
does not arise even from millions of sacrifices."

892The news of the Lord's birth spread everywhere;
drawn by the Lord, everyone lost their composure.

893Countless people rushed to Mishra's house;
no one could tell who was a god and who a human.

894In Mishra's house an ocean of bliss surges;
the wise describe in detail the pastimes of the Lord's birth.

895Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Vasanta):
"Victory, victory!" — a clamor [fills] the town of Nadia:
from the womb of Shachi Gorachand was born.

896The lunar day is the full moon of Phalguna, the nakshatra Phalguni;
at an auspicious moment Gora was born, the jewel of the twice-born.

897Surpassing the full moon, He manifested [Himself];
the darkness went far away, having lost hope.

898In the Dvapara-yuga there was the descent of Krishna;
He Himself then slew the asuras.

899From the womb of Shachi there was the descent of Gora;
in the Kali-yuga Gora delivered the living beings.

900So sings Vasudeva Ghosha, cherishing hope in his heart,
relying on the two feet of Lord Gora.103

901Again, raga Vasanta:
Gaurachandra has appeared;
in all ten directions joy has arisen. (Refrain.)

902In beauty [He] surpasses millions of Madanas;
He laughs, hearing His own kirtana.

903His face and eyes are exceedingly sweet;
all the signs of a great king are seen.

904On His holy feet shine [the marks of] the flag and the thunderbolt;
all His limbs captivate the minds of the world.

905All misfortunes have gone far away;
all riches have become manifest.

906Acknowledging Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda [as his Lords],
Vrindavana Dasa sings [Their] qualities.

907Again, raga Vasanta:
At an auspicious moment of the full moon of Phalguna,
having given birth to a son, Shachi gazes at the son.

908Moment by moment so many [feelings] rise in [her] heart;
taking [Him] for golden fresh butter, she does not dare to touch [Him].

909With how much care she takes [Him] onto her lap!
[She] tells the excellent Mishra of the son's birth.

910Jagannatha, the crest-jewel of brahmanas,
hearing of the son's birth, floats in an ocean of happiness.

911With what longing he hurries [there]!
Beholding the moon-like face, he cannot contain himself.

912Gathering his dear ones,
he performs auspicious rites for the welfare of the son.

913On all sides are cries of "Victory, victory!";
all say, "Blessed, blessed are the father and mother!"

914In everyone's heart happiness grows;
the Suradhuni and the Earth forget all sorrows.

915All ten directions have become bright;
beasts, birds, trees and creepers — all have blossomed with joy.

916What more can Narahari say?
With the rising of Gaurachandra, suffering and darkness have gone.

917Again, raga Dhanashri:104
The full moon of Phalguna, the very limit of auspiciousness: the Moon of Gokula has appeared.
In the town of Nadia, in house after house, an ocean of bliss surges.

918What merriment among everyone together!
Shachi-devi joyfully, holding her son on her lap, abides in the birth chamber. (Refrain.)

919To see the child they run from all four sides; no one can keep composure; in the darkness of the eclipse, who recognizes whom? — [such is] the movement of countless people.

920Seeing the child's sweetness to their eyes' fill, [people] forget their own bodies.
Narahari says: what new love the son of Shachi reveals!

921Again, raga Kamoda:
In the supremely auspicious womb of Shachi abides Gaura, the Lord of Gokula;
the gods again and again offer praises and obeisances; the house fills with joy.

922A lovely night of the full moon of Phalguna; as the moon rose, Rahu swallowed [it].
At such a time the Lord appeared, having first made His name manifest.105

923Cries of "Victory, victory!" fill the world; no one keeps composure;
entering Mishra's house and seeing the infant, [all] become as if mad.

924They perform various auspicious rites, ever new; all desires are fulfilled.
Narahari says: the weight of pride of mighty Kali is smashed to pieces.

925Again, raga Vasanta: "Victory, victory, victory!" — an auspicious clamor; the night of the full moon of Phalguna is newly beautiful; from the womb of Shachi Gaura has appeared, the delight of Vraja. The fine little body of the child shines — like kunkuma, like steady lightning; the sweet moon of His face gleams, shattering all composure.

926Seeing the Lord's appearance, the gods in the sky with [their] hosts again and again shower [Him] with garlands of flowers; [their] limbs are filled with abundant thrills of ecstasy. In their hearts they form so many wishes; stirred, they tell of the lovely deeds; their eyes brim with tears — how many [wondrous] sights they obtain in great delight!

927Skillfully the kinnaras sing, softly sounds the mridanga: "dha dhiki dhiki ta dhik dhik dhikata taka dhinnana." Hosts of celestial dancing girls dance, performing abhinaya in many ways: "ughata tata ka thai thai thai, ti ai ai a tennana."106

928Pure and bright are the ten directions, gently blows the Malaya breeze; flocks of cuckoos [call] "kuhu" — so full of rasa has spring, the king of seasons, become. The waters of the river of the gods surge, joy spreads over the land of Nadia; from the merriment in Mishra's house Narahari's heart is enraptured.

929Again, raga Vasanta:
Today is the full moon; at the evening hour Rahu swallowed the moon.
Then Gaurachandra rose, destroying suffering and darkness.

930The hearts of all the devotees blossomed; no one keeps composure.
Near the Lord of Sita [the devotees] move about, utterly maddened.

931Again and again Advaita, supremely composed, roars;
He rejoices with His dear [associates] during the eclipse on the bank of the Suradhuni.

932An auspicious clamor filled the whole town of Nadia;
in the merriment no one noticed how the night passed.

933Fair and auspicious is the beauty of Mishra's house; wealth and happiness increase;
many people come — and who goes away, leaving the house?

934All the instruments sound softly; the musicians are drunk with joy;
the singers, skilled in song, sing in so many ways.

935How many dancers dance, calling out "tatta thai tathai";
the bards proclaim the spotless glory, unfolding all the grace [of their art].

936Mishra, gladdening the hearts of the supplicants, gives fitting gifts;
the incomparable waves of fresh butter Ghanashyama beholds.107

937Again, raga Vasanta, Todi:108
At what an auspicious moment is the birth of Gorachand — the stealer of the world's minds, the Lord of Gokula!
Seeing her son's face, how much happiness Shachi feels — can another tell of it?

938The women of the town of Nadia come in rows, carrying trays full of many gifts. The wives of the gods, beautifully adorned, mingling with the humans, gaze at the child and cannot be still.

939Sri Sita-devi, coming and entering the birth chamber, sees the infant, and her heart rejoices. Together with Malini and others [she] is immersed in various delights and performs so many auspicious rites.109

940And how many cowherd women, hundreds upon hundreds of cowherd men come in lovely attire, bringing yogurt. All, their hearts overwhelmed, by [their] former nature scatter yogurt in the middle of the courtyard.110

941Clapping their hands, laughing, they dance finely; seeing this, the gods, taking the guise of cowherds, dance in the courtyard — who does not dance there? — ceaselessly crying "Victory, victory!"

942So the instruments resound that there is no merriment [anywhere] like it; in Mishra's house is the very custom of Nanda's house. What can Narahari say? At the festival of the Lord's birth, in their jubilation no one remembers anything.

943O Srinivasa, what shall I say of the birth?
Here Nilambara Chakravarti calculates the lagna.111

944Here on the eighth day eight [kinds of] beans are distributed;
countless children filled this courtyard.112

945Here the gods see the Lord's pastimes;
in various merriments a month was completed.

946Here, as Vishvambhara rose and lay down,
mother and father see various marks on [His] holy feet.113

947Here at the child's utthana festival the women
perform auspicious rites — that is a wondrous tale.

948Here Vishvambhara, on the pretext of crying,
suddenly makes everyone say "Haribol."

949What shall I say of the wondrous manifestations of [His] childhood mood?
Vishvambhara reached the age of four months.

950In this house Ai, having laid Vishvambhara down,
went off somewhere, leaving the child alone.

951No one understands the child's wondrous doings:
[He] spoils various provisions in the house.

952Coming back, [she] sees her son lying in bed.
"Who did this?" she thinks to herself.

953Here at six months, at the time of the annaprashana,
the name-giving took place — with exceeding merriment.114

954The names Sri Nimai and Vishvambhara — by popular custom;
then [His] name became widely known in the world.

955The rites of the annaprashana of which people sing
were all performed in Nadia with great bliss.

956In a song — raga Kamoda:
The men and women of Nadia, regarding [it] as the fruit of their pious deeds and greatly delighted at heart,
all come to Nimai's annaprashana, bringing various gifts.

957The beauty of Shachi's son [all] behold to their eyes' fill — on the lap of the fortunate Nilambara. [He] is all in new and ever new ornaments; on His hips a silk dhoti, its end swaying.

958His little body surpasses a golden lotus; and for His face — what comparison? [What is] the splendor of the moon! How wondrously, as [He] takes grains of sweet rice, [He] lights up with a gentle smile!

959At such jubilation who can keep composure? To tell of the merriment, words do not come to the lips. All praise Shachi and Jagannatha; Narahari's heart overflows with happiness.

960What shall I say? Shachi-devi, staying here,
obtained bliss from the honor of all the people.

961Here Ai, in great happiness, having laid her son down,
having prepared kajal, applies [it] to His eyes to refresh [them].

962Here Ai sits, with the women all around;
taking Nimai onto her lap, she suckles [Him].

963Here Ai, to lull Nimaichand to sleep,
sings in the sweetest voice whatever comes to her mind.

964O Srinivasa, here Shachi Thakurani
fondled the child so much — I do not know how to tell it.

965In this courtyard the Lord crawled on His knees;
that wondrous beauty the wise describe with joy.

966As [it is said] in a song:
How can I tell with one mouth the pastimes of Gorachand?
Nimbly crawling on all fours, in many playful ways, goes the child of Shachi.

967Drool trickles — the face is so lovely to see;
the charming red lips surpass a ripe bimba fruit.

968Angada and valaya bracelets adorn the two lovely arms;
on the feet are magara kharu anklets, at the neck a tiger's claw.115

969A golden chain on the head, a silken tassel;
Vasudeva Ghosha says: I offer myself up [for Him].116

970Again, raga Todi:117
Jagannatha Mishra, in great happiness,
taking his son onto his lap, kisses [His] moon-like face.

971He arranges ornaments in the hair on His head;
running [his] fingers [through it], he feels affection well up in his heart.

972Nimai, from His father's lap,
nimbly gets down to roam about the courtyard.

973He crawls about the courtyard;
golden anklets jingle on His lovely feet.

974As He goes, He looks back;
Mishra, standing, watches the sweetness of His movements.

975Coming in front of Him, His mother says,
"Come up into my arms, my child — dust is getting on Your body."118

976Putting His hand in His mother's hand,
He climbs onto her lap — gently, smiling, smiling.

977The gleam of His teeth, like drops of milk,
shows when He smiles — who then could keep his composure?

978Whomever He looks at with His two eyes,
He sets afloat forever in an ocean of happiness.

979He looks beautiful on His mother's lap;
Narahari offers himself for the One who enchants the minds of the world.119

980Here Ai, taking her son on her lap, asks,
"Eyes, nose, mouth — which is which? Tell me, Nimai."

981Hearing His mother's words, He is filled with great joy
and points with His little finger to eyes, nose, mouth.

982Crawling on His knees, here He gave joy to a snake:
He lay down on the snake's coils.

983Seeing this, all cried out in fear, "Alas, alas!"
For this reason Ananta-deva comes along this path.120

984Here Vishvarupa, taking Vishvambhara on his lap,
brushes the dust off His body, saying I know not what.121

985Crawling on His knees, He displays all sorts of play,
takes away everyone's sorrow — the beauty is beyond words.

986O Srinivasa, when He [began] to walk on His holy feet,
there was supreme delight in this wondrous courtyard.

987At the touch of His lovely feet the earth's pain is destroyed;
by the rays of His body He draws all hearts.

988Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
Then, in time, He of immeasurable splendor, wandering on His reddish feet,
removed the earth's suffering born of separation.

989Who knows the secret of this spot in the courtyard?
Here He began to walk on His feet.

990Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Todi):
Shachi Thakurani, in a lovely way,
teaches Gorachand to walk.

991Softly, softly, smiling, she says,
"Come here, hold my finger."

992Hearing this, the Moon of Nadia happily,
smiling, takes hold of His mother's finger.

993Slowly, slowly He gets up and stands
and walks two or four steps.

994Letting go of the finger, He falls to the ground;
Shachi, taking [Him] on her lap, kisses His face.

995Climbing onto her lap, He swings His feet;
the anklets jingle on His reddish feet.

996Kneading with His little fingers, He drinks at the breast —
there is no comparison one could give for it.

997He looks playfully in all four directions;
for this Narahari offers himself.

998By His own will Vishvambhara grows day by day;
in supreme delight He wanders alone in this courtyard.

999The women who live in Navadvipa, in great bliss,
come here at dawn and gaze at Gaurachandra.

1000Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Vibhasha):
What a turn of mind in the most virtuous
women of Nadia, devoted to their husbands!
They have no thought for their own sons —
ceaselessly they speak of the deeds of Shachi's son.

1001Seeing that the night is ending, leaving their beds,
they cannot keep patience even for a moment;
filling platters with all kinds of things, row upon row,
they carry [them] to give to the Moon of Nadia.

1002As they enter Shachi's house, in their hearts
whole oceans of delight well up.
They all see: on His mother's lap
Gora, the Moon of Gokula, sits and plays.

1003A delight to the eyes and the life of the women:
getting [Him], taking [Him] on their laps, they forget their bodies.
Narahari says: Ah, I die, I die!
Who created such love?

1004Here was Nimai's wondrous dancing:
clapping their hands, the women make Him dance.

1005Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Todi):
"Dance, my child Vishvambhara!
I will give You a handful to eat of thickened milk, fresh butter and cream."

1006The devoted wives, all around,
say so much to Nimaichand in soft voices.

1007Saying, "Say, say: Hari, Hari!"
they all clap their hands together, again and again.

1008Looking at His mother, Gora,
saying "Hari bol," dances in various styles.

1009What a gentle smile on His moon-face!
It enchants the world, pouring out nectar in heaps upon heaps.

1010Lovely are the glances of His eyes;
seeing the graceful movements of His arms, who could stay steady?

1011What sweet, sweet radiance!
The courtyard flashes with the rays of His golden body.

1012The kinkini bells and anklets jingle beautifully;
Narahari offers himself for the rhythm of His soles.

1013Here the mother, overwhelmed with maternal love,
says so much, gazing at Nimaichand's face.

1014Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Dhanashri):122
Ah, my golden Nimai!
Do not leave Your own home to go to someone else's —
sit and play here, in this spot. (Refrain.)

1015The children will come to play with You —
keep them all right here.
Whatever You want, whenever You want it, I will bring and give;
what is lacking in my house?

1016If anyone says anything [to You], show him [Your] fear,
pleading Your father's prohibition.
If You go out of the house with the restless boys,
can a mother hold her heart steady?

1017If You are out of my sight even for a moment, life will not stay in my body;
Narahari knows my grief.
Heed Your mother's words, sit at home and play,
so that I may always see [Your] moon-face.

1018Here Vishvambhara smears His body with dust;
seeing it, His mother, laughing, cries, "Oh dear, oh dear!"

1019Here, in order to tell His mother something,
He gave up sandesha and the like and ate earth.123

1020One day in this house Shachi, the Mother of the world,
to lull her son to sleep, tells stories from the Puranas.

1021At every phrase [of hers] Vishvambhara lets out a hunkara;
in supreme joy the mother tells on and on:

1022"O my child Vishvambhara! Krishna in Mathura
went to Kamsa's assembly to kill Kamsa.

1023Soon, having fought the demon Kamsa in wrestling,
He threw Kamsa down from the dais to the ground and killed him."

1024Hearing this, the Lord, in a fit of anger, says again and again,
"Whoever else is left — him I will destroy!"

1025Another day the Lord, lying in this house,
in a dream addresses the gods — Shiva, Brahma and the others:

1026"O Shiva, Brahma! Do not be anxious in your minds:
delivering the living beings, I will make [them] mad with sankirtana."

1027Thus Vishvambhara speaks various words in His dream;
hearing [this], His mother, her heart alarmed, goes "thu-thu."124

1028O Srinivasa, what play Vishvambhara displays in His childhood mood —
I do not know how to tell any of it.

1029Ai was in this house with Vishvambhara;
suddenly a great crowd gathered at this spot.

1030Seeing the gods — the Four-faced, the Five-faced and others —
Mother Shachi was filled with fear.

1031Jagannatha Mishra was lying in this house;
she sent her son to his father.

1032Suddenly they hear the sound of anklets;
astonished, the father and mother say so much to each other.

1033At daybreak the father and mother, apprehensive,
performed the auspicious rites that are prescribed.

1034Here Vishvambhara dances among the children;
seeing that beauty, [people] say so much to one another.

1035Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
What is this I have seen — a golden doll!
In Shachi's courtyard He dances, grey with dust.

1036All around Him naked boys have gathered;
in their midst Gora dances, saying, "Hari, Hari."

1037On radiant lotus feet the jewel of the twice-born runs about;
His mother listens with delight to the sound of His anklets.

1038Vasudeva Ghosha, who knows the rasa of childhood, says:
blessed are the people of Nadia, rich is Navadvipa!125

1039O Srinivasa, in this courtyard Vishvambhara
dances with all kinds of play — that delight is enchanting.

1040Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Vibhasha):
In Shachi's courtyard Vishvambhara Raya dances;
laughing, laughing, turning, turning, He hides from His mother.

1041Covering His face with a cloth, He says, "I've hidden!"
Shachi says, "Vishvambhara! I can't see [You]!"

1042Holding the end of His mother's cloth, on restless feet,
dancing, dancing, He goes with the gait of a wagtail.

1043Vasudeva Ghosha says: matchless beauty!
Seeing this child form, the mind of the world is filled with longing.

1044Again, raga Bhatiyali:126
Gora dances, Shachi's darling child.
All around, the boys have gathered and clap their hands,
saying, "Hari bol, Hari bol." (Refrain.)

1045A bright cap on His head, a golden necklace at His throat;127
His mother has fondly dressed [Him] in a little dhara, tied tight.

1046Beautiful curling hair, a shapely body,
attire that enchants the world, eyebrows — the bow of Kama.

1047Many ornaments of silver and gold adorn His body charmingly.
His two feet are red lotuses; when He lifts [them], the anklets jingle.

1048In Shachi's courtyard He dances without pause,
babbling half-formed words.
Vasudeva Ghosha says: take [Him], take [Him], hold [Him] on your lap —
Gora is like the life of [our] life.

1049Again, raga Kamoda:
Playfully Shachi's child dances,
lighting up the world with His beauty.

1050His body surpasses a golden lotus;
grey with dust — as if [covered] with pollen.

1051His dress and ornaments shine beautifully;
saying "Hari," He claps His hands.

1052He smiles gently in a sweet manner —
who then could keep his composure?

1053With what playfulness He looks in all directions!
His mother fills His hand with cream.

1054Striking poses, He whirls again and again;
the end of His dhoti trails on the ground.

1055The bells at His waist — a lovely radiance,
and from them a cascade of jingling: "jhinini."

1056The anklets ring on His feet: "jhanunnu";
Narahari offers himself for Him.128

1057What shall I say? Here the son of Shachi,
holding the end of His mother's cloth, goes about everywhere.

1058The Lord goes outside the house to play;
places pure and impure — He roams everywhere.

1059Standing here, Shachi Ai says,
"Do not go to impure places, foolish Nimai."

1060What Vishvambhara replied to His mother's words —
on merely hearing it, the heart was filled with wonder.

1061In play He plays at monkeys here on the bank of the Ganga;
standing here, His mother calls [Him] loudly.

1062Coming unseen, He slipped into this house
and in anger scatters all sorts of things.

1063Taking Nimai on her lap here, Shachi-devi
says much to Him; Nimai does not heed her words.

1064Getting down from her lap, the Lord runs away;
with a stick in hand Ai runs after Him.

1065People on all sides watch and say again and again,
"Sri Shachi behaves just like Yashoda."

1066Here, making a seat of discarded clay pots,
Vishvambhara sits, with smudges of soot all over His body.129

1067His mother says, "You do not know pure from impure.
Go quickly and bathe; heed my words."

1068Hearing this, He says much in anger, delighted within,
and, taking up a brick, threatens His mother.

1069Here Ai lay in a swoon among the women;
then Nimai brought a coconut.

1070Here He plays with a puppy
and keeps it on the raised step of this house.

1071By a ruse Ai let that puppy go;
here Nimai, weeping, scolds His mother.

1072How Shachi-devi, the Mother of the world, here
consoles the child — who knows that?

1073Here Ai, arranging various offerings,
goes to the foot of the banyan tree to worship Shashthi.130

1074Here Vishvambhara was absorbed in play;
heedless of prohibition, He eats the articles for Shashthi's puja.

1075Here Ai, touching the feet of the elderly women,
begs each one of them for Nimai's welfare.

1076Here the women, taking Nimai on their laps,
teach Him so many things that I cannot tell them.131

1077O Srinivasa, Vishvambhara acts as He wills;
how much mercy He showed to two thieves cannot be told.

1078Seeing many ornaments on Vishvambhara's body,
two men here plotted to take them.

1079Him who bewilders the world they beguiled and carried off;
the thieves, bewildered, wandered about Nadia.132

1080Here, carefully setting [Him] down from their shoulders,
the thieves ran away — this sport went unnoticed by anyone.

1081Nimaisundara is the crest-jewel of the restless;
whatever He does at any time — how could I tell it?

1082Going into anyone's house, He makes the children cry
and smashes all the pots of yogurt and milk.

1083Here they come joyfully with their complaints,
as the gopis in Vraja spoke to Yashoda.

1084O Srinivasa! In this town of Nadia,
in Mishra's house, the service of guests was beyond all measure.

1085Be it a brahmana or a sannyasi, or whoever it might be,
he received all with honour, with great joy in his heart.

1086One day there came a certain tairthika brahmana133 —
of divine radiance, pure in conduct, the best of all.

1087His learning in all the shastras no one could fathom;
his worship was the six-syllable mantra of Sri Gopala.

1088The ornament at his neck was Sri Bala-gopala, a shalagrama;134
with his lips he ceaselessly chanted the name of Krishna.

1089Seeing him, Mishra, with great joy in his heart,
gave him lodging in this house according to due custom.

1090Here the brahmana suddenly saw Vishvambhara:
"Whose boy is this?" — and he cannot turn his eyes away.

1091"I have never seen such a boy anywhere," —
growing agitated, the brahmana says to himself.

1092Looking at the brahmana, the Lord smiled slightly
and went outside the house to play with the children.

1093The brahmana, very composed, says nothing to anyone;
seeing Mishra's efforts, he rejoices in his heart.

1094With great care Mishra had the brahmana cook;
the cooking was finished when evening had almost passed.

1095To offer the bhoga to Krishna, the best of brahmanas sat down in meditation;
there came the beautiful Vishvambhara, the Knower of hearts.

1096Laughing with great joy, He eats a mouthful of rice;
seeing this, the fortunate brahmana cries, "Alas, alas!"135

1097Mishra, in great anger, wants to beat his son;
saying much, the brahmana held back Mishra's hands.

1098At Mishra's word he cooked again;
and again Vishvambhara ate in the same way.

1099Again, at the humble entreaty of Vishvarupa,136 the best of brahmanas
cooked once more; once more Vishvambhara eats in the same way.

1100The Lord, affectionate to His devotees, having eaten three times,
at the end showed such grace as is impossible to tell.

1101By the Lord's will much of the night went by;
all who were here fell asleep.

1102The merciful Vishvambhara, who enchants the worlds,
speaks many sweet words to the brahmana.

1103The Lord, who submits to His devotees, here in this kitchen
showed a wonder: the brahmana beholds Vishvambhara.

1104Eight-armed: in four [hands] the conch, the disc and the rest;
with two He eats butter, with two He plays the flute.

1105Beautiful in every limb, adorned with jewelled ornaments,
with the play of His eyes He enchants the world.

1106The brahmana sees the bank of the Yamuna, Vrindavana,
and all around shine the cows, the cowherds and the gopis.

1107Seeing this, the brahmana fell to the ground in bliss
and washed the Lord's lotus feet with his tears.

1108The ocean of mercy, the Lord, the son of Shachi,
revealing [to him] His pastimes in Nadia, embraced [him].

1109He forbade him to disclose all this to others;
when the Lord made Himself manifest, all this too became manifest.

1110Remaining in Nadia in a hidden form, the brahmana
beholds the Lord's pastimes, on which Brahma and the others meditate.

1111Here one day the son of Mishra
wept so that hearts were torn apart.

1112Jagadisha and Hiranya,137 on the holy day of Ekadashi,
had carefully prepared various foods for Vishnu.

1113That very food Vishvambhara wanted to eat first;
the brahmanas Jagadisha and Hiranya heard of it.

1114Before it had become Vishnu's offering, they brought it and gave [it to Him];
eating it here, He stopped crying.

1115Over there is the house of Jagadisha and Hiranya;
they had great affection for Jagannatha Mishra.

1116What shall I say of Nimai's incomparable childhood doings!
Whatever He wanted at any moment — if it was not given, there was trouble.

1117Standing here, Nimai gazes at the sky
and says to Mother Shachi, "Catch the moon and give it to me."

1118Seeing a bird fly, here the son of Shachi
weeps, saying, "Catch it and give it to me."

1119All the girls together, coming here,
tell Mother Shachi of Nimai's mischief.

1120Right here the pious brahmanas come
and tell Mishra of Nimaichand's mischief.

1121Standing here, Ai says to Vishvambhara,
"Go quickly and call Vishvarupa."

1122Vishvarupa is in Sri Advaita's assembly;
[Vishvambhara] says to him, "Come and eat; Mother is calling."

1123Holding the end of His elder brother's cloth, Vishvambhara,
enchanting the hearts of all, came home.

1124At that very moment I cleaned the place and made it ready;138
here the two brothers sat down to eat.

1125O dear Srinivasa, what more is there to say?
When I think of all that, my heart breaks.

1126Here Shachi and Mishra reason with their son:
"What you did, dear child, is not proper.

1127Sri Murari Gupta is like a rishi in Nadia;
everyone respects him in every way.

1128At mealtime you passed water onto his plate —
who in the world would not censure this?

1129He is wise, and so he did not hold it against you;
never do such a thing anywhere again."

1130When the time came to begin His studies, Sri Mishra here,
at a most auspicious moment, placed chalk in his son's hand.139

1131Writing "ka, kha, ga, gha," he says, "Write, dear child."
Kneeling, He writes — seeing that, all sorrow vanishes.

1132Looking [at the letters], Nimaichand says "ka, kha, ga, gha";140
hearing this, Mishra's heart overflows with bliss.

1133The Lord, in His pauganda age, is absorbed in the taste of learning;
when He is not allowed to write, He shows restlessness.

1134Whatever He writes grows day by day;
here everyone praises Vishvambhara.

1135Here Jagannatha Mishra, his heart full of great joy,
set about teaching Vishvambhara.

1136Opening a book, he gave [Him] lessons here;
Vishvambhara became absorbed in study.

1137Standing right here, Vishvambhara-raya
tells Mother Shachi to observe Ekadashi.

1138Gladdened by her son's words, with care
she keeps the vow of Sri Ekadashi above all else.

1139Here Jagannatha Mishra, in great joy,
thinks of giving Vishvarupa in marriage.

1140Vishvarupa, having judged everything to be impermanent,
accepted sannyasa for the sake of Krishna.

1141He became known by the name Sri Shankararanya;
he goes on pilgrimage to the tirthas, as the ancient custom is.141

1142Vishvarupa is a portion of Sri Baladeva;
sixteen years of age, of surpassing beauty.

1143Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the first prakrama:
"Having said this, the physician began [to tell] the delightful, auspicious,
purifying narrative of Vishvarupa, a portion of Baladeva.142

1144The glorious Sri Vishvarupa, a treasury of all virtues, sixteen years old, utterly pure, attained the position of an acharya; his mind was attached to hearing about the Self and reflecting [on Him]; he was devoted in prema; all-knowing, his heart ever attached to the feet of Narahari, joyful, peaceful, full of contentment, without attachment to the world, a knower of the Vedas, a knower of rasa."143

1145Here Vishvambhara weeps and rolls in the dust,
His heart utterly distraught at separation from His elder brother.

1146Here Shachi and Jagannatha Mishra both weep;
at the weeping of the two no one can keep calm.

1147"Where is Vishvarupa?" — crying out, they call again and again;
who among the people of Nadia does not weep, [remembering] his virtues?

1148Mishra's house was filled with weeping;
when one thinks of all that, one's life burns with grief.

1149Here everyone consoles Shachi and Jagannatha;
by Vishvambhara's will they grew calm.

1150One day here [He] says to His father and mother,
"In Vishvarupa's sannyasa there is great good.

1151He will deliver his father's family and his mother's family,
and I shall serve you both."

1152Hearing their son's words, both became very joyful;
taking [Him] on their lap, they kissed the moon of His face.

1153O Srinivasa, after Vishvarupa's sannyasa
[His] restlessness fades little by little, day by day.

1154Here Mishra Purandara says to Shachi,
"Vishvambhara has reached the age for the chuda-karma."144

1155Saying this, the two of them, by the procedure prescribed in the Vedas,
performed their son's chuda-karma right here.

1156In a song (raga Dhanashri):
How full of joy today, with a great throng of people,
is Shachi's radiant house!
The solace of everyone's life — Nimaichand's chuda rite —
at what a wondrous auspicious moment!

1157Adorning Vishvambhara with divine garments and ornaments,
seating Him on a divine seat,
whatever the Vedas prescribe and whatever the custom of the people —
all this Mishra carries out with care.

1158The noble barber came and does his work,
to put a yellow thread at the base of the ear.
The women cry "jaya" — who does not raise shouts of victory?
Auspiciousness spread over the earth.

1159The brahmanas recite the Vedas, the bards compose verses [about Him],
the musicians play many kinds of instruments.
All the dancers dance — how much can Narahari tell? —
the singers sing [His] spotless fame.

1160The Lord is full of consciousness and bliss, His play is like that of people:
before the ear had been pierced, [the barber] saw a hole in it.

1161Seeing this, the barber was amazed in his mind;
by the Lord's will he says nothing to anyone.

1162All that Sri Jiva examined in the Sandarbhas —
Narahari, having received permission, rejoiced in it.145

1163Again, raga Velavali:146
Today is Gaurachandra's incomparable chuda, auspicious as the Vedas enjoin;
crowds of people in the house.
The wives of Sri Navadvipa, by matchless custom, give forth "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu" —
what joy to the ear!147

1164The assembly of brahmanas, gods on earth, shines; in many modes the sound of the Vedas,
most sweet, fills hearts with delight.
Sutas, magadhas and bandis compose new tales of [His] deeds;
reaching the ear, they steal the heart of the world.148

1165The players of mridanga and other instruments utter in various ways: "dha dha dhilanga
dhiki taka dhinnina."
The skilled sing in fine metre; the dancers dance, calling out:
"tatta thai thai ti ai tinnina."149

1166Covered with thrills of rapture, full of zeal, the best of Mishras, distributing
many goods, satisfies all the supplicants.
What can Narahari say of the boundless splendour! Beholding [it],
the gods, absorbed [in bliss], in the sky loudly and ceaselessly proclaim, "Jaya, jaya!"

1167Look, Srinivasa: here, outside the house,
surrounded by His companions, Nimai plays.

1168On that road the women, overwhelmed,
stand and gaze at Nimaichand's beauty.

1169One day here the venerable Mishra
shows boundless parental love to Vishvambhara.

1170After some days, here Jagannatha Mishra
thinks in his mind, "I shall give my son the sacred thread."150

1171Gathering his kinsmen and friends, he fixed the day;
Mishra's house was filled with great joy.

1172At the time of the sacred thread the festivities have no end;
the fortunate describe it in many ways.

1173As [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
What joy in the town of Nadia!
The son of Sri Shachi-devi will put on the sacred thread —
this news is in every house.

1174Overwhelmed with love, who does not run
with all kinds of gifts to Mishra's home?
Mishra's home is incomparable, the throng of people boundless —
who is not lost in that splendour?

1175Mishra, in great joy, performs the rites according to the Vedas
and gives the sacred thread to Gorachand.
Gaura's form is enchanting, He is clad in red cloth,
a divine staff in His hand, a bag on His shoulder.

1176The Lord playfully begs alms; seeing this, the wives of the gods all together
mingle with humans to give alms.
Those who are dear to the Lord — with what delight
they give alms into the Lord's bag!

1177All the auspicious rites — who can tell how many?
And what victorious cries of the women!
The brahmanas sound the Vedas — hearing it, who can keep his composure?
The bards recite the praises of the forefathers.151

1178Cries of "Jaya, jaya!" filled all the directions;
dance, song and music of every kind.
Narahari Dasa says: the supplicants, [receiving] fitting gifts,
intoxicated with happiness, sing [His] good fame.

1179Again, raga Dhanashri:
In the house of Jagannatha Mishra
music sounds in the auspicious rite.

1180The women raise cries of victory,
the bards recite the praises of the forefathers.

1181At an auspicious moment the son of Shachi
puts on the sacred thread. (Refrain.)

1182With what can this sacred thread be compared?
It is Ananta Himself in subtle form.152

1183The sweetness of the shaven head —
whose heart does it not steal?

1184Red cloth is His fine garment;
with His beauty He lights up the ten directions.

1185On all four sides is the assembly of brahmanas,
and in their midst Gora, king of the twice-born.

1186A divine staff in His hand, a bag on His shoulder;
seeing this, who can keep his composure?

1187[His] attire shines — [He is] in the mood of Vamana;
with His grace He enchants the minds of the world.153

1188Smiling gently, speaking most sweetly,
He begs alms from the devotees.

1189All wish to give Him their life as alms;
whatever they give, their heart is not content with it.

1190The wives of the gods, mingling with humans,
give alms, gazing at the moon of His face.

1191Who does not offer up his life [for Him]?
Everyone raises cries of victory.

1192Ghanashyama says: in Mishra's home
the ocean of happiness surges.

1193Again, raga Suhai:
Gaurasundara at a supremely auspicious moment put on the sacred thread;
Shachi and Mishra, skilled in the rites the Vedas prescribe, [did all] by incomparable custom.

1194Various auspicious rites take place; the wives of the clan give forth "ulu-lu-lu-lu-lu-lu." The bards sing [His] good fame, drinking in the auspicious beauty with their full gaze.

1195The skilled sing in new talas and play the murajas and other drums resoundingly;
the dancers dance, calling out thickly, "dha dhi dhikata dhilanga."

1196The minds of the gods are deeply absorbed, beholding the charming play; filling the world ring cries of "Jaya, jaya, jaya!"; Narahari Dasa offers himself up [for Him].

1197O Srinivasa, here Vishvambhara-raya
longed with all His heart to study.

1198Understanding his son's wish, Mishra Purandara
took [Him] to the house of Gangadasa Pandita.

1199He entrusted his son to Gangadasa;
Gangadasa carefully teaches [Him] grammar.

1200Day by day [He] became wonderful in grammar;
seeing this, who in Nadia does not praise Him?

1201One day here Lord Gaurachandra,
having eaten tambula, smiles softly.

1202Suddenly, right here, He fell into a swoon;
His mother and father carefully brought Him back to consciousness.

1203Having come to Himself, the Lord comforted His mother and father
and spoke much about Vishvarupa and other things.

1204In this house Jagannatha Mishra Purandara
sees in a dream that Vishvambhara has taken sannyasa.

1205Waking in the morning, distraught,
he prays much, calling on the gods.

1206At daybreak he says to Sri Shachi-devi,
"It seems my Nimai will not stay at home."

1207Here Shachi Ai says to Jagannatha Mishra,
"Nimai will stay at home; there is nothing to worry about.

1208Apart from study nothing pleases Nimai;
He will be fit to serve His mother and father."

1209Mother Shachi spoke [to him] in many ways,
yet he cannot forget the terrible dream.

1210One day, sitting here, Mishra Purandara
says within himself, "My son will leave home."

1211Saying this, he, losing his composure, heaves long sighs;
suddenly a fever appeared in his body.

1212What shall I say of how Mishra's disappearance came about?
The heart breaks when one remembers all that.

1213Here, fallen on the ground, Shachi and Shachi's son
weep so that they make [the whole] world weep.

1214By the Lord's will the residents of Navadvipa
calmed the two of them, and all [themselves] grew calm.

1215O dear Srinivasa, here Vishvambhara
consoled His mother, speaking very sweet words.

1216What can I say of the kind of love the mother had!
Apart from Vishvambhara she knows nothing else.

1217Who can understand the heart of Gaurachandra?
He performs pastimes beyond the reach of Brahma and the others.

1218One day Nimai, as He was going to bathe in the Ganga,
asked His mother for flower garlands and other things.

1219Over a slight delay He fell into a great rage
and spoiled everything there was in the house.154

1220At last He lay down in this courtyard;
the Lord, the son of Shachi, fell asleep.

1221After a while, knowing that He had woken,
[the mother] brushed the dust from His body and raised her son.

1222Having made ready the flower garlands and other things, she gave them to her son;
having bathed in the Ganga, Gaurahari joyfully came back.

1223One day here Shachi says to her son,
"Today there is no food at all in the house."

1224Hearing His mother's words, the Lord with a joyful heart
brought two tolas of gold and gave [them to her] here, in private.155

1225Seeing the gold, Mother Shachi grew anxious at heart:
she cannot understand this play of her son at all.

1226One day Mother Shachi, sitting here,
ponders in her mind on getting her son married.

1227The age of pauganda has ended, kaishora is beginning;
moment by moment [His] beauty grows — boundlessly, ever more wondrous.

1228Who, seeing Nimaichand, can remain composed?
What His wondrous doings are, no one else knows.

1229To increase His mother's supreme joy,
the Lord came to wish to marry.

1230Here, reflecting on the shastras, the son of Shachi
went along that path to the bank of the Ganga.

1231The Lord's beloved, Lakshmi-devi, came to bathe in the Ganga.
How they saw each other — [so] the wise describe it:

1232Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
The daughter of Vallabha, virtuous Lakshmi,
surrounded by her friends,
goes to the bank of the Ganga to bathe,
glancing timidly on every side.156

1233Seeing Gaurangachand a little way off,
[she feels] a hidden love well up;
drinking the nectar of the sweetness of that beauty,
she cannot keep her composure.

1234Gora, the jewel of virtues, recognizing His beloved,
looks at Lakshmi.
Lakshmi's body, surpassing pure gold,
enters, as it were, into the very depth of [His] heart.

1235The two skilfully meet with the corners of their eyes,
and others cannot know of it.
The Lord of Narahari, smiling softly,
went home in joy.157

1236Here, sitting, the son of Sri Shachi
said to me, "What is in your mind will come to be."

1237One day here Vanamali Acharya
speaks with Mother Shachi of a marriage.158

1238Lakshmi is the daughter of Vallabha Acharya; with her
the marriage was settled on another day.

1239Here the mother speaks of her son's marriage;
hearing it, the son of Sri Shachi applies Himself to the task.

1240All that was needed for the wedding was quickly prepared;
the wedding day was fixed, at an auspicious hour.

1241Talk of the wedding is in every house of Navadvipa;
drawn by the Lord, no one can remain composed.

1242All the devotees of all the incarnations, in Nadia,
sport in the forms of women and men — by His will.

1243By His will no one knows himself;
all the deeds they do are according to their former nature.

1244How the women and men went here,
what this wedding was like — the wise describe it:

1245Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Dhanashri):
What joy in the town of Nadia!
Talk of Nimai's wedding is in every house.

1246Women and men of Nadia alike —
the hearts of all well up [with longing] to see the wedding.

1247The bards hurry along at a run,
thinking to themselves, "We shall get much wealth."

1248All the dancers, musicians and the rest
rush to and fro, cherishing so many hopes.

1249The astrologers hurry along at a run:
"We shall find a wondrous auspicious moment and have the wedding performed."

1250The garland-makers go joyfully
with garlands of many flowers to the home of Sri Shachi.

1251Who with one mouth could tell how many [they are]?
The poor and the beggars go by the hundreds.

1252In Narahari's heart is this hope:
"Shall I see the wedding festivities to my eyes' content?"

1253Again (raga Dhanashri):
All the young new brides of Nadia
say in private, smiling sweetly,
"How blessed we are — we shall see such
a wedding, floating in that ocean of joy!"

1254One says, "Vallabha Acharya is noble,
his wife devoted to her husband and of good conduct.
So it seems to me: by former merit
they will obtain this son-in-law, so very hard to obtain."

1255Another says, "Blessed is Vallabha's daughter,
Lakshmi, a beauty, like [the goddess] Lakshmi.
What [other] fortunate girl is there such as she,
who will obtain a husband surpassing Madana?"

1256Yet another says, "Wonderful! The matchmaker was
Vanamali — how much joy he has found!"
"Today is the adhivasa — come, come, dressed in your finery!" —
so Narahari, coming, said, and went away.159

1257Again (raga Dhanashri):
"The home of Sri Shachi is full of beauty —
in it an ocean of bliss will surge.
Today is the adhivasa: adorned, there will shine
Gora, full of happiness, the moon of Gokula."

1258Saying this in their hearts, unable to stay still,
the young women of good families look about on every side.
To what can it be compared? — as if from the houses
a lovely garland of moons had come out.

1259Colourful garments, shining ornaments,
on every limb a fine array;
with many graceful movements they go in rows,
lighting up the roads of Nadia.

1260With what longing they come to Ai
and bow down — with what tenderness [Ai receives them]!
Finding the Lord of Narahari in the courtyard,
they cooled their hearts, gazing at that face.

1261Again (raga Kamoda):
In Shachi's courtyard, full of beauty,
on all sides the brahmanas chant the Vedas.

1262What bliss is revealed today!
At an auspicious hour, the adhivasa of Nimaichand. (Refrain.)

1263The intimates offer scents and garlands;
the radiance of Gora's body lights up the quarters.

1264In the midst of the assembly Gora, the jewel of the twice-born,
shines, surpassing how many hundreds of millions of Kamadevas!

1265Whoever looks even once at Gora
cannot keep composure and forgets himself.

1266Everyone who came to the adhivasa
is gladdened with gifts of scents, sandal and the rest.

1267Having performed the adhivasa according to the rules,
Vallabha Acharya went to his own home.

1268There is no end to telling of that happiness:
together with the married women, Ai performs the auspicious rites.160

1269The women raise cries of victory;
the bards recite auspicious panegyrics.

1270Dancing, singing, music of many kinds —
no one has the power to offer a comparison.

1271Who does not say, "Wonderful, wonderful!"?
The whole world is filled with the delightful sound "Jaya, jaya!"

1272Mingling with the people, the gods
watch the festivity of the adhivasa, says Narahari.

1273Again (raga Dhanashri):
Today, overcome with tenderness,
Vallabha Acharya performs the rite of adhivasa
together with the brahmanas close to him. (Refrain.)

1274With what love the mother
dresses her daughter Lakshmi in fine garments and ornaments!
In the lovely courtyard, on a splendid throne,
having seated [her], the friends float in happiness.

1275When at the auspicious hour scents and garlands are offered,
from the joy in her heart the radiance of [her] body grows.
Her heart is not still: unseen [by others], she sees
on all sides throngs of celestial women.

1276Conches, bells and the rest — music of many kinds;
dancing, singing; the bards utter blessings.
At the women's cries Narahari cannot
keep his composure — he offers himself up [for it].

1277Again (raga Kamoda):
When the night of the adhivasa had passed,
everyone performs all the duties of the wedding.

1278Surrounded by brahmanas,
Nimai performs the rites enjoined by the Vedas.

1279The crowd of people cannot be described;
there is a great clamour of voices: "Take! Give!"

1280Many instruments play without pause,
the singers sing enchantingly.

1281The bards recite panegyrics,
the women raise sweet cries of victory.

1282Everyone rejoices in the women's rites;
Narahari floats in that ocean of happiness.161

1283Again (raga Kamoda):
The young wives of good families, their hearts rejoicing,
playfully dress themselves to go and fetch the water.
Gazing and gazing at the moon of Gora's face, smiling,
they cry "ulu-ulu", the hairs of their bodies standing on end with delight.162

1284They go out from their homes — how much rises in their hearts! —
intoxicated by the fragrance of the body of the moon Gaura.
Their hearts are unsteady, they are overwhelmed with feeling;
in the corners of their eyes — so many kinds of playful glances!

1285How much they say to one another — indistinctly, under their breath;
which of them, in the way of playful beauties, does not offer herself up [for Him]?
With their garments, ornaments and attire they destroy [all] composure —
who could find a comparison for that beauty?163

1286Anklets, belts of bells, the sounds of many instruments —
how sweet it is, words cannot express.
Having finished the water rite, they enter the house;
Narahari's heart surges with happiness.

1287Again (raga Kamoda):
How wondrous! In the house of Sri Shachi
are auspicious [rites] of many kinds; amid the clamour all
go about the business of the wedding.164

1288Gora, the moon of Gokula, is adorned;
in the bath enjoined for the wedding, beyond measure
the ocean of bliss surges.

1289The young wives of good families, with charming skill,
saying, "We shall anoint [His] lovely locks with oil,"
again and again loosen them and tie them up.

1290One rubs [His] body with turmeric;
seeing [Him] dulled with turmeric, all laugh
and offer up their lives for Him.

1291One applies scents to [His] body;
the fragrance of that body steals the pride of these scents —
who could find a comparison for [that] body?165

1292[He] was bathed with Ganga water;
Narahari, taking a towel, wipes
[His] body, playfully.166

1293Again (raga Kamoda):
Today, with what joy in their hearts,
seated on their seats, the friends
dress Vishvambhara!

1294They smear [His] body with scents and sandal;
they draw a tilaka on [His] lovely forehead —
who would not be charmed by it?

1295Having bound up the curly locks beautifully,
with joy in their hearts, in a charming way,
they wind [them] round with a garland of malati flowers.

1296They put earrings in [His] ears; they flash against the slopes of [His] cheeks — the pair of cheeks steals the pride of a mirror.

1297On [His] neck they place a necklace of jewels;
on the broad chest it swings so gracefully — who can give a comparison for it?

1298On [His] arms, angada armlets; on [His] wrists, bracelets; on [His] fingers, rings; having put [them] on, they gaze at [His] face and cannot keep their composure.

1299[His] waist, surpassing [that of] a lion, is slender;
as they adorn [it] with a golden chain, [their] eyes stop blinking.

1300The arrangement of [His] attire entices the world;
having dressed [Him] in a cloth with a red border, Narahari gazes at [that] beauty.

1301Again, raga Kamoda:
Having dressed [Him], the companions
give into His hand a golden mirror like the moon.

1302Seeing Nimaichand's attire —
what to speak of others — even the gods cannot turn away their eyes.

1303Shachi Ai, with her friends,
performs so many auspicious rites, gazing at her son's face.

1304The young wives, standing at a distance,
gaze at Gorachand and cannot keep their composure.

1305The women raise the cry "ulu-ulu";167
talk of the joyful wedding filled the world.

1306Bowing at [His] mother's feet,
Gaura-raya sets out to be married.

1307The brahmanas sound the Vedas;
many instruments play, and the sound pierces the sky.

1308Who can tell [that] merriment?
Narahari swims in that ocean of happiness.

1309Again, raga Bhupali: Today, at the auspicious moment of godhuli,168 Gaura — jewel of virtues, enchanter of the world — in attire arranged as befits a wedding: the radiance of [His] most tender body brims over. Breaker of the pride of millions of Manmathas, lotus-eyed, delighter of people's hearts, looking in all four directions, smiling softly, softly, seated in a chaudola palanquin, He shines.

1310He goes toward Vallabha's house surrounded by brahmanas; the pace very slow and sweet; the bards pronounce many blessings; the world fills with the cry "Jaya, jaya!" The dancers dance, calling out "thai tata"; "khonga khoddina" — how many are absorbed in song;169 composing [songs of His] lovely deeds, joining the svaras, the virtuosos shower juicy rasa.

1311So many, many kinds of instruments are played; without a break sound the syllable-bols for the instruments; the skilled players seem to swim amid an ocean of music. In the sky the gods are utterly absorbed; again and again they gaze with unblinking eyes; in great rapture, unseen, they descend to the earth — what merriment in [their] hearts!

1312Countless women and men run; the broad road is incomparably lovely; hundreds and hundreds of bright lamps display the rays of the lord of the night. The earth blooms in still greater gladness; the waters of the Jahnavi surged; what can Narahari Dasa say? All the beasts and birds float in happiness.

1313Again, raga Bhupali:
To see Gorachand's wedding,
with such longing in their hearts the young wives of Nadia run — none can keep her composure.

1314Incomparable are their attire and garments, their bodies adorned with ornaments, glittering; that grace shines beautifully. As they walk, the kinkini bells on their waists and the anklets on their feet ring; with a very sweet gait they light up the road.

1315In that rapture of rasa, how much [they] say to one another — how charming! At the base of their noses swing besara pendants.170 On lovely faces covered by veils — soft, soft smiles; whom does the flash of those smiles not bewitch?

1316Tinged with collyrium, surpassing the charming khanjana bird — lovely glances of eyes in all four directions. Narahari's heart overflows as he beholds the Lord of [his] life entering Vallabha's house.

1317Again, raga Kamoda:
Gora Raya in Vallabha's house
increases Vallabha Mishra's great joy.

1318Vallabha, overjoyed,
performs the auspicious rites prescribed for the wedding.

1319Vishvambhara, with joy in [His] heart,
stood on a low stool at the place of the wedding rite.171

1320With the grace of [His] limbs [He] steals [their] life;
with the radiance of [His] beauty He lights up the ten directions.

1321What comparison can be given for [His] moonlike face?
With a slight smile [He] destroys the pride of nectar.

1322The glance of [His] eyes has a lovely manner;
whomever [He] looks at cannot keep composure.

1323Makara earrings at the base of [His] ears;
whom does the arrangement of [His] curly hair not bewitch?

1324Angada armlets and bracelets suit [Him] beautifully;
seeing [that] beauty, how many Madanas die of shame!

1325To receive such a bridegroom with the uruthi rite,172
the bride's mother goes with the matrons.

1326Who can describe that beauty?
With seven lamps in hand [she] circles [Him] seven times.

1327Supremely wonderful are the women's rites!
Having received the bridegroom, all go into the house.

1328The fortunate Vallabha Acharya
had his daughter brought in to perform the kanya-dana.

1329They seated [her] on a divine throne;
it became bright with the rays of [her] body.

1330Her body is very tender;
[her] face, suffused with smiles, surpasses the full moon.

1331She is dressed in many-coloured garments;
many ornaments of jewels glitter.

1332Such a daughter, with all the proper rites,
Mishra gave to the son of Shachi.

1333The brahmanas sound the Vedas;
all the women of good families raise the cry "ulu-lu-lu."

1334Instruments of many kinds play;
the dancers dance, the bards recite the raybar.173

1335The gods, mounted on celestial chariots,
rain down flowers unseen, crying "Jaya!"

1336The world was pervaded with great happiness;
how much can Narahari tell with one mouth?

1337Again, raga Bhupali:
Gora, jewel of virtues, with [His] beloved, dear [to Him] as life, delights there in the basar.174
The young wives of good families come and go again and again, full of merriment.

1338Some, on various pretexts, make jokes, laughing and laughing with delight of heart.
Someone, placing tambula in Gora's lotus hand, says: "Put [it] in Lakshmi's mouth."

1339Someone, placing tambula in Gora's moonlike mouth, feels great love grow in her heart. Someone, longing for [His] touch, ties [His] hair and, flustered, cannot keep her composure.175

1340Someone, seating Lakshmi on Vishvambhara's lap, gazes with charming grace.
Narahari says: the rasa that surges in the basar has no comparison.

1341Again, raga Todi:
On the day after Gorachand's wedding,
how much joy surges [in all] as the night gives way to dawn!

1342The young wives of good families run from all sides;
seeing the beauty of bridegroom and bride, all gladden their eyes.

1343How fortunate is Vallabha's wife!
Having obtained a jewel of a son-in-law, she does not know where she is.

1344Mishra Vallabha is exceedingly generous;
what does he not do for the welfare of his son-in-law!

1345Splendid! Vallabha's son-in-law, Gaurahari,
rejoiced, having performed the rites prescribed for the wedding.

1346[Vallabha] brought the rites to completion in proper order;
Narahari says: the gods praise Vallabha.

1347Again, raga Todi:
Gaura, the moon of Gokula, set out for His own home as night turned to dawn.
In private Vallabha, with affection, said much to Lakshmi.

1348Gazing at the road, all the women cannot keep their composure; [tears] stream from [their] eyes. Lakshmi's companions know that Lakshmi's Lord has set out.

1349Conches, dundubhis and bheris sound — instruments of many kinds.
Troupes of dancers dance; the virtuosos sing songs unceasingly.

1350The brahmanas utter the Vedas; the bards proclaim [His] virtues. The world is filled with [the cry] "Jaya, jaya!" — what [can] Narahari [say] of the Lord's play in [His] home?176

1351Again, raga Kamoda:
Having married, Vishvambhara
came from His father-in-law's house to His own home.

1352[That] joy I cannot describe;
all the chaste wives perform auspicious rites.

1353Shachi, taking her daughter-in-law on her lap,
blessed [her], [showering her] with much paddy and durva grass.

1354Sri Shachi's affection has no limit;
so many times she kisses her son's face and her daughter-in-law's face!

1355Seeing the beauty of Lakshmi and Vishvambhara,
no one can turn away [their] unblinking eyes.

1356Gora Raya, enchanter of the world,
pleases everyone with very sweet words.

1357The bards, dancers, musicians and all the rest —
[He] fulfilled the desires of each.

1358Narahari says aloud:
may I see such merriment in Nadia!

1359O Srinivasa, I saw [it] to my eyes' fill;
all the merriment of the wedding I cannot describe.

1360In this house Vishvambhara with Lakshmi
always delighted [in His play], [His] heart full of gladness.

1361There is no end to telling of Sri Lakshmi's character,
in the happiness of whose service Ai was immersed.

1362Sri Lakshmi's Lord, Gaurachandra-Narayana,
was immersed in the rasa of learning together with His students.

1363All the learned men who live in the town of Nadia —
all hold Vishvambhara in respect.

1364Who in Nadia does not praise [Him], seeing [His] conduct?
The Lord shows everyone fitting honour.

1365Bowing to Ishvara Puri, His own servant,
[He] brought [him] with care and gave him bhiksha in this house.177

1366One day here, under the pretext of "vayu," the Lord
manifested prema-bhakti; others did not know [it].178

1367Respectable people came and devised various remedies;
by His own will the Lord restrained [His] bhava.

1368When [He] became well, joy arose in everyone;
after much talk, all judged [it] to be "vayu."

1369At the door of this Vishnu-mandapa, Gora Raya,179
seeing the full moon, played the flute in that mood.

1370Only Ai hears; others do not get to hear;
thus [He] displays various sports at His will.

1371What shall I say, Srinivasa, of Gauranga's deeds?
[He] became eager to bless Vanga.180

1372Here, lovingly bowing at [His] mother's feet,
[He] went to Bengal, taking [His] students.

1373Lakshmi remained here, remembering the Lord;
the serpent of separation from the Lord bit Lakshmi's foot.181

1374On the bank of the Ganga, Lakshmi-devi disappeared;
here, in great grief, Ai weeps.

1375Coming right here, everyone consoles Shachi;
Shachi thinks in her heart of her son's departure.

1376The Lord, the Knower of hearts, learning of Lakshmi's disappearance,
quickly set out from Bengal.

1377Coming here, He bowed at His mother's feet,
and here, saying much, He consoled His mother.

1378Who can understand the wonderful sport of the Lord?
Taking His students with Him, He is overwhelmed by the delight of learning.

1379Here the mother ponders in her heart her son's marriage;
she searches but does not find a girl worthy of her son.

1380The daughter of Sanatana Mishra, Vishnupriya —182
[Shachi] chose her when she went to the ghat of the Ganga to bathe.

1381Kashinatha Pandita, by the order of Sri Shachi,
carefully arranged the marriage with him.

1382Hearing of the match of Vishvambhara with Vishnupriya,
everyone was filled with the highest joy.

1383Buddhimanta Khan and Mukunda Sanjaya,183
taking on themselves the charge of the wedding, say to each other:

1384"This wedding will be like that of a king's son,
so that the eyes of all the people who see it are gladdened."

1385Gaura, the son of the lord of Vraja, who is subject to the will of His devotees,
hearing the devotees' words, smiles slightly.

1386Buddhimanta Khan and the others, with great joy in their hearts,
set about the preparations for the wedding in earnest.

1387Here they had huge canopies stretched out;
bringing banana trees, they planted them here.

1388Full pots and all the other kinds of auspicious things —
the people appointed to prepare them were beyond counting.

1389To prepare flower garlands, sandal paste and the rest,
they appointed people in this secluded place.

1390The provisions they gathered cannot be told;
in spending their wealth they rejoiced beyond measure.

1391Singers, musicians, dancers and all the others —
all of them were stationed in these places.

1392The adhivasa is on the day before [the wedding]: great preparations;184
invitations were sent out all over Navadvipa.

1393The throng of people on the day of the adhivasa,
the clamor that arose — who could describe it?

1394Ai is ceaselessly immersed in great bliss;
she entrusted her friends with performing the auspicious rites.

1395How the wives devoted to their husbands came to this house,
how on the day of the adhivasa they fetched the [ritual] water,185

1396what merriment there was at the adhivasa and the wedding —
all this the poets have described in many ways.

1397Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
Through the town of Nadia the word went round:
"Gora, the jewel of virtues, will marry again!

1398Fortunate is Sanatana Mishra:
he will give his daughter [in marriage] to Nimaichand.

1399That girl's name is Vishnupriya;
in beauty and virtue she has no equal in the world.
