2007The giver of the jewel of prema-bhakti, the son of Shachi,
ceaselessly delights in the bliss of sankirtana.

2008Absorbed in sankirtana, unaware of Himself, the Lord
went along this road on a tour of the town.

2009Displaying great play on the tour of the town,
the Lord with His companions sits here, joyful.

2010The pastimes of Vraja always surge in [His] heart;
Mukunda and others sing of them in the sweetest voices.

2011The Lord has a great longing to hear of His own qualities;
who can understand [His] charming, unfathomable deeds?

2012At the Lord's hint, Gadadhara here
creates the Lord's attire with ornaments of flowers.

2013Dasa Gadadhara and Narahari, dear to the Lord,300
supply all the materials for the attire, having prepared them.

2014[Gadadhara] created for the Lord a world-enchanting attire;
whoever looks even once loses all composure.

2015The beauty of the attire has no comparison;
millions of Kamas faint at the radiance of [His] limbs.

2016What became of the Lord's dear [associates]
as they gazed at [His] moon-like face — who knows how to tell?

2017Overcome with bhava, all offer themselves [to Him];301
they perform arati; there is no end to the joy and splendour.

2018Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Gauri):
Glory, glory to the arati of young Gaura!
He shines on the throne like a golden mountain —
the radiant thief of the hearts of the young women of the world. (Refrain.)

2019Sri Advaita, overflowing with prema, performs arati,
gazing at His own Lord.
On a golden plate studded with jewels
flicker the lamps that dispel the darkness of sins.

2020On the right, wondrous in splendour and manner,
is Nityanandachandra, immersed in rasa;
on the left, Gadadhara, full of grace;
someone there holds a new, shining umbrella.

2021The excellent Srinivasa showers [Him] with garlands of flowers;302
Narahari waves the chamara whisk without pause;
the excellent Shuklambara anoints [Him] with sandal paste;
Murari Gupta cries out, "Jaya!"

2022Madhava, Vasu Ghosha, Purushottama,303
Vijaya, Mukunda and other kings among the skilled
sing sweetly, [displaying] ragas, shrutis, murchhanas,
gramas, the seven svaras and their incomparable varieties.

2023Murajas, mridangas, changas and dhakkas sound;304
vinas, nishanas and flutes — to every end;
again and again the bells; the jhanjharis clash;
"jhan-na-na" the cymbals roar, deep and terrible.

2024Vakreshvara dances in supreme delight;
full of rasa is his splendour, his movement that of a skilled dancer.
He calls out [the syllables]: "dhikata, dhidhi kata,
taka thai thai thai ti" — in many varied ways.

2025Overwhelmed by the former rasa are the rasika Gadadhara,
Shridhara, Gauridasa, Haridasa.305
Who can describe it all? The devotees are utterly intoxicated,
beholding the sweet smile on Gaura's face.

2026The hosts of the gods in the sky are immersed [in bliss]; together with his retinue
the lord of the gods with great effort humbly entreats.
The Lord of Parvati and the Four-faced thrill with rapture;
in streams, in streams, torrents of tears flow from [their] eyes.306

2027The three worlds rejoice, Shesha sings the glory,
the sages offer praises, uttering new names.
Narahari's Lord, the ornament of Vraja, full of rasa,
bestows supreme bliss on the town of Nadia.

2028Beholding the supremely auspicious arati,
all were overwhelmed and forgot themselves.

2029Bringing various foods, [the devotees] feed the Lord;
at the Lord's command all eat with delight.

2030Seeing that the night was far advanced, everyone
lay down to sleep, each in his own place.

2031Knowing that Gaurachandra would lie down, Gadadhara
prepared a very soft, charming bed.

2032The Lord goes to lie down, full of joy,
adorned with garlands and sandal prepared by Gadai.

2033In this room Vishvambhara lay down;
near [Him] lay Gadadhara Pandita.

2034Drinking the nectar of each other's words, both were absorbed [in it].
Who can understand the lila of Gaura and Gadadhara?

2035Waking at dawn, Gadadhara, with joy in his heart,
does what the wise describe.

2036Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the second prakrama:
Gadadhara, greatly wise, a brahmana born of a noble family
and a devotee full of prema, abides near His feet.

2037Staying with him at night, He spoke auspicious words:
"In the morning you should give the prasada to the Vaishnavas."

2038Having said this, Hari gave into his hand the garlands from His body.
Then, in the clear morning, they all came.

2039Whatever had been given for each one, that he gave to him.
Then they, joyful at heart, having bathed in the waters of the river of the gods,

2040having worshipped Jagannatha and offered naivedya,
came again with delighted hearts to Him, the Lord of the lords of the gods.307

2041Every day Gadadhara, having anointed Him with sandal paste,
always joyfully places garlands on His body.

2042In the bedchamber, having made a bed near Him, happily
he sleeps, filled with faith, listening to His nectarean words.

2043And thus also in the Sri Chaitanya-charita-mahakavya:
And that Gadadhara Pandita, the best of the virtuous,
always remaining closely at His side,
day after day serves Him, dearer
than his own life, with intense eagerness.308

2044At night, staying near Him, steady,
he eagerly lies down to sleep.
The nectar of His pastimes is ceaseless,
and ceaselessly it is relished by him.

2045O Srinivasa, at the end of the night the Lord
delights in supreme bliss together with the assembly of devotees.

2046Here, on a splendid seat, sits the Lord Gaura-raya;
the townspeople run to see [Him].

2047Coming to the Lord, they bow again and again.
The Lord says, "May all have bhakti for Krishna."

2048Showing boundless mercy to all, the Lord
instructs [them] in the maha-mantra of Hari's Name:

2049"Hare Krishna Hare Krishna Krishna Krishna Hare Hare
Hare Rama Hare Rama Rama Rama Hare Hare."

2050Again the Lord says insistently, "Brothers,
all of you go home and chant the Name of Hari.

2051By the power of the mantra every perfection will come;
by chanting this mantra you will attain supreme bliss."

2052Again, holding a straw between His teeth, He says to all,
"Perform the kirtana of Sri Krishna day and night."

2053Receiving such instruction from His holy mouth, all,
bowing down, go home and chant the mantra.

2054At the Lord's command all, with jubilation in their hearts,
began sankirtana in every house.

2055The wicked Kazi could not bear the kirtana at all;
he forbade the kirtana; the Lord heard [of it].309

2056Hearing this, Gaurahari, filled with great anger,
proudly reveals His own true nature.

2057Again and again, with great fervour, He roars;
the Lord, together with His associates, prepares for nagara-kirtana.

2058Everywhere the word spread: "The son of Shachi
will today perform kirtana throughout the town."

2059Gaura-raya gave the townspeople this command:
"At the hour of cow-dust, all of you come here."

2060The townspeople, their hearts rejoicing,
came here in their finery — the splendour was extraordinary.

2061There was no end to the people, O Srinivasa;
cries of "Jaya, jaya!" filled the earth and the sky.

2062Sri Gaurasundara, with great jubilation,
first began the sankirtana here.

2063In attire that enchants the world Gaurachandra dances;
on His left is Gadadhara, on His right Nityananda.

2064Advaita, Srivasa, Haridasa, Vakreshvara,
Narahari, Gadadhara Dasa, Damodara,310

2065Murari, Mukunda, Vasu, Govinda and all the others —
all dance and sing; who can describe the splendour?

2066Here, greatly overwhelmed in sankirtana,
Gauranga Himself divided [the singers] into sampradayas.311

2067At the Lord's command the joyful Sri Advaita Raya
goes ahead from here with one sampradaya.

2068At His dancing and singing no one can remain composed;
women and children alike all cry aloud.

2069From here separate, separate sampradayas —
Srivasa and the others — go, dancing and singing in great delight.

2070[Another] sampradaya is the Lord, the son of Shachi:
He goes along this road, His beauty enchanting the world.

2071Here Ai together with her daughter-in-law
was overwhelmed with prema, beholding that beauty.312

2072The Lord Gaura-raya reveals a wondrous lila:
He plunges everyone into the ocean of the bliss of sankirtana.

2073With one mouth, how can I tell that wonder?
Having performed nagara-kirtana, the Lord came here.

2074Here He sits, surrounded by everyone;
the night passed in telling of Krishna's deeds.

2075One day Gaurachandra, in the town of Nadia,
went round the houses of the Vaishnavas, one after another.

2076First of all He went along this road,
surrounded on all four sides by His dearest associates.

2077Having wandered everywhere in great joy,
the Lord, returning home, sits right here with His associates.

2078O Srinivasa, one day here
He danced in sankirtana in attire that enchants the world.

2079Who can understand the Lord's deeds?
In sankirtana He shows mercy to anyone at all.

2080[There was] a brahmana from the land of Vanga, pure in conduct, with his son —
a mendicant brahmana named Vanamali.

2081He sees Gaurachandra as dark [like Shyama] and beautiful,
a peacock feather on His head, wearing yellow garments.

2082He touches the flute to His lips; seeing this, [the brahmana], beside himself,
raised an uproar, crying, "This is Krishna! Krishna!"

2083What can I say of the fortunate brahmana Vanamali!
Here [the Lord] gave [him] the priceless jewel of prema.

2084Here the Lord told the devotees of the glory of the Name;
a wretched student pained [Him], [calling it] arthavada.313

2085Together with His associates He bathed in the Ganga in His clothes,
and never, even by mistake, did He look at that man's face.

2086One day Gaura-raya, in the bliss of sankirtana,
playfully planted a mango seed here.

2087At that very moment a tree grew and began to bear fruit;
plucking many ripe mangoes, [the Lord] offered [them] to Krishna.

2088Without skin or stone, equal to nectar;
one fruit fills the stomach of one [person].

2089The Lord ate those fruits and fed the devotees;
every day, all twelve months, [the tree] bears fruit — such is this wondrous lila.

2090One day here, during kirtana,
great masses of clouds gathered — frightening to see.

2091When the Lord stood here holding the mandira cymbals,
the clouds flew away; all rejoiced at heart.314

2092To teach the people, the Lord, the independent Ishvara,
together with His associates cleans the temple of Vishnu.

2093Thus [it is said] in the Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charita, in the second prakrama:
Then on another day the Lord, teaching His own [devotees] bhakti,
went with the brahmanas to the temples, broom in hand,

2094carrying a spade on His shoulders and a dhati cloth at His waist,
wearing a turban of neta cloth, radiant like the rising sun.315

2095The Acharya and other great souls, spades and brooms in hand,
becoming Krishna's haddipa sweepers, the gate of the temple316

2096and its walls they cleaned together with Krishna — they who were full of virtues.
Such teaching Nrihari Bhagavan, though wholly independent,
out of compassion gave hundreds of thousands of times.317

2097One day here [the Lord] repeats, "Gopi, gopi."
Someone says, "Why does Nimai not say 'Krishna'?"

2098Not understanding His intent, that wretched student
said many such things; hearing them, [the Lord] became like Rudra.

2099Stick in hand, the Lord rushes to beat him;
the brahmana flees, his heart in great fear.

2100That student, joining with other students,
reviles the Lord — whatever comes into anyone's mind.

2101By reviling the Lord the students' intelligence was destroyed;
in none of them does [even] well-studied learning manifest.

2102What is in the Lord's mind He does not reveal;
together with His associates He delights in kirtana in His own house.

2103One day Keshava Bharati came here;
bowing to him, [the Lord] invited [him] and gave him alms.

2104I do not know what passed between them;
Bharati quickly went away to Kantaka-nagara.318

2105Having gone to Srivasa's house and come back, Vishvambhara
sits right here together with His dear Gadadhara.

2106Having bathed, He goes to perform the worship of Vishnu;
His face, chest and cloth are wet with the tears of His eyes.

2107Gaura-raya cannot stop the streams from His eyes;
at the Lord's command Gadadhara worships Vishnu.

2108The Lord is deeply immersed in the pastimes of Vraja;
ceaselessly Gadadhara speaks of them.

2109Who can understand the pastimes of Gaurachandra?
He fulfils completely the desires of all.

2110He gives contentment to Devi Vishnupriya;
He acts in such a way that His mother is pleased.

2111O Srinivasa, in this house of the Lord
I have shown which pastimes He performed in which places.

2112By beholding all these places sorrow is destroyed,
and prema-bhakti, rare even for the gods, is attained.

2113Now I will show the places outside the house;
I will tell a little of what pastimes took place where.

2114From His very childhood, in places outside the house,
the Lord performed wondrous pastimes with His companions.

2115Having shown you all those places,
I will come back and show you the places in this house again.

2116I will also tell what happened in which place;
just now I cannot tell all of it.

2117Having said so much in this way, from the Lord's house
Ishana sets out together with Srinivasa and the others.

2118He speaks to Srinivasa in sweet words:
here in His childhood the Lord played with the children.

2119O Srinivasa, beneath this kadamba
the naked Lord played among the crowd of boys.

2120Respectable people gaze at the Lord's matchless beauty;
the Lord, His face upturned, looks closely at the tree.

2121He asks for kadamba flowers from anyone at all;
everyone says, "There are no flowers now, Nimai."

2122Hearing this, He half began to weep — a wondrous beauty:
in His two eyes, teardrops like pearls.

2123The Lord, His lovely moonlike face shining, says to everyone:
"You will surely get a flower — look now."

2124A certain fortunate [man], gazing at the tree,
sees a flower and quickly plucked it.

2125Placing the flower in Nimai's hand, he took Him on his lap;
great astonishment arose in everyone's mind.

2126Beneath this banyan, taking her son on her lap,
Ai worships Shashthi, offering various gifts.319

2127Here stood an old neem tree:
without fruit, [yet] the fragrance of its flowers was extraordinary.

2128Its shade was most dense, its beauty boundless;
no bird ever sat upon that tree.

2129For as long as Vishvambhara lived at home,
He played beneath that tree — most charming play.

2130The Lord gave His command to Gauridasa Pandita,
and from that tree he manifested two Deities.320

2131How the two Lords became manifest —
that is a most wondrous story, a wondrous pastime.

2132Gauridasa Pandita is full of supreme prema;
he is exceedingly dear to Nityananda and Chaitanya.

2133What shall I say of Nimaichand's play?
By His own will He wanders wherever He likes.

2134All the mischief He makes in the houses of friends and kin —
only Ananta has the power to tell it.321

2135In this brahmana's house one day Vishvambhara
stole milk and drank it with a fearless heart.

2136Seeing a pot of yogurt in a hanging sling, His joy swells;
making a hole in the pot, He puts His mouth beneath it.

2137Having eaten the yogurt, He walks off slowly, slowly;
the brahmana came and caught Nimai by His left hand.

2138Clasping the brahmana's feet, the Lord says again and again,
"I won't do it again, I beg you!"

2139Hearing this and seeing the face dotted with drops of yogurt,
the brahmana was overwhelmed and cannot turn his eyes away.

2140The brahmana says to Nimaichand again and again,
"Every day you shall eat my yogurt and milk."

2141Such various mischief He makes from house to house;
outwardly they are all angry, while in their hearts they rejoice.

2142Along this road the two fortunate thieves,
leaving Vishvambhara at [His] house, ran away.322

2143Here Gaurahari plays, gathering up dust;
the wondrous beauty He had then I cannot describe.

2144O Srinivasa, look at this secluded place:
here that tairthika brahmana lived in secret.323

2145This is the dwelling of the brahmanas Jagadisha and Hiranya,
whose offering [the Lord] ate on Ekadashi.324

2146Sitting here, the brahmanas, in the sweetest words,
joyfully tell of Nimai's restlessness.

2147Look at this beautiful sandbank of the Jahnavi:
here the son of Shachi plays with the children.

2148Games that no one has ever seen or heard of —
those games He plays with great delight in His mind.

2149Along this road Murari Gupta comes;
while explaining jnana, he waves his hands about.

2150The Lord mimics him in the same way;
He went to his house at his mealtime.

2151Speaking of tattva-jnana, He passed urine on his plate.
Look here: the dwelling of Murari Gupta.325

2152Look at this wondrous deity on the bank of the Ganga:
by its grace all desires are fulfilled.326

2153Having bathed in the Ganga, the maidens worship the deity;
suddenly the son of Shachi came.

2154Sitting among the maidens, He makes all kinds of fun;
seeing all this, waves of happiness swell.

2155Vallabha's daughter came here on another day;
what shall I say of the play that took place with her!327

2156Along this road Vishvambhara with the children,
having played, goes home every day.

2157Right here [they] quarrel with other children;
Nimai's companions defeat them all.

2158Nimaisundara is the crest-jewel of the restless;
restless boys are always with Him.

2159At this ghat of the Jahnavi the son of Shachi
makes mischief beyond all counting.

2160The brahmanas and good people, outwardly angry,
go and tell Mishra of [Nimai's] restlessness at bathing time.

2161All the girls go and tell Mother Shachi
the wondrous story of Nimai's restlessness.

2162Beneath this tree the noble Vishvarupa
reflects in his mind: "Nimai is not a human being."

2163Here Sri Advaita and the other beloved ones of the Lord
weep, seeing the evil disposition of the living beings.

2164Vishvarupa explains that devotion to Krishna is the essence [of all];
hearing this, Advaita-deva gives a thunderous roar.

2165Taking Vishvarupa in His arms, Advaita dances;
here the bliss of all the devotees is boundless.

2166Sitting here, everyone tells of Krishna's deeds;
hearing His own story, the son of Shachi came.

2167Naked, grey with dust — seeing [Him], all
were enchanted; no one can turn their eyes away.

2168Standing here, Vishvambhara with a joyful heart
says to Vishvarupa, "Come and eat."

2169Along this road, holding Vishvarupa's cloth,
He goes home — wondrous is that gait.

2170Vishvarupa walks along with Vishvambhara
and again and again looks at Nimaichand's face.

2171What shall I say of Vishvarupa, Srinivasa!
After some time Vishvarupa took sannyasa.

2172On account of Vishvarupa the devotees here,
saying so much, in distress wish to go off to the forest.

2173Struck by the thunderbolts of the pashandas' words, the devotees,
sitting here, are sunk in great sorrow.

2174Here Sri Advaita-deva, the abode of virtues,
with great, proud assurance reassures the devotees.

2175In this house the devotees raise the sound of Hari's name;
hearing it, Vishvambhara comes running.

2176Everyone says, "Why have You come here, child?"
Hearing this, He says, "For what purpose did you call Me?"

2177Saying this, He goes off to play with the children;
by His will no one can recognize [Him].

2178O Srinivasa, what shall I say of this place?
[Here] Nimai studies, and all the people praise it.

2179Fearing in his heart a sannyasa [like] Vishvarupa's,
the father forbade Vishvambhara to study.

2180Not allowed to study, Nimai is sad at heart;
again He took up His insolent pranks with the children.

2181In all these houses He makes all kinds of mischief;
[people] are angry, [yet] no one can say anything.

2182Jagannatha Mishra, at the word of respectable people,
with a joyful heart tells his son to study.

2183Nimai studies with His beloved child companions;
sitting here, He pursues various branches of learning.

2184This is the house of the one dearest to Jagannatha Mishra,
who busied himself zealously with Nimai's sacred-thread ceremony.

2185This is the home of Gangadasa Pandita;
here the son of Shachi studies grammar.

2186Growing more wonderful in grammar day by day,
He composes His own commentary on grammar.328

2187Of Krishnananda, Sri Kamalakanta and Murari Gupta,
staying here, He asks trick questions with a joyful heart.329

2188Immersed in the delight of learning, Sri Gaurasundara
performs pastimes beyond the reach of Brahma and the others.

2189At this ghat of the Jahnavi, with His students,
having sported in the water, He goes home in great merriment.

2190Having worshipped Vishnu and watered Tulasi,
having eaten prasada, He comes and stays right here.

2191Without talk of the scriptures nothing pleases Him;
having become a great pandita, He roams about Nadia.

2192One day here He said many things
to Murari Gupta, yet at this there was no anger in his heart.

2193The Lord and the servant — both discuss the scriptures;
what to speak of others — hearing it, the gods rejoice.

2194Murari, a portion of Rudra, does not know himself;330
at the Lord's explanation great bliss grows in his heart.

2195Look, this is the house of Sri Vallabha Acharya,
whose daughter is Lakshmi, beautiful in every respect.

2196What can be said — how fortunate is Vallabha Acharya!
Here he gave his daughter to Vishvambhara.

2197Before the wedding, on the bank of the Ganga, on this path,
Sri Lakshmi met Vishvambhara.

2198This is the house of Vanamali Acharya,
who took the greatest pains over Lakshmi's wedding.

2199Having married Sri Lakshmi, Vishvambhara
goes along this path to His own home in great merriment.

2200Here many people praise Vishvambhara;
they praise Shachi, who has such a son.

2201Here, staying, all the devotees of the Lord,
not recognizing their own Lord, give [Him] so much instruction.

2202Sri Mukunda Pandita, staying here,
argues much with the Lord, putting forward theses and objections.

2203Here, angered by the words of the pashandas,
Advaita, with a roar, says to everyone:

2204"In a few days, here within Nadia,
you will see Krishna." Hearing this, all rejoiced in their hearts.

2205Look, this is the house of Gopinatha Acharya;
from time to time Vishvambhara comes here.

2206Sri Ishvara Puri stayed here for some days
and here composed the book Krishna-lilamrita.331

2207He bestows the greatest affection on Gadadhara Pandita;
seeing his outbursts of prema, he taught him [his book].

2208Sri Puri has the utmost love for Vishvambhara;332
every day he asks [Him] to correct the book.

2209Vishvambhara shows him the greatest deference
and does whatever pleases him.

2210Here, together with Gadadhara Pandita,
there was discussion of the scriptures — and great amusement in it.

2211Here all, hearing Vishvambhara's discussion of the scriptures,
bless [Him], saying, "May [You] have bhakti for Krishna!"

2212Here to Vishvambhara, when He bowed
to Srivasa and all the other Vaishnavas, [they] give so much instruction.

2213Look, this is the house of Sri Mukunda Sanjaya;
here the Lord constantly engages in the scriptures.

2214Sitting right here, all the brahmanas say,
"'Vayu' has taken possession of Vishvambhara's body."

2215These were transformations of prema-bhakti, but no one knows it;
hearing that the "vayu" has subsided, all rejoice in their hearts.

2216Wondrous are Gauranga's pastimes in Navadvipa:
with everyone He always converses smiling.

2217Who is not enchanted on seeing the son of Shachi?
Along this path the Lord goes for a walk through the town.

2218In this weaver's house the Lord Vishvambhara,
taking cloth, put [it] on — the beauty is captivating.

2219In these houses of the cowherds, with the greatest delight,
He eats yogurt, milk and fresh butter in great happiness.

2220In this perfume merchant's house Gaurahari
put on divine fragrances, showing favor.

2221In this garland-maker's house, with the students,
He puts on divine garlands — they sparkle on His body.

2222Coming to this betel seller's house, Gaura-raya
chews betel with joy in His heart.

2223O Srinivasa, Gaurachandra with His associates
roams Navadvipa in great merriment.

2224Formerly, walking through the city of Madhu, the Lord
satisfied the hearts of all in just this way.333

2225Coming to this house of the conch merchant,
He took a conch with great amusement.

2226This, in the middle of Navadvipa, is the house of the all-knowing one (sarvajna);334 here came the Lord, the son of Shachi.

2227With the sweetest words the Lord says to the all-knowing one,
"Who was I in another birth? Come, tell Me."

2228Hearing this, the all-knowing one chants the excellent Gopala mantra;
by the power of the mantra he sees the son of Vasudeva:

2229seeing the four-armed One with conch, disc, club and lotus,
he looks at Vishvambhara and again closes his eyes.

2230Again he sees the son of Nanda, the Holder of the flute,
in the divine pose bent in three places, dark and beautiful.

2231Seeing the avataras — Sri Rama, Varaha, Nrisimha and others —
the all-knowing one ponders ceaselessly in his heart.

2232The Lord says, "Tell [it] — I will listen." The all-knowing one replies,
"I will tell later; now, please, go."

2233Hearing this, smiling ever so gently, Sri Gaurasundara
came here, to this house of Shridhara.335

2234All the fun the Lord has with Shridhara —
no one can tell it with one mouth.

2235Having roamed through Navadvipa, Vishvambhara
went along this path with everyone to His own home.

2236Pastimes of eagerness for a fight and others are beyond words;
He performs them all whenever the Lord so wishes.336

2237Along this royal road the Lord, the son of Shachi,
walks in attire that enchants the world.

2238Unexpectedly — a meeting with Srivasa Pandita;337
and of all the talk with him there is no reckoning.

2239O Srinivasa, sitting here, Gaurachandra,
filled with bliss, gazes at the beauty of the Ganga.

2240On all four sides are the disciples, the beauty is boundless;
the Lord discusses the scriptures and enchants everyone.

2241One of the disciples, to the Lord Vishvambhara,
very softly tells the news of the digvijayi.

2242On his tongue the goddess Sarasvati speaks;
having conquered everywhere, he has come to Nadia.

2243By the power of his learning the digvijayi counts no one for anything;
with him are elephants, horses, palanquins and many people.

2244All the great teachers of Navadvipa
became very anxious at heart.

2245Hearing this, smiling ever so gently, Vishvambhara says,
"The Lord (Ishvara) leaves no one's pride standing."

2246Seeing [His] beauty from afar, the digvijayi
came near, greatly astonished.

2247Vishvambhara, showing him the greatest respect,
asked him to describe the glory of the Ganga.

2248The digvijayi, with great pride, composed many verses;
Vishvambhara asked him to explain them.

2249The verses are very difficult, accessible to no one;
laughing, the digvijayi explains the meaning of his own verses.

2250When the brahmana, having explained the verses, fell silent,
Vishvambhara pointed out faults at the beginning, middle and end of the verses.

2251The digvijayi, defeated, fell to thinking;
and yet the son of Shachi preserves his honor.

2252"Lord Gaura-raya is the complete Brahman, the eternal" —
such knowledge came [to him] by the mercy of Sarasvati.

2253The digvijayi took shelter at the Lord's feet;
the mercy the Lord showed [him] cannot be described.

2254The digvijayi belongs to a Vaishnava sampradaya;
he introduces himself by the name Keshava Kashmiri.338

2255The disciple of Sri Narayana is Hamsa — so it is proclaimed;
Sanaka and the others, the four Sanas, are his disciples.339

2256The disciple of Sanaka is Sri Narada Mahashaya;
his disciple is Nimbaditya, the abode of virtues.

2257The disciple of Sri Nimbaditya is Sri Srinivasacharya,340
whose glory became manifest everywhere.

2258His disciple is Vishvacharya, foremost in every respect;
his [disciple] is Sri Purushottamacharya, the learned.

2259Sri Vilasacharya is his disciple, most steadfast;
his disciple is Sri Svarupa Acharya, the profound.

2260His dear disciple is Sri Madhavacharya, the best of the best;
his dear disciple is Srimad Balabhadracharya.

2261His disciple is Padmacharya, renowned everywhere;
his disciple is Sri Shyama Acharya, of beautiful conduct.

2262His dear disciple is Acharya Gopala;
his disciple is Kripacharya, supremely merciful.

2263His disciple is Devacharya, the abode of virtues;
his disciple is Sri Sundara Bhatta, the compassionate.

2264Srimad Padmanabha Bhatta is his disciple;
his disciple is Sri Upendra Bhatta, whose fame [is great].

2265His dear disciple is Ramachandra Bhatta;
his disciple, dear to all, is Sri Vamana Bhatta.

2266His disciple is Krishna Bhatta, deeply serene;
his disciple is Padmakara Bhatta, the learned.

2267The disciple of Sri Padmakara is Sri Shravana Bhatta;
his disciple is Bhuri Bhatta, whose conduct is extraordinary.

2268His very dear disciple was Sri Madhava Bhatta;
his disciple was Shyama Bhatta, of great realization.341

2269His disciple was Sri Gopala Bhatta, of noble character;
his disciple was Balabhadra Bhatta, pure in his ways.

2270His disciple was Gopinatha Bhatta, revered by all;
his disciple was Sri Keshava Bhatta, wondrous in his deeds.

2271His disciple was Sri Gokula Bhatta, most steadfast;
his very dear disciple was Keshava Kashmiri.

2272By performing japa of the mantra of the goddess Sarasvati
all learning dawned in him, and his power grew.

2273Having conquered all directions, [he won] fame as "the digvijayi";
[he was] of a most cultured brahmana family of the land of Kashmir.

2274At a most auspicious hour he came to Navadvipa;
giving up everything, he departed at the Lord's command.

2275Keshava Kashmiri, the digvijayi, ashamed of this,
described the enjoyment of the lilas under the name "Laghu-Keshava."342

2276Fortunate is the digvijayi Keshava Kashmiri:
there is no end to telling of the happiness in which he was immersed.

2277The defeat of the digvijayi at the hands of Nimai
is known everywhere; people proclaim this glory.

2278Wherever one goes, one hears only these words:
"Nimai Pandita is the crest-jewel of teachers."

2279Thus [He] plays many sports on the bank of the Ganga;
the Lord, who acts as He wills, goes home by this path.

2280One day, as [He] was going along this path,
[He] sees twenty sannyasis coming.

2281With the greatest respect [He] brings all those sannyasis
home and feeds them various foods.

2282Thus [He] constantly feeds sannyasis;
all are greatly amazed, for [they] see [Him] earn nothing.

2283The Lord desired to go to Bengal;
having set out, [He] stopped at the house of this brahmana.

2284The Lord, having gone to Bengal with His students,
sent Sri Tapana Mishra to Kashi.343

2285Having blessed Bengal, [He] returned after some days;
the brahmanas, going out to meet [Him], bring [Him] along this path.

2286Surrounded by His students, Sri Gauranga-sundara,
enchanting the hearts of all, goes to His own home.

2287Sitting here, the brahmanas, with restless hearts,
speak very softly of the separation from Lakshmi.344

2288"Vishvambhara has come back from Bengal;
seeing the house empty, He will feel great sorrow in His heart.

2289Nimai Pandita is a jewel among great men."
Saying this, all went to console [Him].

2290One day someone came here after bathing;
not seeing tilaka [on him], [the Lord] taught [him] to apply [it].

2291O Srinivasa, here Nimai, in sport,
teased the people from Bengal in various ways.345

2292The sports that Vishvambhara reveals here —
words do not come to the mouth to tell them all.

2293Look, here is the house of Sanatana Mishra,
who was the Raja-pandita, eminent in every respect.

2294Sanatana Mishra's daughter is Vishnupriya;
with one mouth I cannot tell of her deeds.

2295Sanatana Mishra, with great joy in his heart,
gave his daughter to Vishvambhara here.

2296Look at the dwelling of Kashinatha Pandita;
he took very great pains over Vishnupriya's wedding.

2297Here the devotees, greatly distressed,
lament at not finding the company of devotees.

2298Saying, "Ha Krishna, ha Krishna!" they heave deep sighs;
at that time Thakura Haridasa came.

2299Wondrous are the deeds of Haridasa Thakura;
how much of them shall I tell? They are known everywhere.

2300Here Gaurachandra, sitting, reflects in His heart:
"My descent is for revealing prema-bhakti.

2301Coming back from Gaya, I shall destroy the sorrow of the devotees
and reveal prema-bhakti, which is supremely rare."

2302Having reflected thus, the Lord, with joy in His heart,
consoling His mother, sets out on pilgrimage to Gaya.

2303Having set out, [He] stayed in the house of this brahmana;
in the morning He went along this path with His students.

2304Having made [the pilgrimage to] Gaya, Vishvambhara [showed] Ishvara Puri
so much favor — who can tell of it?

2305There the manifestation of prema-bhakti began;
with His students [He] set out for Navadvipa.

2306Sri Shachi's son came to Navadvipa;
in Navadvipa there was great bliss for all.

2307Everyone went out to meet [Him] and bring [Him] back;
along this path the Lord went home.

2308Gaura-raya swims in the rasa of prema-bhakti;
seeing [this], all the Vaishnavas rejoice at heart.

2309To Srivasa, Ramai, Gopinatha and Gadadhara
Shriman joyfully says here:346

2310"Nimai Pandita has come back from Gaya,
and there is not a trace of all that [former] haughtiness.

2311Telling us of the holy place Gaya,
He cannot speak of the lotus feet of Vishnu:

2312[tears] pour from both His eyes like the current of a river;
saying 'Krishna!' He falls to the ground unconscious.

2313I saw wondrous transformations of His prema."
Hearing [this, all] say much — great is everyone's joy.

2314Here Srivasa and the others, having praised Vishvambhara,
go and sit in the house of Shuklambara on the bank of the Ganga.

2315Here is the dwelling of Shuklambara Brahmachari;
coming back from Gaya, the Lord came here.

2316Seeing Shriman Pandita and the others here,
[He] speaks of Krishna, and [His] heart overflows.

2317Regarding Himself as lowly, the son of Shachi,
clasping everyone by the neck, weeps.

2318The devotees who were hidden here and there —
all weep from Gaurachandra's prema.

2319The Lord says, "Who is weeping inside the house?"
Shuklambara says, "Your Gadadhara."

2320How the outpouring of prema began I cannot tell;
the brahmachari sank into an ocean of bliss.347

2321Ratnagarbha Acharya, near this tree,
recites a verse of the Bhagavata with great joy in his heart.348

2322Hearing the glorification of devotion to Himself,
Gaurachandra, fainting from prema, falls right here.

2323Sri Ratnagarbha's good fortune cannot be described:
regaining consciousness, the Lord embraced him.

2324O Srinivasa, what shall I say of this place?
The Lord reveals Himself in His own kirtana.

2325Seeing Vishvambhara's absorption in prema, the devotees
here reported everything to Sri Advaita.349

2326The all-knowing Prabhu, Lord Advaita,
on hearing [this], in great joy — the hair on His body stood on end.

2327In many ways He made [it] known to the devotees;
what He had seen in a dream, that too He told.

2328Who can understand the acts of Advaitachandra?
One moment He reveals [the truth], the next He conceals it.

2329Having heard wondrous words from Advaita,
the devotees, bowing to Him, departed.

2330O Srinivasa, the deeds of Gaurachandra
became known in Nadia day by day.

2331At this ghat of the Ganga the Lord, intoxicated with the rasa of bhakti,
serves the devotees in every possible way.

2332The humility [He] shows I cannot describe;
Gaurahari makes known that service to the devotees is foremost.

2333What shall I say? In the Lord's heart is a great wish:
to receive the devotees' blessings constantly.

2334In secret the Lord enjoys [His pastimes] in Nadia;
who can know [Him] if the Lord [Himself] does not make [Himself] known?

2335Though Nimai Pandita is revered by all,
He carries the Vaishnavas' flower baskets and dhotis without shame.

2336Here the devotees, gazing at Gaurachandra's face,
give blessings, giving much instruction.

2337Vishvambhara, taking the dust of the devotees' feet on His head,
says so much — who can repeat it?

2338One day, along this path, Lord Vishvambhara
went to Advaita's dwelling, and with [Him] Gadadhara.

2339Seeing [Him], Advaita here was overwhelmed with prema;
again and again the golden body trembles.

2340Advaita Acharya, with great joy in His heart,
saying many things, prepares [all] for the worship of the Lord.

2341With fragrances and flowers He worships the Lord's feet;
bowing again and again, He offers praise.

2342Seeing Advaita's actions, Gadadhara laughs;
biting his tongue with his teeth, he says in a soft voice:

2343"You should bestow blessings that bring good;
to treat a boy like this is not proper."

2344Laughing, Advaita says, "You do not know yet;
who this boy is you will know in a few days."

2345Hearing [this], Gadadhara was amazed at heart;
in his mind he reflects: "Surely this is the Lord."

2346After a while Gaura-raya, returning to outward awareness,
says many things to Advaita and conceals Himself.

2347The Lord, Gaurahari, is subdued by Advaita's prema;
the delight that took place here I cannot tell.

2348Cherishing many longings, with joy in His heart,
from here Advaita went to Shantipura.

2349The happiness the Lord knew here, absorbed in sankirtana —
[even] the Four-faced One does not know how to describe that absorption.

2350All the Vaishnavas could not remain steady in prema;
the notion that Lord Vishvambhara was a human being left them.

2351Here, absorbed in prema, the Lord told the Vaishnavas
what He had seen in the village of Kanai Natashala.350

2352Here, in sankirtana, He gives out hunkaras and thunderous roars;
hearing [them], the crowds of pashandas all but die, ranting wildly.351

2353At the words of the pashandas the Vaishnavas grieve;
that the Lord has descended — this no one knows.

2354To destroy [their] grief and to make Himself known,
He wanders through Nadia in most beautiful attire.

2355Dressed up, He comes from the house along this road;
seeing [Him], the pashandas all but die, ranting wildly.

2356Seeing the world-enchanting beauty of Gaurachandra,
the virtuous were filled with great joy.

2357Women and men alike — all are stirred at heart;
seeing Gaurachandra, they say so much to one another!

2358Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
Gaura, the best of moons, the Enchanter of Vraja,
wanders through Nadia.
Old men without number, who have come out onto the road,
gaze [at Him] with joy in their hearts.

2359One says: "What is this? Ananga, so finely formed —
who created [him]?
Such wondrous, abundant beauty
has come before [our] eyes!"

2360Another says: "What is this — is love being born?
What can I say — it cannot be told.
In the casket of my heart I will hold [Him] every moment —
tell me, by what means [can this be done]?"

2361Others, in so many, many ways,
ceaselessly give good blessings.
Narahari Dasa ever takes in
the sweetness of the Lord, filling his eyes.

2362Raga Kamoda:
What joy there is in Nadia today!
All the old women on the road, standing in rows,
gaze at Shachi's darling child. (Refrain.)

2363One says to another: "He is no human being at all —
I have understood this, reflecting in my heart.
A youth such as this I have never seen nor heard of the like,
since I was born in the land of Bharata."

2364One says again and again: "What can I say? At last
all [our] sorrows have come to an end."
Another says: "What is in my heart I cannot express:
blessed is this life in Nadia!"

2365One says: "Blessed is Shachi! How many pious deeds she has done —
that I do not know how to tell.
She whom He, with this moon-like mouth, always calls 'Mother' —
who else has such good fortune?"

2366One says: "May He wander through Nadia just like this,
taking all the virtuous with Him."
Another says: "This is all my heart wishes: that golden Nimai
may never leave Nadia."

2367One says: "May He always dwell in Nadia in well-being —
this I pray to the Creator.
Gora is the life of Narahari, the very pupil of my eyes;
may I die taking His misfortunes upon myself!"

2368Raga Bhupali:
Hearing that Gauranga is coming, the blind
step out of their homes.
Gaining sight, they look [at Him] again and again;
their bodies fill with delight.

2369One, taking another's hand, says softly:
"Today it has borne fruit.
To give us great bliss the Creator made [us] blind —
he did not let us look at anything else.

2370Having drunk the nectar of this beauty, what my heart is doing
cannot be known.
Whoever has not seen such beauty
is blind, though he has eyes.

2371To look always, again and again they rush forth —
[my] eyes cannot hold to patience.
Narahari is my witness: I have given these eyes
to golden Nimaichand."

2372Raga Todi:
Hearing that Gora, the jewel of virtues, is wandering through Nadia,
the lame, going out onto the road,
gaze at that face with unblinking eyes —
their hearts overflow with bliss.

2373One says: "Listen: the Creator is merciful —
now I have understood this in my heart.
The purpose for which you made [me] lame — that fruit
you have brought to ripeness now, after so many days.

2374Had I not been lame, on household business
I would have gone to a distant land.
Had I died there, not knowing [of Him],
there would have been no end to my sorrow.

2375That I may remain lame just as I am —
this I pray to the Creator —
that I may always see the Lord of Narahari in Nadia,
filling these eyes."

2376Raga Kamoda:
Gora, the enchanter of the world, the jewel of virtues,
walks along the royal road with so many graceful movements.
Hundreds upon hundreds of Madanas, swooning,
roll at [His] lotus feet.

2377On all sides people come running, racing one another,
enchanted by the matchless beauty.
Who does not offer [for Him] body, mind and life,352
telling one another of [His] lovely deeds?

2378In the town of Nadia, in dandyish attire,
all the young nagaras stroll about.353
Looking at Gorachand, all of them
lost their pride as nagaras.

2379Those in the world who were most experienced
and drunk with the pride of their refinement in rasa —
says Narahari — like fireflies
before the moon, so did they become.

2380Raga Dhanashri:
The Moon of Nadia, playfully, along the royal road
walks swaying, His heart thrilling with delight.
All the young women, unseen, in agitation,
longingly cast half a glance at that form.354

2381One says: "Look, look, friend, here is
Gora's beauty — is it not a heap of nectar?
With the red of betel the lips are glowing,
and on them — what a gentle, sweet smile!

2382How the garland of rangana flowers sways!
With the play of His eyes He enchants the world.
How lovely the mass of curling locks!
On His forehead shines a tilaka of sandal paste.

2383What a shape His pair of arms has, [reaching] to the knees!
Who would not lose her heart to that broad chest?
I am deeply immersed in the rasa of the Lord of Narahari —
I have bid farewell forever to shame and family."

2384O Srinivasa, the Lord, wandering through Nadia,
reveals Himself to give happiness to the devotees.

2385Walking gracefully, He looks all around;
He sees herds of cows, beautiful on the bank of the Ganga.

2386Lowing "hamba," herd after herd, the cows run;
they drink water and, tails raised, look about on all sides.

2387They butt one another; seeing this, the Lord
roars out: "I am He! I am He!"355

2388In wondrous ecstasy, along this road Vishvambhara
joyfully ran to the house of Srivasa.

2389In Srivasa's home, in this room, with the door shut,
[Srivasa] worships Nrisimha-deva, wholly absorbed [in worship].356

2390Gaurachandra kicks this door;
at that hunkara Srivasa's meditation was broken.

2391Angry that his meditation has been broken, the brahmana looks around on all sides —
and sees the effulgent Vishvambhara seated in virasana.357

2392Holding in four hands the conch, disc, club and lotus,
He roars loudly, saying much to Srivasa.

2393Srivasa is stunned with fear — nothing comes [to his mind];
at the Lord's command, rejoicing, he offers praise.

2394The wondrous deeds of the Lord in each of His incarnations —
these, in that ecstasy, he reveals through his praise.

2395Learned in all the scriptures, the venerable Srivasa
offers praise before the Lord — his heart overflows.

2396Hearing the wondrous turns of [his] praise, Gaurahari
mercifully granted [him] the boon he desired.

2397There is no limit to the good fortune of Srivasa and [his] family;
right here Srivasa worships the Lord's feet.

2398That wondrous puja is beyond comparison;
how pleased [the Lord] is with the puja — who can tell?

2399On the heads of all [He] places [His] lovely feet;
in supreme bliss He destroys the fear of the devotees.

2400Here a little girl named Narayani,
at the Lord's command, weeps, [crying,] "Krishna!"358

2401That girl is the daughter of Srivasa's brother;
a four-year-old girl, exceedingly fortunate.

2402All the Lord's absorptions in bhava are beyond the perception of others;
returning to outer awareness, Vishvambhara becomes bashful.

2403"Tell no one," He said to Srivasa,
and from here, along this road, He went to His own home.

2404One day the Lord, absorbed in the mood of Sri Varaha,
roaring, goes along this road to Murari's dwelling.

2405Entering this Vishnu shrine, Vishvambhara
took the form of Varaha, supremely beautiful.

2406Seeing here in front of Him a water vessel — a gadu jug —
He seized [it] in His teeth, absorbed in His own feeling.

2407The Lord says to Murari again and again:
"All this time you did not know of My incarnation!"

2408At the sight of the Lord, Murari was stunned:
what to say — nothing comes to his lips.

2409"Speak, speak!" says the Lord. "There is nothing to fear."
Murari offers praise; streams [of tears] flow from his eyes.

2410Hearing Murari's praise, Lord Gaurahari
in ecstasy says so much that I cannot recount it.

2411How much mercy the Lord showed Murari,
what bliss Murari felt — who can tell?

2412In this way the Lord, in the homes of all the devotees,
bestowing great mercy, makes Himself known.

2413Recognizing their own Lord, the devotees with joyful hearts
perform sankirtana, taking no account of the pashandas.

2414One day Srivasa and Murari, coming here,
spoke to each other of the glories of Gaurachandra.

2415Srivasa Pandita in remorse says again and again:
"All this time I did not recognize my own Lord!

2416My heart is ever breaking — what more can I say?
Such a Lord carried my flower basket and [my] dhoti!

2417I gave [Him] blessings, saying, 'May there be bhakti for Krishna!'
To Krishna Himself I gave so much instruction to worship Krishna!"

2418Thus Sri Murari and the others dear to the Lord,
all, lamenting greatly, weep.

2419Here the Lord, to Srivasa and all the other devotees,
gives hints of Nityananda's coming.

2420Suddenly coming to Nadia, Nityananda
stayed in secret; Gaura-raya came to know of it.

2421Revealing [to the devotees] Nityananda, hidden from others,
He goes along this road to meet Him.

2422Sri Nandana Acharya is supremely fortunate;
look, Srinivasa, here is his house.

2423The Lord, coming to this house with the company of devotees,
sees Nityananda sitting absorbed in meditation.

2424The incomparable sweetness of Nityananda's form
the devotees, standing, behold, filling their eyes.

2425Before Nityananda, Vishvambhara shines;
Nityananda sees the captivating beauty of the Lord.

2426Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata:359
"Vishvambhara's form is like that of Madana;
divine fragrances and garlands, clad in divine garments.

2427What is the lustre of gold before that body?
To gaze on that face the moon itself longs.

2428At the sight of those teeth, pearls lose their pride;
seeing that dressed hair, one loses one's senses.

2429Reddish to behold are those dawn-coloured eyes;
one wonders: is there any other lotus like them?

2430Those two arms reaching to the knees, the broad chest;
on it shines a white sacred thread, very fine.360

2431On the forehead, a wondrous, beautiful upright tilaka;
without ornaments, every limb is captivating.

2432What are millions of jewels when one looks at those nails?
What would nectar do when one sees that smile?"

2433How Nityananda-raya, seeing Vishvambhara's beauty,
rejoiced in His heart — how could I tell it?

2434To reveal the heart of Nityanandachandra,
Srivasa recited a shloka at the Lord's hint.

2435Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Tenth Canto (10.21.5):
With a crown of peacock feathers, in the form of the finest dancer, with karnikara [flowers] on His ears,
wearing a garment golden-yellow like gold, and the Vaijayanti garland,
filling the holes of the flute with the nectar of [His] lips, He whose glory is sung by the bands of cowherd boys
entered Vrindavana, made delightful by His footprints.

2436Hearing the shloka of meditation on Krishna, Nityananda-raya —
the bhava that overcame Him, who does not sing of it?

2437Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Mayura):361
Overflowing with bhava, beautiful Nitai,
gazing at the radiance of Gora's moon-face —
how much rises in [His] heart! He cannot stay still;
on every limb, fresh waves of horripilation.

2438What divine madness! — now a lion's roar,
now He rolls on the ground;
now a deep sigh, now loud laughter;
His cloth slips off, He is awash in the tears of [His] eyes.

2439Now leaps with both feet, now trembling in the body,
now He runs — no one can hold Him;
now, having said something, He becomes motionless,
sheltering in Vishvambhara's embrace.

2440Taking Nityananda on His lap, in the tears of His eyes
the Lord is awash — such is the way of prema!
Narahari says: Srivasa and the others all around
weep — no one can keep his composure.

2441O Srinivasa, here there is endless bliss;
the whole world knows how Nityananda was overcome with bhava.

2442Here Nityananda stays on Vishvambhara's lap;
seeing it, Gadadhara smiles softly, softly.

2443Lord Vishvambhara and Nityananda, staying here —
I cannot tell what the two of Them spoke about.

2444The happiness in which Srivasa and the other devotees here were drowned —
all of it cannot be told with one mouth.

2445Here the son of Shachi says to Nityananda,
"Tomorrow is the full moon — Your Vyasa-puja."362

2446"Where will the puja be?" — hearing this, with joy in His heart
[Nityananda], laughing, says, "In the house of this brahmana here — Srivasa."363

2447At Nityananda's words Vishvambhara here rejoiced;
there was a long conversation with Srivasa.

2448All of them, from the house of Nandana Acharya,
went along this path to the house of Srivasa Pandita.

2449O Srinivasa, in this courtyard of Srivasa
Gaurachandra dances in sankirtana with Nityananda.

2450The two Lords dance, all around are the devotees;
that rapture of prema cannot be described.

2451Here Gaurahari, absorbed in the mood of Balarama,
reveals [it] with reverence before Nityanandachandra.364

2452Leaping up, the Lord mounts the cot
and calls out without stopping, "Varuni! Varuni!"

2453Someone filled a vessel with Ganga water and brought [it];
all see the Lord as if drinking kadambini.365

2454He asks Nityananda for the sacred plough and club;
Nityananda gave [them] — the fortunate saw it.

2455Here in joy Prabhu, the son of Padmavati,
beheld the six-armed form of Sri Gaurachandra.366

2456Here the Lord called out, crying, "Nada! Nada!" —
by the word "Nada" He indicated Advaita Acharya.367

2457Immersed in the bliss of prema, He says so many things;
hearing them, the devotees are filled with the greatest joy.

2458Here Nityananda was overwhelmed with prema —
where did His staff and waterpot end up!

2459In His childlike mood Nityananda is always restless;
Gaurachandra, holding Him, calms Him.

2460Here at night Nityananda, saying who knows what,
broke His staff and waterpot and threw [them] down here.368

2461Lord Vishvambhara, taking the staff and waterpot,
gave [them] over to the Ganga — I do not know what He said [then].

2462Taking Nityananda with Him, [He] bathed in the Ganga;
the fun that was there cannot be told.

2463Taking fragrances, sandal paste and the like, according to various rules
the Lord here began the Vyasa-puja.

2464What the Vyasa-puja was like I cannot tell;
I gazed my fill at the delights of the Vyasa-puja.

2465Here the Mother of the world, Shachi Ai,
seeing Nimai and Nitai, was filled with equal affection [for both].

2466The transformations of bhava that [were] in the sankirtana of the Vyasa-puja —
when I think of all that, my heart breaks.

2467Here was the eating of the offerings of the Vyasa-puja;
who can tell what delights there were in it?

2468Here grew a kunda tree, full of beauty;
in gathering [its] flowers the Vaishnavas had the greatest bliss.369

2469O Srinivasa, one day Gaura-raya
came here in haste from His own house.

2470The Lord, laughing, says to Srivasa,
"Advaita is coming, bringing the articles for worshipping Me.

2471He wishes to see My majesty."
Having said this, overcome with prema, [He] roars.

2472O Srinivasa, from here Gaura-raya [goes]
into this shrine of Vishnu and sits on Vishnu's throne.370

2473Surrounding [Him] on all sides, the devotees
gaze at the Lord's moon-face.

2474Nityananda holds an umbrella over [His] head;
Gadadhara offers tambula to [His] mouth.

2475All are engaged in service in various ways;
at that time Advaita arrived.

2476Prostrating himself on the ground, Advaita Gosani approaches;
the happiness that arose [then] has no end in the telling.

2477He gazes at the Lord's wondrous beauty:
an effulgence like millions of suns, enchanting the worlds.

2478Gaura's body is adorned with various jewelled ornaments;
smiling, He plays the flute, standing in tribhanga.371

2479Brahma, Shiva, Shesha and the other gods and rishis —
all offer praises before the Lord.

2480Beholding the Lord's wondrous majesty,
Advaita Acharya rejoiced in his heart.

2481The Lord says to Advaita again and again,
"For the sake of your vow is My descent."372

2482So many such things, overcome with prema, He says to Advaita;
hearing them, all the devotees are in great joy of heart.

2483With joined palms Advaita stands;
the Lord says, "Worship Me together with your wife."

2484Hearing this, Advaita's heart overflowed with bliss;
he washed the Lord's feet with scented water.

2485Moistening tulasi buds with sandal paste,
with what longing he places [them] on the Lord's feet!

2486Having performed worship with great care with sixteen offerings,
he offers praises to the Lord in countless ways.

2487Overwhelmed, he is awash in the tears of [his] eyes
and falls, rolling, at the Lord's feet.

2488Knowing Advaita's desire, Gaura-raya
lifted His foot and placed [it] on Advaita's head.

2489When [He] placed His foot on Advaita's head,
then a great cry of "Jaya! Jaya!" arose.

2490O Srinivasa, here Sri Advaita, at the Lord's command,
dances in the Lord's sankirtana.

2491Seeing that rapture of prema, who could keep his composure?
The beauty of that body steals the hearts of all.

2492Fixing his eyes on Sri Gaurachandra's lotus face,
with who knows what bliss, he cannot hold his heart steady.

2493Unable to keep his composure, he rolls on the ground;
looking toward Nityananda, he is awash in tears.

2494The ways of Advaita Acharya — who can understand them?
After a while, by the Lord's will, he became calm.

2495Gauranga, giving Advaita [His] garland,
says again and again, "Ask a boon, ask a boon!"373

2496Advaita says, "I have attained every perfection";
and saying, "Be merciful to the living beings," he chose this boon.

2497All that was spoken between Sri Advaita and Vishvambhara —
who can understand the inner meaning of all those words?

2498All were immersed here in great bliss,
hearing the words full of prema of Nityananda and Advaita.

2499Along this path Prabhu Gaurachandra went home;
Nityananda stayed in Srivasa's house.

2500With his companions Advaita went to his own abode;
look, here is Advaita's abode, full of beauty.374

2501The devotees happily went to their own homes;
what I saw — how can I tell it with one mouth?

2502O Srinivasa, by Gaurachandra's will
devotees, coming from afar, gather in Nadia.

2503Pundarika Vidyanidhi, drawn by the Lord,
with a mind burning with eagerness to see the Lord,

2504with many people, Vidyanidhi, [coming] from Vanga
to Nadia, went along this path to [his] house.

2505Sri Mukunda, a resident of the same village, rejoicing,
came here and met Sri Vidyanidhi.375

2506This is the abode of Pundarika Vidyanidhi,
for whom the son of Sri Shachi wept.

2507He is a supreme Vaishnava; how would others understand [it]?
Only Sri Mukunda and Vasudeva Datta know [him].

2508What his outward conduct is like — what shall I say of it?
Dressed like a prince, he sits here.

2509Hearing that [he was] a supreme Vaishnava, Pandita Gosani376
came here with Mukunda to see him.

2510He did not know Sri Vidyanidhi's inner state:
at the first sight [he] formed the notion — "a worldly Vaishnava."377

2511Understanding Gadadhara's heart, Mukunda, finding a way,
reveals what lay in Vidyanidhi's heart by means of a verse.

2512Thus [it is said] in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, in the Third Canto (3.2.23):
"Oh, wonder! He whom Baki, wishing to kill [Him], made drink
the deadly poison of her breast — [from Him] she, though wicked,
attained the destination befitting a nurse; other than Him,
to what other merciful [Lord] shall we go for shelter?"378

2513And in the same [work], in the Tenth [Canto] (10.6.35):
"Putana, the killer of the world's children, the rakshasi who fed on blood,
though wishing to kill [Him], gave her breast to Hari — and attained the good destination."379

2514Hearing the shlokas, Vidyanidhi, his heart losing all composure,
says again and again: "Speak on, speak on, Mukunda!"

2515Trembling, sweat, thrills, hunkaras — beyond measure;
he weeps, streams flow from both his eyes.

2516Flinging his body down, he falls upon the ground;
from the blows of his feet the bed and everything else flew far away.

2517Of all his fine attire not a trace remained;
his beautiful body became grey with dust.

2518He rolls about on the ground, lamenting so much —
who, seeing that absorption in bhava, could keep his composure?

2519Here he fell into a swoon;
regaining consciousness, after some time he grew calm.

2520Seeing [this], Gadadhara Pandita was greatly amazed;
his body was drenched with his own tears.

2521He says to Mukunda: "I have committed an offence;
you have saved me," — and praised him so much.

2522The offence would go if he became his disciple —
informing the Lord [of this], he became his disciple.

2523Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata, in the Madhya-khanda:
"At Gadadhara's words the Lord was pleased;
He began to say, 'Quickly, quickly!'"

2524Then Sri Gadadhara, from Premanidhi,
gladly received initiation into the mantra himself.

2525What more can I say of Pundarika's greatness,
whose disciple is Gadadhara: this is the limit of his bhakti!

2526A worthy guru, Pundarika; the disciple, Gadadhara;
both are the body of Sri Krishna Chaitanya.380

2527O dear Srinivasa, what can I say of this?
Gadadhara Pandita became [his] disciple here.

2528When [he] was becoming a disciple, Mukunda and the other Vaishnavas —
all were overwhelmed in great prema.

2529Hearing of this, Nityananda-Haladhara
laughs softly, softly, with great joy in His heart.

2530Who can understand Nityananda's nature?
Always in the mood of a child He stays in Srivasa's house.

2531Srivasa's wife, Sri Malini, devoted to her husband,
always serves Nityananda as a mother serves her son.

2532He Himself does not eat, taking up food with His own hand;
with a mother's love Malini joyfully feeds [Him].

2533What Srivasa's love for Nityananda is like —
no one else has the power to tell it.

2534The Lord tested Srivasa's heart;
knowing [his] deep attachment, He gave [him] a boon and entrusted [Nityananda to him].381

2535Nityananda in the mood of a child roams through Nadia;
He goes to the houses of Gangadasa and Murari Gupta.

2536From there, swimming in the Ganga with great delight,
He comes running joyfully to see Ai.

2537How Ai loves Nityananda with a mother's love —
when I think of all that, this heart of mine breaks.

2538O Srinivasa, how much shall I tell you?
The wondrous ways of the Lord I saw here.

2539With Nityananda, Advaita, Gadadhara and others,
setting out from His own house, He comes in great delight.

2540There is no limit to the beauty of the Lord with [His] associates;
entering Srivasa's house, He sits down at this spot.382

2541Look: here is Srivasa's lovely courtyard;
here Vishvambhara began the sankirtana.

2542Srivasa, Mukunda and Sri Govinda Datta —
all of them, with their [singing] groups, became intoxicated with sankirtana.383

2543Nityananda, Advaita, Gadadhara, full of prema —
all of them, beside themselves, behold the Lord's dance.

2544In the sankirtana Shachi's son dances;
from the blows of [His] feet the earth trembles without pause.

2545What the beauty of the Lord's fine attire is like, what [His] absorption in bhava is like — the wise describe, with boundless joy in their hearts.

2546Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Gauri):
The champaka, gold, flowers, the golden mountain
the loveliness of Gaura's body has surpassed.
His lofty neck — no limit [to its beauty] can be grasped;
His bearing enchants the mind of the world.384

2547Glory to the son of Shachi, worshipped in the three worlds,
who destroys the fear of the deadly serpent of the Kali age! (Refrain.)

2548His body is stirred with abundant thrills,
His heart overflows with the weight of prema;
a soft, soft smile, faltering speech —
how many Mandakinis stream from His eyes!385

2549He dances [to the song of] His own qualities, His eyes rolling;
hundreds of devotees, gathered together, sing.
In that rasa the whole circle of the earth floats, helpless —
[only] Govindadasa has not touched it.

2550Again, raga Todi:
Gaura dances, overflowing with bhava,
His body covered with abundant thrills.

2551The moon of His face shines, joined with a smile,
ceaselessly raining the nectar of rasa in streams.

2552His eyes, surpassing the young dawn, are brimming with moisture;
He makes so many [graceful] movements, putting Kusumashara to shame.386

2553His hands, [like] young shoots — the gestures are exceedingly beautiful;
with what delight He sets His feet upon the earth!

2554Every moment He is wild, like an intoxicated elephant;
He glitters — is it a golden mountain?

2555The matchless attire and hair steal the composure of the eyes;
on all four sides the beloved associates sport in joy.

2556They sing ever newer songs, ever sweeter;
to hear [them] all the men and women come running.

2557Khamak and mridanga sound delightfully,
ceaselessly beating out "dha dha dhigi ti."387

2558Purandara with the gods proclaims, "Glory, glory!"
Blessed is the Kali age — [the fortune of other ages] is slight by comparison.388

2559All the sinners floated in the ocean of happiness;
deprived of this is only the foolish Ghanashyama.

2560Again, raga Nata:
Gaurahari dances, the moon of the twice-born line.
His pair of feet, all-auspicious, removing fear,
He sets upon the earth with supreme grace.

2561Ceaselessly overflowing with His former bhava,389
His body is thickly covered with thrills, [like] a kadamba [with blossoms].
Curling hair, a golden sheen, smooth and glossy —
like a cloud on the peak of a golden mountain.

2562A garland of malati flowers, adorned with bees,
sways, lovely, hanging and glittering on His chest.
A snare for Manmatha, a jewel delighting the mind —
His eyes, [like] a pair of reddish lotuses, tremble.

2563Seeing the matchless dance, the beloved associates
sing, pouring down sweet, sweet rasa.
All people are immersed in the ocean of happiness;
the foolish Narahari, far away, does not touch [it].

2564Again, raga Ghantarava:
Gaura dances, the master of all dancers;
His matchless movements steal Madana's pride.
Shattering the pride of the blazing sun,
with the radiance of His body He lights up all the quarters.

2565Wild, matchless, His roar surpassing a lion's —
hearing [it], the mighty elephant of Kali is afraid.
Again and again He leaps; His gait graceful and restless;
from the blows of His feet the earth shakes.

2566The associates humble the pride of the Kinnaras:
joyfully they sing, and the nectar of rasa flows.390
Many khols and khamaks sound — the sound
touches the sky; who can keep his composure?

2567Matchless power — the wicked, trembling,
take shelter and fall at [His] feet.
The fame of Narahari's Lord remains, filling the world:
He ceaselessly distributes the supreme, most rare treasure.

2568Again, raga Mayura:
Today, at the auspicious beginning of the kirtana, Gaurasundara, joyful in the dance,
shines sweetly amid His skilled associates in Srivasa's courtyard.
Putting to shame the pride of golden filaments, with the lovely radiance of His body delighting Atanu,
the lotus-eyed One, glancing restlessly in the four directions, enchants the minds of people.

2569A dancing gait; the soles of His feet very tender; as He keeps the tala, the earth shakes; He makes hastakas — swift, well-formed — the splendour of His most graceful bud-like hands.391 His teeth outshine a string of pearls; smiling softly, softly, He rains nectar; the sweetness of His lovely face, full of rasa, surpasses a host of autumn moons.

2570Smooth curling hair, gathered up; a fine tilaka and sandal, beautifully applied;
abundant ornaments; His body sparkles; the curves [of His form] cannot be told.
To the Lord's left is Gadadhara Pandita, to the right the handsome Nitai,
in front Sri Advaita; seeing [Him] wild, the gods come running.392

2571Vasudeva, Srivasa, Nandana, Vijaya, Vakreshvara, Narayana, Gopinatha, Mukunda, Madhava — these wondrous masters sing. Rama on the left; Garuda, Govinda and others play the mardala: "dhiki ta ta dhik, dhini-nini-nini-ni."393 Narahari says: the sound of "Glory, glory!" filled the world.

2572Again, raga Dhanashri:
In Srivasa's courtyard, to a charming measure,
Chaitanya-raya dances.394
Humans and gods, men and women —
all come running to see.

2573The circle of devotees sings auspicious [songs],
khol and karatalas sound.
In the midst, wild, Nitai dances,
intoxicated with the bhava of [His] Brother.

2574His arms, surpassing golden pillars, beautifully rounded,
His waist surpassing a lion's.
In His moon-like face is the abode of Madana;
an appearance enchanting the world.

2575I do not know how many men and women of the fourteen worlds,
gazing and gazing at [His] form, weep.
He roars again and again, leaps over and over,
and, taking the guise of a wrestler, dances.395

2576With reddish eyes, pouring down prema,
He drenches the circle of the earth.
Upon the circle of the earth a downpour of prema
has Avadhutachandra released.

2577The lord of Shantipura roars ceaselessly,
seeing the transformations of prema;
clasping [His] holy feet, weeps
the magnanimous Srivasa Pandita.396

2578Mukunda, full of eagerness, weeps, sobbing,
embracing Gadadhara.
Prema flows from the eyes; Thakura Abhirama
again and again [cries], "Hari, Hari!"

2579They know neither day nor night, floating in the rasa of prema —
all the companions.
For Vrindavana Dasa, prema is revealed
by the lotus feet of Nitai.

2580O Srinivasa, in this courtyard of Srivasa,
the dancing and kirtana — who could describe [them]?

2581How many people fitted [here] — there is no counting;
what can I say — wondrous is the power of this courtyard!

2582Unable to get into the kirtana, [for] the gates were shut,
how many hundreds of people here all but die, raving!397

2583In the sankirtana the night passed to the third prahara;
no one's body grew weary.

2584Everyone supposes it is the third prahara of the night;
how many yugas passed in it — that [they] do not know.

2585Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata, in the Madhya-khanda:
"[It was] a year in name only: how many yugas passed!
In the bliss of absorption in Chaitanya [they] noticed nothing."

2586Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the second prakrama:
Thus the Lord, Murari, spent the whole night for the delight of the minds of His own people;
the long [time, as long as] a year, the best of the noble ones took for a moment, and attained unceasing happiness.398

2587In the sankirtana, in a wondrous absorption in bhava,
the Lord called the devotees by their former names.

2588Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-bhagavata, in the Madhya-khanda:
"Looking at all the Vaishnavas one by one,
the Lord, absorbed in bhava, calls [them], naming [them] by their former names.

2589In whatever bhava the Lord manifested whatever —
what to speak of others: at that, wood and stone melted.

2590Nityananda, Advaita, Gadadhara and all the rest —
what shall I say of what they all became?"399

2591O Srinivasa, by the order of Gaurachandra
the kirtana grew still at the end of the night.

2592The Lord, absorbed in bhava, again looks in all four directions;
with the shalagrama-shila in His lap He sat on the couch.400

2593Having said much to the devotees, Gaura, the treasury of virtues,
partook of yogurt, milk, fresh butter, and the like.

2594How [all] went on with the devotees in the mood of servitude,401
how that absorption was — that cannot be described.

2595Sri Murari Gupta, with great joy in his heart,
staying here, gazes at the beauty of the Lord.

2596Gora, the life of Janaki, says to Murari,402
"Let Me hear verses composed by you."

2597Sri Murari Gupta recites the Ramashtaka;
hearing it, [the Lord], in the mood of Rama, is gracious to Murari.

2598Smiling gently, gently, in great bliss He praises [him]
and writes on his forehead the name "Ramadasa."403

2599The account of that Raghunathashtaka is very sweet:
from one who hears it all sufferings go far away.

2600Thus [it is said] in the Sri Chaitanya-charita, in the third prakrama:404
Then the Compassionate One said to Murari, "Recite yourself
your poetry." Hearing this, he recited [it] in auspicious syllables.

2601Now, the ashtaka:405
Him whose radiance of the jewels of the shining crown illumines the quarters,
who wears two earrings like rising Brihaspati and Kavi,
whose face is like the moon without a spot —
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2602With eyes like lotuses opened by the rays of the rising sun,
with lips [like] beautiful bimba fruits, with a lovely nose,
with a charming smile that has conquered the rays of the moon —
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2603Him with a neck [like] a conch, the Unborn, whose form is like a lotus,
shining, wearing strings of pearls and golden necklaces,
like a cloud joined with lightning and flocks of cranes —
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2604The lotus resting on her upturned palm with her excellent fingers
turning into [a lotus] of a hundred and five more petals,
Sita, shining like glowing gold, stands at His side —406
that best of the Raghus I constantly worship.

2605Before Him is the best of archers, his body shining like gold,
devoted to serving his elder brother, rich in excellent ornaments,
the great splendour called Shesha, who bears the name Lakshmana —
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2606Him who is the moon [risen] from the ocean of the dynasty of the Raghava kings,
who, having slain the rakshasas Maricha, Subahu, and others,
protected the sacrifice — the heap of merit of the descendant of Kushika —407
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2607Having slain Khara and Trishiras with [their] host, [and also] Kabandha,
having made the holy Dandaka forest free of Dushana,408
He made friendship with Sugriva, killing [his] enemy —
that Raghava, the slayer of the Ten-faced, I worship.

2608Having broken the Pinaka, He performed with the daughter of Janaka
the rite of the wedding festival; on the road the lord of the Bhargavas
having conquered, the best of the Kakutsthas brought joy to his father —
Rama, the guru of the three worlds, I constantly worship.

2609Having thus heard the eight shlokas on Raghunandana, the lion among kings,
the Lord, [His] foot on the head of the physician Murari
placing, wrote on [his] forehead:
"O, by My mercy be you 'Ramadasa'!"

2610What shall I say? Seeing such great mercy to Gupta,
the devotees rejoiced greatly in their hearts.

2611At daybreak the Lord went to His own house;
the devotees went each to his own home.

2612What shall I say? He always sports with the devotees;
constantly absorbed in bhava, He cannot become calm.

2613The Lord's holy absorption is beyond the reach of others;
day and night His body is drenched with the tears of His eyes.

2614One day, by this road, with the assembly of devotees,
He goes from the house to the bank of the Ganga in great delight.

2615At the Lord's command, here the dear devotees
began a sankirtana rare [even] for the gods.

2616In absorption He goes dancing among the devotees;
who does not sing of the Lord's wondrous deeds?

2617Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Shri):
The golden body that steals the heart joyfully roams with the devotees,
with a grace that enchants Madana.
The body that robs gold of its colour — a fresh cloud of compassion has filled [the world],
the friend of the burning world.

2618Now weeping, now laughing, [His] colour changes, [His] speech is sorrowful,
in His eyes an ocean of tears.
Day and night He is overwhelmed by bhava, rows of hairs standing on end [like] nipa flowers,
His face an autumn moon.

2619His sweet words have conquered nectar; on His reddish feet the jingle of anklets;
He walks slowly, slowly.
The whole world floats in bliss; Govindadasa hopes
for a drop of the ocean of prema.

2620Again, raga Todi:
Behold, Gaurachandra manifest, surrounded by the host of stars — the devotees,
illumining the whole world with the lustre of kunda and gold.
For the helpless and fallen [He is] the friend of the kumudas [— the moon]; seeing [Him], the ocean of rasa surges;
dispelling the darkness in the cave of the heart, [He] has risen both day and night.

2621His body, naturally beautiful and sweet, in bliss upon bliss knows no restraint;409
swaying, swaying, swaying, He walks and plays like a maddened king of elephants.
Engaged in dance He is lost to Himself, [saying] "Mukunda, Madhava, Govinda!" —
He weeps, laughs, falls to the ground; rows of hairs standing on end shine.

2622Who can tell the glory of [His] glory? His own and others He seizes and embraces;
joyfully raining the nectar of prema — and the thirsting earth became intoxicated.410

2623In that rasa the high and the low float; Govindadasa alone is deprived:
who knows at what moment who fashioned [his] chest, hard as wood!

2624Again, raga Ashavari:
The son of Shachi, Gaurasundara, the enchanter of the mind, dances.
So many, so many mridangas sound, beating out "dhi-dhi-kata dhilanga";
they sing sweet melodies; the movements of [His] limbs
are supremely beautiful. (Refrain.)

2625Incomparable rasa rejoices today: He sports among the dear devotees;
His most graceful attire sparkles, robbing young women of their composure.411
Lovely hair adorned with flowers; earrings in the ears, cheeks [like] mirrors;
tilaka on the forehead, charming brows — bees, eyes — lotuses.

2626The nostrils — an abode of fragrance; the face puts a host of moons to shame;
a gentle, gentle smile, teeth [like] kunda [buds], sweet speech.
The neck takes away the burden of Madana's pride; the two arms surpass an elephant's trunk;
soft armpits, a broad chest, an incomparable garland swinging.

2627The navel shines, encircled by three folds; the line of hair — [like] a serpent;
the slender young waist with its girdle breaks the pride of the lion.
He wears excellent garments and attire; even Shesha cannot describe the thighs;
the soles of the feet of Narahari's Lord put the young dawn to shame.

2628O Srinivasa, the Lord on the bank of the Suradhuni,
immersed in the bliss of sankirtana, walks slowly, slowly.

2629He reveals the good fortune of the Ganga to the utmost:
with His associates He sports on the bank of the Ganga.

2630Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Natta):
On the bank of the river of the gods sports Gaura, in unchanging youth;
the lustre of [His] body crushes the pride of lightning, gold, and kunkuma.
His moon-like face torments Madana; [He is] a snare for the eyes of all young women;412
when He laughs, the rows of His teeth shine — a line of kunda flowers.

2631Of the colour of collyrium and massed clouds, the curling hair steals composure;
the attire is spotless, the clusters of locks shine incomparably.
The tilaka on the forehead sparkles brightly; the brows move charmingly, [like] serpents;
the restless glance, the corner [of the eye] tinged with rasa — an abode of beauty.

2632Earrings adorn the ears and cheeks; the neck is encircled by a forest garland;
the arms are long, bracelets on the wrists — so tender, I offer myself [to them]!
The broad, excellent chest is incomparable — it ruins so many hosts of virtuous wives;
the graceful, very slender waist humbles the pride of the lion.

2633The arms sparkle, the knees are youthful, the feet [shine] with rays [like] rows of dawns;
in the weight of the sweet fragrance of [those] lotuses the devotee-bees are entranced.
A cloud of compassion, known to the whole world, ever raining the nectar of prema,
[yet] Narahari's mind is very dull — it does not touch [it] in the least.

2634Again (raga — the name is unclear):413
The bank of the Suradhuni is a supremely pure place;
there all the generous devotees rejoice.
They sing so many, so many nectarean songs,
they play instruments of every kind.

2635The jewel of virtues, young Gaura, dances.
Smeared with sandal, [His] limbs are very lovely;
wondrous beauty — the thief of the minds of women. (Refrain.)

2636The eyes — petals of a spotless lotus — are brimming [with lustre];
the play of the brows, the fresh play of the locks.
The face puts to shame a host of autumn moons;
the smile crushes the pride of millions of Madanas.

2637Restless, graceful, on the broad chest
sparkles a necklace of jewels that surpasses lightning.
When the feet of Narahari's Lord keep the beat,
then what a sweet sound — the jingling of the anklets!

2638Again, raga Vasanta:
On the bank of the Suradhuni, young trees and creepers,
ever new, new shoots, flowers blossoming.
Enchanted by the fragrance, swarms of bees hum;
cuckoos and parrots flit about on all sides.

2639There dances the dancer, young Gaura.
Smeared with saffron, musk, and sandal,
[His] body, red with phagu, shines all the brighter. (Refrain.)

2640Incomparable attire, garments, jewelled ornaments;
the lovely, swaying forest garland sparkles.
New graceful movements enchant the minds of the world;
again and again He keeps the beat with His soles.

2641The associates sing supremely sweetly;
beholding the moon of [His] face, [they are] in unbroken joy.
The gods in the sky, absorbed [in bliss], cry, "Jaya, jaya!";
Narahari plays the sweet mridanga.

2642Again, raga Vasanta:
Today on the bank of the Suradhuni beautiful Gaura is lost in dance;
[His] body, smeared with drops of phagu and fragrant sandal, shines.

2643On the forehead sparkles incomparable tilaka; a graceful mass of hair;
the earrings in the ears adorn the cheeks; the play of the brows is boundless.

2644Restless eyes — lovely lotuses; the radiance of the face conquers the moon;
red lips, a lovely smile — soft, soft; the teeth put pearls to shame.

2645The arms — golden lotus stalks; the broad chest subdues Manmatha;
on the neck a garland of malati, charmingly made, colourful, swaying.
