he performed all the marriage rites enjoined by the shastras.

3903When he gave his daughters to Nityananda,
at that moment the gods showered flowers.

3904He sees his son-in-law together with his own daughters;
he does not know how much happiness surges in his heart.

3905He cannot blink — a great longing grows;
looking at Nitai, he sees the form of Balarama.

3906The luster of [His] limbs steals the pride of a silver mountain;
the moon of His face surpasses the splendor of the very essence of the moon.

3907His body is adorned with ornaments of various jewels;
so beautiful in every limb, He enchants the world.

3908He sees Vasu[dha] and Jahnava as Varuni and Revati;
the luster of their limbs surpasses heaps of gold and kunkuma.617

3909To the left and right of Baladeva they shine,
radiant in wondrous garments, ornaments and the rest.

3910To give happiness to the devotees — a great manifestation of majesty;
seeing it, Suryadasa forgot himself.

3911Tears stream from his eyes, he cannot control his body;
even as he was bowing and offering prayers, his sleep broke.

3912After a while, composing himself, at daybreak
he himself went to the house of that brahmana.

3913Bowing respectfully to the brahmana, he said,
"What you spoke of must be done; there must be no more delay."

3914Hearing this, the brahmana rejoiced and, taking four people with him,
set out, remembering Durga and Ganesha.

3915He, known everywhere, came to Nadia
and with joy at heart went to Srivasa's house.

3916In the house of Srivasa Pandita, among His dear ones,
he sees Nityananda sitting on a splendid seat.

3917Beholding the beauty that enchants Kandarpa,
he considers himself blessed; his eyes are full of tears.

3918Honoring the brahmana, Srivasa Mahashaya
offered [him] a seat and asked after his welfare.618

3919The brahmana said, "All is well; I have come from home.
What is on my mind I shall tell in private."

3920Srivasa took the brahmana to a secluded place;
the brahmana, delighted, says to Srivasa:

3921"Having heard by word of mouth the talk of an auspicious marriage,
I have settled on a bride and hurried here.

3922The daughter of Suryadasa Pandita is like Lakshmi;
I have looked everywhere — there is none to compare with her.

3923As Nityananda-deva is, so is His wife;
you will see with your own eyes — what more shall I say?

3924Suryadasa Sarakhel is foremost in every respect;
[his house] is a fitting place for Nityananda-chandra's marriage.

3925This is no matter for delay — I have told you;
take counsel and give me leave."

3926Srivasa Pandita spoke most sweet words:
"What you yourself have undertaken will surely come about.619

3927Today I shall send Krishnadasa to Baragachhi,
and tomorrow we shall all go there from here.

3928Come there with the pandita — there is no need for delay;
need I say more? You yourself will accomplish everything."

3929At Srivasa's words the brahmana took his leave
and quickly informed the pandita in Shaligrama.

3930Srivasa Pandita, greatly delighted,
informed everyone, telling Advaita Acharya [as well].

3931Nityananda-Haladhara smiles gently;
the heart of Nityananda is inaccessible to others.

3932Everyone rejoiced at the matter of the marriage;620
Krishnadasa quickly went to the village of Baragachhi.

3933Krishnadasa, the son of Raja Hari Hod,
very intelligent, quickly made [all] the preparations.

3934Everywhere the news of the auspicious marriage spread;
"A wonderful match!" everyone says everywhere.

3935From Navadvipa, everyone, taking Nityananda along,
set out joyfully for the village of Baragachhi.621

3936As they were entering the outskirts of the village of Baragachhi,
the villagers came forward to receive [them].

3937The brahmanas and good people were beyond counting;
seeing Nityananda-chandra, all rejoiced.

3938Krishnadasa took [them] to his own house;
charming lodgings were provided for all.

3939Shaligrama is a short distance from Baragachhi;
receiving the news, all rejoiced at heart.

3940Suryadasa Pandita to his younger brother Krishnadasa
speaks in private in very sweet words:622

3941"Take these supplies and come afterwards with the brahmanas;
I shall go ahead."

3942Having said this, he came quickly to Baragachhi
and presented himself before Nityananda Prabhu.

3943He falls, rolling at Nityananda's feet;
Suryadasa is awash in the tears of his two eyes.

3944Clasping both [His] feet with both hands,
he wants to say something, but words do not come.

3945Smiling softly, softly, Nityananda, absorbed in prema,
mercifully embraced Suryadasa.

3946Suryadasa is ceaselessly overwhelmed with bliss;
who can understand Suryadasa's heart?

3947Seeing the stirrings of prema in [his] brother, Gauridasa
cannot keep his composure; within his heart is great delight.

3948Suryadasa met with everyone;
the Lord's adhivasa was fixed for an auspicious moment.

3949Taking various articles [for the rite], together with brahmanas,
Krishnadasa Pandita came from home.623

3950The brahmanas and good people living in the village of Baragachhi —
all of them came at the hour of godhuli.

3951The brahmanas and good people sit on all sides;
in the middle Nityananda shines at the auspicious adhivasa.

3952All the women and men gaze, unable to look their fill;
an auspicious clamour of instruments arose.

3953As [it is said] in a song (raga Mangala):
Today, at the auspicious moment, at Nitaichand's adhivasa —
what a display of beauty!
In matchless attire [He] shines splendidly;
the radiance of [His] body sparkles and glitters.

3954Of how many hundreds of Manmathas [He] takes away the pride!
Lovely is the moon of [His] face, mingled with a smile.
[His] lovely eyes surpass the petals of the lotus;
[His] glance leaves no one [his] composure.

3955On all sides the brahmanas recite the Vedas;
seeing [His] lovely bearing, [they] rejoice at heart.
The women's hearts overflow with delight;
again and again [they] give forth "ulu-lu-lu-lu."

3956The sound of many instruments pierces the sky;
the dancers dance — what sweet movements!
The world fills with cries of "Jaya, jaya!";
Ghanashyama says: great merriment!

3957All the brahmanas and good people who had come to the adhivasa
went to their homes content.

3958Between Baragachhi, Shaligrama and the other villages,
day and night, many hundreds of people come and go.

3959When Nityanandachandra's adhivasa had been performed,
Suryadasa, mounting a carriage, quickly went home.

3960With great joy in his heart, taking the brahmanas,
[he] performs the adhivasa of the brides at an auspicious moment.

3961Although in a dream [he] had seen the power of [his] daughters,
still, from parental love, [he] was utterly overwhelmed.

3962The Pandita's house became full of auspiciousness;
on all sides people come and go.

3963Taking the articles for the adhivasa from Baragachhi,
the brahmanas joyfully went to Suryadasa's house.

3964Who knows how to tell the merriment at the adhivasa?
The wives of the gods and others watch that splendour with delight.

3965As [it is said] in a song (raga Bhupali):
The goddesses Vasudha and Jahnava — the very limit of beauty —
[their] bodies adorned with the ornaments of the adhivasa.
The lovely radiance sparkles and glitters,
as if lightning, kunkuma and ketaki.624

3966On all sides the brahmanas count themselves fortunate;
looking at the brides, [they] rejoice at heart.
Sounding the Vedic [hymns], they give blessings,
placing paddy and durva grass on the heads of both.

3967The Pandita's wife cannot keep her feet on the ground;
[barely] does she hold her heart in patience.625
[Her] women friends perform various auspicious rites,
give forth "ulu-lu-lu" — with what longing!

3968Many instruments sound — conches, bells and others;
the clamour is beyond compare.
Narahari says: the wives of the gods watch unseen —
how much merriment in [their] hearts!

3969When the rite of adhivasa was complete, the brahmanas
joyfully went each to his own home.

3970At the adhivasa of the bridegroom and brides — happiness above all;
fortunate people watched, unable to look their fill.

3971At the hour of godhuli the Lord, from Baragachhi,
set out for Shaligrama to be married.

3972Many instruments sound — that happiness has no limit;
seeing that splendour, the people were amazed.

3973As [it is said] in a song (raga Deshapala): Breaker of the weight of pride of millions of Manmathas, the supremely elegant Nitai Haladhara, goes seated in a new chaudola palanquin; [His] beauty brims over.626 Arrayed in attire as befits a wedding — how many kinds of ornaments shine on [His] limbs! Lovely eyes, a lotus face; a soft smile charmingly flashes.

3974Exceedingly intoxicated as they drink in [His] beauty, the brahmanas cry "Jaya, jaya!";627 the bards, glad at heart, again and again proclaim [His] spotless fame. Leaving their homes, women and men run, [and] can find no restraint; gazing, they stand on all four sides without blinking, floating in the happiness of the rasa of seeing.

3975The virtuosos sing — tanas, shrutis, svaras, ragas, murchhanas, gramas most sweet; the dancers dance, calling out "taka-taka thai-ta thai-thai thi ni-ni-na." The musicians play a great many instruments; the tala is displayed — none could be more skilful: "thonka na-na-na-na, thonga thunkata, dho dhilanga dhiki dhi ni-ni-na."628

3976Countless lamps blaze upon the earth; the night became bright as day; a vast clamour sounds unceasingly; the road along which all the people go is resplendent.629 The gods, [abiding] in the sky, watching unseen, in rapture, thrilling, shower flowers; the incomparable pastime of the Lord of Narahari Dasa enchants people's hearts.

3977Entering Shaligrama, Nityananda Raya
goes with a jubilant heart to Suryadasa's house.

3978As soon as the lotus feet of Lord Nityananda touched [them],
the people of Shaligrama became vessels of bhakti.

3979Sri Vasu and Jahnava, both, hidden from sight,
saw the Lord of [their] life and became greatly delighted.

3980The Pandita's wife, with her women friends,
utterly overwhelmed, watched, remaining unseen.

3981With [her] friends [she] beautifully adorned the brides;
what comparison can be given? — the beauty became boundless.

3982At Suryadasa's house the crowd was immense;
what the gathering of brahmanas was like cannot be told.

3983According to custom and scripture, fortunate Suryadasa
gave his two daughters to Nityanandachandra.

3984Seeing the bridegroom and the brides, the brahmanas praise [them];
in heaven, on earth and in the netherworld [cries of] "Jaya, jaya!" arose.

3985All the people of the villages near Shaligrama,
seeing the wedding, praise [it] — each as much as [he can].

3986On the day after the wedding there was great rejoicing:
Nityananda fulfilled all [their] desires.

3987At the time of farewell Suryadasa, in humility,
said so much that I cannot repeat [it].

3988With Sri Vasu and Jahnava, Lord Nityananda
came to Baragachhi — there was great rejoicing.

3989Srivasa's wife and all the other elder [women],
overwhelmed with joy, did all that was proper.

3990Seeing the beauty of Sri Vasu and Jahnava, [all] were amazed;
the longing that had been in everyone's heart was fulfilled.

3991Sri Vasu and Jahnava, Nityananda's beloveds,
are Sri Varuni and Revati, a treasury of all virtues.630

3992Thus [it is said] in the Sri Gaura-ganoddesha-dipika:631
His beloveds, Sri Vasudha and Jahnava, sprung from portions of Sri Varuni and Revati,
are the daughters of the great soul named Sri Suryadasa, [the embodiment of] Kakudmi, radiant as the sun.

3993Some call Sri Vasudha-devi Kalavani,
and some declare Jahnava to be Ananga Manjari.
Both are correct by the earlier principle — such is the view of the saintly.632

3994In the village of Baragachhi merciful Nityananda,
staying for some days, enjoys various pastimes.

3995The giver of bhakti, the refuge of the life of Sri Vasu and Jahnava —633
countless are [His] virtues; [He] is utterly intoxicated with love for Gora.

3996The deeds of Nityananda, the purifier of the fallen,
the great poets describe; [they are] known throughout the world.

3997In a song (raga Kamoda):
Krishna's elder brother Rama, the son of Rohini,
the treasure of the life of [His] two beloveds, Varuni and Revati —

3998blessed in the age of Kali is that beautiful Nitai,
the elder brother of Chaitanya, the son of Padmavati.

3999The Lord of the life of Vasudha and Jahnava, full of prema —
by His own nature the Lord became merciful to the living beings.

4000Intoxicated with love for Gora, [He] knows neither day nor night;
by giving the nectar of prema, [He] purified the earth.

4001From anuraga for Gora that body is crimson;
it sparkles and glitters, surpassing molten gold.

4002In [His] ears swing earrings that entice the minds of sages;
[His] arms reach to the knees; matchless beauty.

4003Seeing [His] broad chest, who would not lose his head?
Chaste women of noble families renounce their families.634

4004With that moon-like mouth [He] always says, "Gora, Gora!";
tears flow from [His] eyes, streaming over face and chest.

4005With [His] dear associates, in that rapture,
[He] always floats in the ocean of the happiness of sankirtana.

4006With world-enchanting grace dances the treasury of virtues —
rare [even] for the gods, the limit of all beauty.

4007Gazing at Nitaichand, who can stay steady?
Even a heart like stone melts.

4008To sinners and the fallen [His] compassion has no limit;
such a Lord wretched Narahari did not worship.

4009After some days Nityananda Raya, together with everyone,
came from Baragachhi to Nadia.

4010Seeing both Sri Vasu and Jahnava here, Ai
showed [them] such affection that it is beyond my power to tell.

4011All the wives of the devotees dear to the Lord,
seeing Vasu and Jahnava, were overwhelmed with joy.

4012Taking Ai's permission, Nityananda Rama
went by way of Shantipura to Saptagrama.

4013At the devotees' wish the Lord, going to Khardaha,
settled His beloveds in a wonderful dwelling.

4014For some time Nityananda enjoys [His pastimes] there;
[His] dear associates felt great bliss.

4015Having enjoyed sankirtana in the region of Khardaha,
[He] came to Nadia to see Ai.

4016I have told this whole account briefly;
the fortunate [poets] will describe [it] in detail.

4017The qualities of the supremely merciful son of Padmavati
the poets describe in various ways.

4018In a song (raga Kamoda):
Lord Nityananda Rama, matchless in beauty and qualities,
was born from the womb of Padmavati.
Taking His own companions with Him, for twelve years, joyfully,
[He] played in Sri Ekachakra.

4019When Gora descended, on the pretext of accompanying a sannyasi,
[He] left home.
Having wandered through the holy places, after twenty years
[He] joyfully came to Nadia.

4020Finding [His] life, Gorachand, falling into that snare of prema,
[He] threw far away [His] staff and water-pot.
Ever intoxicated in sankirtana, [He] goes with the Lord to Kshetra
and breaks the Lord's staff into three pieces.635

4021By the Lord's command, coming from Kshetra to Gauda,
[He] did the work dear to the Lord's heart.
The refuge of Narahari Dasa, the husband of Vasu and Jahnava,
distributed prema to anyone and everyone.

4022O Srinivasa! Sri Advaita, together with [His] companions,
is ceaselessly absorbed in singing of Gaura's deeds.

4023Now in Shantipura, now in Nadia He stays;
who does not sing the qualities of Sri the son of Nabha?636

4024Thus [it is said] in a song (raga Kamoda):
Sri Advaita — the jewel of virtues, the treasure-mine of all rasas —
took birth from the womb of Nabha.
Born in Navagrama in Vanga, and having joyfully played there,
after some time He came to Shantipura.

4025After the departure of father and mother He went wandering to the holy places,
and on returning settled in Shantipura.
Becoming the husband of Sri Sita, and performing many austerities every day,
He brought down Krishna and Haladhara.

4026Seeing the pastimes in Nadia, He always delighted [His] eyes,
and danced in kirtana in many styles.
Receiving in His own house Gorachand, the crest-jewel of sannyasis,
He served Him with joy.

4027While the Lord stayed in Nilachala, He went back and forth there,
and made everyone mad with the qualities of Gora.
Narahari Dasa says: merciful Sri Advaita —
this glory resounds through the three worlds.

4028Srivasa, Murari Gupta and the other devotees
ceaselessly sing of Gaura's deeds.

4029What can I tell? All of them are full of great mercy;
in many ways they work the good of living beings.

4030All that I saw I cannot tell;
when I think of all that, my heart bursts and I die.

4031Saying much in this way, Ishana Mahashaya,
in the rapture of prema, utterly lost his composure.

4032After a while, growing steady, he, together with those three,
lay down to sleep at night in the Lord's courtyard.

4033Much of the night passed — there is no sleep for Srinivasa;
he gazes all around at the Lord's house on every side.

4034I do not know in what wonder he says within himself,
"Why is this house of the Lord built of grass and the like?

4035Why did the Lord, depriving [them] of these pastimes in Nadia,
make [His] associates dwellers in distant lands?

4036These pastimes in Nadia are supremely wonderful,
yet all that company could not see them."

4037As he was saying much in this way, sleep overcame him;
in a dream he sees the splendour and the pastimes in the Lord's house.

4038First he sees the golden town of Nadia;
the ghats of the Suradhuni, paved with jewels, captivate the heart.

4039Then he sees the abode of Gaurachandra:
the abodes of Indra and the other [gods] are not worthy of that splendour.

4040How — and which Vishvakarma — built [these] mansions?
On all sides a golden wall surrounds them.

4041[In them are] separate, separate sections — there is no counting them;
whenever and wherever He wishes, there the Lord sports.

4042In the middle of the inner apartments a flower garden is resplendent;
there stands a wondrous pavilion made of jewels.

4043In the middle of the pavilion is a splendid canopy,
beneath it a beautiful jewelled throne.

4044On the throne Gaurachandra enjoys [His pastimes];
Lakshmi and Vishnupriya shine on the left and the right.637

4045[His] body is adorned with many jewelled ornaments;
the garments He wears are wondrous and captivating.

4046Beholding the splendour that enchants the worlds,
hundreds of thousands of maidservants fan [Him] with chamaras.

4047All of them offer betel, garlands and sandal;
the Lord with His beloveds sports in the company of [their] friends.

4048While he was beholding such play, his sleep broke;
at that very moment sleep again overcame him.

4049In the dream he sees in another section — all of jewels —
the wondrous beauty of a pavilion, an abode of happiness.

4050There is a wondrous throne made of jewels;
upon it the son of Shachi shines.

4051The radiance of [His] body enchants millions and millions of Kandarpas;
the moon of [His] face is lovely, surpassing a host of moons.

4052Nityanandachandra shines, supremely beautiful;
Sri Advaita-deva, Sri Pandita Gadadhara,

4053Vidyanidhi, Gangadasa Pandita, Srivasa,
Sri Chandrashekhara Acharya, Murari, Haridasa,

4054Damodara Pandita, Mukunda, Vakreshvara,
Gauridasa, Suryadasa, Gadadhara Dasa,

4055Sri Mukunda, Narahari, Sri Raghunandana,638
Chiranjiva Sena and Sulochana Sena,

4056Dvija Haridasa, Shuklambara Brahmachari,
Srivasa Pandita, Nandana Acharya, Shridhara,639

4057Vijaya, the jewel Sri Chandrashekhara Acharya,640
Sri Svarupa, Kashishvara, Yadunarayana,

4058Sri Lakshmipati, the master Madhavendra Puri,641
Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, Keshava, Shankara,

4059King Sri Prataparudra, Raya Ramananda,
Trimalla, Venkata Bhatta, Sri Prabodhananda,

4060Sri Gopala Bhatta, and also Sri Raghunatha Bhatta,
Sanatana, Rupa, Jiva the son of Vallabha,642

4061Bhugarbha, Sri Lokanatha, Raghunatha Dasa,
Raghava Pandita, who lives at Govardhana —

4062in the north, the south, the east, the west
the Lord's devotees are countless: who can know [them all]?

4063Surrounded by all the devotees, Gaura-raya enjoys [His pastimes];
seeing that splendour, [Srinivasa] rejoices in his heart.

4064As he, together with the assembly of devotees, was about to bow to the Lord's feet,
his sleep broke; awake, he looks in all directions.

4065He grew distraught — and sleep again overcame him;
in the dream he sees another section, full of splendour.

4066There on a jewelled throne Vishvambhara shines;
on all sides servants are intent on serving [Him].

4067Brahma, Shiva, Indra and the countless gods,
falling at [His] feet, offer praises to the Lord.

4068Seeing the great manifestation of the Lord's majesty,
his whole body thrills with rapture, and great joy fills his heart.

4069Beholding in another section the pastimes of Vaikuntha,
he cannot hold his body still — his heart rejoices.

4070He beholds in another section the pastimes of Ayodhya;
joy arises — how much he says within himself!

4071Beholding in another section the pastimes of Dvaraka,
he loses his composure in bliss and cannot restrain his heart.643

4072In another section he sees the pastimes of Mathura;
merriment arises, and a gentle smile is on his lips.

4073In another section he beholds the pastimes in Vraja:
amid the host of gopis he sees himself.

4074Beholding the beauty of the dance in the Sri rasa-mandala,
he is overwhelmed with great bliss — how many [feelings] rise in his heart!

4075As soon as he saw the pastimes in the nikunja, full of splendour,
his sleep broke; he sees that it is the time of dawn.

4076After a while, growing steady, Acharya Thakura
reflects within himself on the abundant mercy [of the Lord].

4077Whoever hears all these accounts with faith,
his desire Gaurahari fulfils.

4078This circuit of Navadvipa is full of supreme bliss;
the one to whom the Lord is merciful comes to love it.

4079Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the Bhakti-ratnakara.

Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the twelfth wave, called "The Description of the Circuit of Sri Navadvipa and Other Matters".

  13. The Sri Chaitanya-chandramrita is a Sanskrit poem by Prabodhananda Sarasvati.

  26. A verse of Svarupa Damodara, quoted in CC Adi 1. These are the Lord's three desires (173–174): to know the greatness of Radha's love, His own sweetness that she tastes, and the happiness she feels.

  610. The father of Achyuta is Advaita, the father of Achyutananda.

  643. "Loses his composure in bliss" — per the scan of the 1912/13 edition: "আনন্দে অধৈর্য্য না ধরিতে পারে হিয়া" (ānande adhairya; the middle letter of the first word is damaged; OCR: B "আনালা," 1960 edition "সামনে অধ").
